rows.title: India's environmental policy framework - National Environment Policy, EIA, polluter pays and precautionary principles

secs.t: Environmental principles - precautionary, polluter pays, public trust, absolute liability (and the cases)

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2024 and 2025 both asked what the precautionary principle means: "act/stop even without full scientific certainty".
Under the precautionary principle, the burden of proof shifts to the actor undertaking the potentially harmful activity to demonstrate that it is benign.
The 1996 Indian Council case affirmed polluter pays, the 1997 Kamal Nath case recognised the public trust doctrine, and the 1996 Vellore case recognised the precautionary principle.

secs.t: Environmental Acts and bodies - year and purpose

x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 protects wildlife and habitats and regulates hunting.
The Water Act was enacted in 1974, the Forest (Conservation) Act in 1980, the Environment (Protection) Act in 1986 and the National Green Tribunal Act in 2010.
Environmental Impact Assessment is mandatory under the
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986

secs.t: Eco-Mark scheme - launch, what it certifies, products, administering bodies

x: The Eco-Mark scheme was launched in 1991 to label environment-friendly consumer products.
The Eco-Mark logo is
an earthen pot
, used for labelling environment-friendly consumer products.
The
Bureau of Indian Standards
certifies products under the Eco-Mark scheme.
The notified product groups include soaps and detergents, paper, plastics, cosmetics, aerosols and food items.

secs.t: National Environment Policy - year, objectives, principles

x: The National Environment Policy was adopted in 2006 and serves as India’s overarching environment policy.
The NEP 2006 rests on the idea that conservation and livelihood security go together rather than being opposed to each other.
The NEP objectives include conservation of critical resources, inter-generational equity and integration of environment into development plans.

secs.t: National Action Plan on Climate Change - missions

x: The eight missions include Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture and Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change.
The mission specifically concerned with the Himalayan region is the
National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem
The core listing additionally includes
climate change and human health

secs.t: AP environmental institutions - EPTRI, APPCB

x: The APPCB functions under the Water and Air Acts, issues consents and classifies industries, including White and Green categories.
White-category industries are practically non-polluting, while Green-category industries have low pollution potential.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Coastal Regulation Zone provisions fall under the
Environment (Protection) Act
The criticism concerned thin baseline data and the adequacy of the initial environmental information.
The Vanashakti ruling is associated with 31 July 2026.

rows.title: National income concepts - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, factor cost vs market price, GVA, deflator
sub: Group-II M2-A-2: National income of India - concepts: GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, GVA, factor cost and market price

secs.t: Aggregates and conversions - GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP, depreciation, NFIA

x: Exam angle: numerical questions give GDP, NFIA, depreciation and net indirect taxes and ask for NI.
NDP = GDP – depreciation, NNP = GNP – depreciation, and NNP at factor cost is National Income.
Depreciation, or consumption of fixed capital, is deducted because production used only to replace worn-out capital adds nothing new to the productive stock.
GNPMP = 500 – 10 = ₹490 crore; NNPMP = 490 – 50 = ₹440 crore; NNPFC = 440 – 40 =
₹400 crore
NFIA is
factor income received from abroad minus factor income paid abroad
GDP is based on production within domestic territory, whereas GNP includes the income of nationals or normal residents wherever located.

secs.t: Definitions - stem to term

x: GDP
measures the market value of final goods and services produced within a country's geographical boundaries during a year, including production by residents and non-residents.
GDP is the market value of final output, represented as quantity of output (Q) multiplied by its price (P).
Factor income
consists of payments to factors of production: wages, rent, interest and profit.

secs.t: Factor cost vs market price - bridging items, GVA at basic prices

x: GDPFC = GDPMP – indirect taxes + subsidies.
Indirect taxes and subsidies, not direct taxes, form the relevant bridge.
Production taxes are levied irrespective of the quantity of output;
stamp duty
and property tax are examples.
GVA at basic prices continues to be used in the 2022-23 series.
CSO/NSO headline sectoral growth is based on
GVA at basic prices
The difference between GDP and GVA at the relevant price level is attributable to
net product taxes

secs.t: National income - the standard aggregate

x: National Income is NNP at factor cost.
National income is the sum of wages, rent, interest and profits earned by factors belonging to the country, including the adjustment for NFIA.

secs.t: GNP vs GDP - when one exceeds the other

x: Factor income earned by an Indian resident abroad is excluded from India's domestic product but included in its national product.
India's net factor income from abroad is usually negative, making GNP lower than GDP.

secs.t: GDP deflator - ratio, comprehensiveness, purchasing power

x: The 2022–23 series uses
double deflation
, which separately deflates output prices and input prices.
The difference in deflator growth caused manufacturing's nominal share to fall, while its real share remained approximately 17–18%.
When prices rise, a given amount of money purchases fewer goods and services.
A rising GNP or GDP deflator indicates a higher general price level.
Debtors and real-asset holders may gain, while creditors and fixed-income groups may lose.

secs.t: Transfer payments and transfer earnings - in or out

x: Commission on resale is payment for a productive service and is included.
Transfer earnings
are not payments for factor services and are therefore excluded from national income.
Value added at each stage is included, while intermediate goods are excluded separately to avoid double counting.

secs.t: Nominal vs real GDP; personal and disposable income identities

x: The increase in nominal GDP is exactly matched by the increase in the price index from 100 to 120, so output measured at constant prices remains unchanged.
Personal disposable income equals personal income minus
personal direct taxes and non-tax payments such as fines and fees
Personal Income is derived as National Income minus undistributed profits, social security contributions and corporate tax, plus transfer payments and net interest paid by the government.

secs.t: PPP exchange rates - basis, PPP vs market rate

x: PPP prices a common basket using prices prevailing in each country, thereby removing differences in price levels.
PPP estimates are made under the International Comparison Program of the UNSD, with the World Bank as global implementing agency and the NSO as India's nodal agency.
Lower prices in India make its output larger when valued using purchasing power parity than when converted at market exchange rates.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The new GDP series with base year 2022-23 was released by the National Statistical Office on
27 February 2026
The new GDP series introduced
double deflation and Supply-Use Tables
as important methodological features.
GDP measures production within the domestic territory, while GNP is based on the income or production associated with the country’s nationals or residents.
Andhra Pradesh per capita income is computed on the basis of
Net State Domestic Product (NSDP)

rows.title: Methods of measuring national income - product, income and expenditure methods; difficulties
sub: Group-II M2-A-3: Measurement of national income - product, income and expenditure methods; difficulties

secs.t: Methods of measurement - names, and the non-method

x: Exam angle: "Cost and accounting method" is
not
a method of measuring national income.
The production or product method measures national income by summing the value added by each producing unit, which is equal to the value of the final product after avoiding double counting.
The income method is also called the factor income or factor payment method because it aggregates incomes earned by factors of production.
Business investment is the most volatile component
of expenditure, while private consumption is the largest and net exports form the last component in the stated ordering.

secs.t: Inclusion/exclusion test

x: Imputed rent of owner-occupied houses
is included because the housing service has an economic value even when no rent is actually paid.
Transactions in shares and bonds merely transfer ownership of financial assets and do not represent current production.
Changes in inventories are included, while tax revenue as such, interest on public debt and unpaid services of housewives are excluded.

secs.t: Method to sectors - how India applies each

x: The expenditure method is used partly for construction, and expenditure data including PFCE acts as a check on and cross-check of demand-side estimates.
India applies the production method to agriculture, mining and manufacturing, the income method to services, and the expenditure method partly to construction and as a cross-check.

secs.t: State income estimation - AP methods and sectors

x: GST data is now available in addition to the earlier practice of allocating manufacturing GVA according to States' shares in the Annual Survey of Industries.
The guideline seeks to integrate administrative records, sector databases and surveys, while improving coverage of services and the unincorporated segment and consistency with national accounts.
APSES continues to use 2011-12, while the uniform guideline moves States towards 2022-23 and requires consistency with national accounts.

secs.t: Economists' definitions of national income

x: Marshall defined the national dividend in terms of the net aggregate of commodities and services produced by labour and capital acting on natural resources.
Irving
Fisher
's definition is based on the services received by ultimate consumers.
Simon
Kuznets
described national income in terms of the net output flowing to ultimate consumers from the productive system.

secs.t: Circular flow of income - leakages and injections

x: Factor payments constitute the money flow from
firms to households
in return for factor services.
Taxes and imports withdraw income from the domestic circular flow, while government spending and exports inject income into it.
The three leakages are saving, taxes and imports, while the three injections are investment, government spending and exports.

secs.t: Difficulties in measuring national income in India

x: The informal sector is difficult to measure because it often lacks proper accounts; a well-documented and fully accounted sector would not constitute the stated difficulty.

The review referred to all three issues: the absence of seasonally adjusted quarterly data, delays in GFCF data by institutional sector and persistent discrepancies between production and expenditure estimates.

secs.t: Double counting - final vs intermediate goods, value added approach

x: Double counting is avoided either by counting only final goods or by adding the value added at each stage of production.
Gross Value Added includes depreciation, while Net Value Added is calculated as GVA minus depreciation.
Under double deflation, real GVA is real output minus real intermediate consumption, with output and input prices deflated separately.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 2022-23 series uses ASUSE, PLFS, GST, PFMS and e-Vahan data.
The new series improves real GVA estimation through double deflation and volume extrapolation.
The AP GSDP for 2025-26 under the Advance Estimates is projected at
Rs 17.62 lakh crore
at current prices.
The alignment of Supply and Use Tables with national accounts is intended
to reduce discrepancies between production-side and expenditure-side GDP
estimates.

rows.title: India's national accounts - NSO/MoSPI, base year revisions, quarterly estimates, informal sector estimation
sub: Group-II M2-A-4: India's national accounts - NSO, base-year revisions and data issues

secs.t: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

x: Exam angle: CPI's old base is the calendar year 2012, not 2011-12.
Periodic revision makes the estimates more representative of changing production patterns and relative prices.
2022-23 was treated as a relatively normal year; 2017-18 involved the GST transition, 2019-21 was affected by COVID, and 2021-22 carried base effects.

secs.t: Early estimates of national income

x: Exam angle: "first Indian to calculate national income by scientific method" = V.K.R.V. Rao.
Dadabhai Naoroji
made the first recorded attempt in 1868 and estimated per capita income at Rs 20.
The committee was constituted in August 1949, chaired by P.C. Mahalanobis, included Gadgil and Rao, and submitted its first report in 1951.

secs.t: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

x: The National Accounts Division handles GDP, consumption and capital formation; ESD compiles IIP; the Kolkata wing conducts ASI; and NSO compiles the National Industrial Classification.
The NSC is the nodal body for statistical standards, includes the CEO of NITI Aayog ex officio, and has the MoSPI Secretary as its Secretary.
The Industrial Statistics Wing at Kolkata conducts the
Annual Survey of Industries
(ASI).

secs.t: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates

x: Advance estimates use the
benchmark-indicator method
, which projects the relevant aggregates using available indicators.
The Provisional Estimate, earlier released on the last working day of May, was shifted to
7 June
from 2026 after consultation with ACNAS.
The change to 7 June was made after consultation with the Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics, referred to as
ACNAS
The 2023-24 current-price GSDP was ₹14,39,674 crore in the Advance Estimate and
in the First Revised Estimate.

secs.t: GSDP estimation - DES AP, sectors, advance estimates

x: The
Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh
, estimates GSDP for the State.
DES Andhra Pradesh estimates GSDP in nine sectors.
The 2025-26 First Advance Estimate placed Andhra Pradesh GSDP at
Rs 17.62 lakh crore
at current prices.

secs.t: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism

x: The MCA-21 company database represented an
enterprise approach
and partly replaced the earlier reliance on ASI for the relevant estimation.
The series was criticised for unusually high manufacturing growth that was inconsistent with physical indicators and for overestimating the private corporate sector.
All four sectoral revisions are correctly stated: agriculture and finance-related activities were revised upward, while trade and road transport were revised downward.
The MCA database listed 1,35,802 manufacturing companies in 2011-12, compared with 67,649 corporate factories in ASI.
HCES 2022-23 was the first full Household Consumption Expenditure Survey since 2011-12; the 2017-18 results were withheld.

secs.t: Quarterly GDP estimates - lag and data sources

x: Quarterly GDP estimates are released about two months after the relevant quarter ends, although older material had indicated about one month.
Quarterly estimates use high-frequency indicators, and GST data has further improved the information base.
The IMF flagged the
absence of a seasonally adjusted series and a lag in disaggregating capital formation

secs.t: Informal sector estimation - methods and data

x: The household or unincorporated sector is benchmarked on ASUSE and subsequently extrapolated with suitable indicators.
PLFS
measures employment, unemployment, LFPR and WPR through monthly, quarterly and annual estimates.
HCES covers household consumption, ASI covers registered factories, ASUSE covers unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises and TUS covers time use.
ASUSE is designed to cover
unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises
, which form an important part of the informal sector.

secs.t: Savings and capital formation estimates - agency and sector shares

x: MoSPI/NSO prepares estimates of consumption, capital formation and saving with institutional-sector detail.
The sectors identified for these estimates are
household, private corporate and public sectors
The private corporate share of GFCF was 33 per cent, described as a decadal low.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Current criticism and debate concern the coverage of the informal sector and the use of MCA-based manufacturing GVA.
The NSO follows IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard norms and acts as India's nodal agency for the International Comparison Programme.
DES-AP moved towards the
base under the MoSPI GSVA guideline.
India was the third-largest economy by purchasing power parity according to the ICP 2021 measure.

rows.title: Trends in India's national income, per capita income and sectoral shares; inter-state GSDP comparison
sub: Group-II M2-A-18: Current state of the Indian economy - growth trends, key challenges and outlook

secs.t: Sectoral share of GVA - at Independence vs now

x: All three statements are correct: agriculture's share was about 17 percent by 2017-18, services exceeded 50 percent, and the order was services greater than industry greater than agriculture.
The estimated sector growth rates for FY 2025-26 were agriculture 3.1 percent, industry 6.2 percent, manufacturing 7.0 percent and services 9.1 percent.

x: Poverty convergence has been observed, with Bihar and Uttar Pradesh reducing poverty fastest.
The MPI range is from 0.002 in Kerala to 0.16 in Bihar, indicating substantial inter-State disparity in multidimensional poverty.
The district MPI headcount ranges from 2.42% in West Godavari to 12.84% in Kurnool.
Rayalaseema and North Coastal districts lag in the context of intra-State disparities.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The debate asks inequality of what—income, wealth or consumption—and along which axis, including caste, class and gender.
A reduction in poverty can coexist with rising inequality when gains are distributed unevenly across population groups.
Consumption data may understate the incomes of the top end, thereby affecting the assessment of inequality.

rows.title: Unemployment - types (structural, frictional, cyclical, disguised, seasonal, educated)

secs.t: Unemployment type → sector/area where predominant

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2025 asked "predominant in agriculture" twice - answer was
Disguised
in GS and
Seasonal
in G2 (when disguised was not an option). Read the options.

Seasonal unemployment is associated with agriculture, tourism and agro-industries; technological unemployment with manufacturing and routine services; cyclical unemployment with recession-hit industry and services; and structural unemployment with the whole economy over the long run.

secs.t: Disguised unemployment - definition and identification

x: Disguised unemployment is identified when removing some workers does not reduce total output, implying zero marginal productivity of those workers.
Disguised unemployment is hidden unemployment, is common on family farms, and involves zero or negative marginal productivity for surplus workers.
Persons in disguised unemployment appear employed, so this hidden form is not captured by headline unemployment rates in the same way as open unemployment.

secs.t: Cyclical unemployment - cause and business-cycle phase

x: Exam angle: "unemployment caused by depression in an economy" =
Cyclical
Cyclical unemployment is linked to the
contraction or trough
phase and begins to decline when recovery or boom starts.
Keynes explained unemployment in developed economies mainly through
deficiency in effective demand
, which is associated with demand-deficient or cyclical unemployment.

secs.t: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes

x: Exam angle: odd-one-out questions list causes (population growth, slow industrialisation, faulty education) and slip in a non-cause such as "high growth of labour-intensive manufacturing".
Rapid population growth, labour immobility and the shift towards capital-intensive production contribute to a long-run shortfall of labour demand relative to supply.
India has substantial seasonal, disguised and underemployment, while its basic unemployment problem is structural rather than solely Keynesian demand deficiency.

secs.t: Educated unemployment and underemployment

x: Educated unemployment is an urban phenomenon in which qualified persons fail to find employment matching their education and the needs of industry.
Invisible underemployment
exists when a person works full-time but earns very little or works below their ability, as in the example of an MBA working as a driver.

secs.t: Frictional vs structural unemployment

x: Frictional unemployment results from the temporary time lag involved in changing or searching for jobs, while structural unemployment is long-term and arises from a mismatch between skills and available jobs.
The temporary gap caused by quitting one job and searching for another is frictional or search unemployment.
A shift from labour-intensive to capital-intensive production changes the demand for labour and creates a long-term structural mismatch.

secs.t: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

x: In hidden or disguised unemployment, persons appear to be employed, but their removal does not reduce output because they contribute nothing or very little to production.
Full employment means that everyone willing to work at the prevailing wage finds work, but frictional and structural unemployment may still exist.
The natural rate is the combination of
frictional and structural unemployment
existing at full employment.

secs.t: Technological unemployment - automation and AI

x: Automation in manufacturing and AI in services can reduce demand for low-skilled and routine jobs, and the resulting technological unemployment is structural in character.
Growth led by capital-intensive sectors such as IT and finance, instead of labour-intensive manufacturing, can produce jobless growth.
Jobless growth denotes capital-intensive growth that does not generate employment in proportion to the increase in output.

secs.t: Okun's law and Phillips curve

x: Stagflation combines high inflation with high unemployment and therefore breaks down the traditional Phillips-curve trade-off.
Okun's law states that a one percentage point increase in unemployment above the natural rate is associated with roughly a 2% reduction in output below potential GDP.
The inverse relationship between unemployment and the gap between actual and potential output is known as Okun's law, associated with
Arthur Okun

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh recorded 4.1% unemployment compared with 3.2% for India, making the AP rate
higher by 0.9 percentage points
A falling unemployment rate may reflect people entering low-productivity work under distress rather than the creation of good or adequate jobs.
India's unemployment is characterised as structural and disguised, while developed countries are described as facing mainly cyclical or demand-deficient unemployment.

rows.title: Measurement of unemployment - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS; PLFS methodology and recent findings

secs.t: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS

x: Exam angle: odd-one-out lists slip in a non-method such as "Current Monthly Status" or "Rangarajan formula" among UPS/CWS/CDS.
CDS records unemployment separately for each day and therefore captures intermittent unemployment that may not be reflected when a person is counted as employed under CWS.
All four statements correctly describe the reference periods and employment criteria of usual status, UPSS, CWS and CDS.

secs.t: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds

x: For 2011–12, the NSS 68th Round reported unemployment rates of 2.7% under UPS, 3.7% under CWS and 5.6% under CDS.
The
NSS 68th Round
for 2011–12 was the last quinquennial employment-unemployment round before the PLFS system became the regular source of such estimates.
CMIE reported approximately
53 million
unemployed persons as of December 2021.

secs.t: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency

x: The Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics was set up on the advice of the
National Statistical Commission
and designed the PLFS framework.
The original PLFS design provided annual rural and urban estimates under UPSS and CWS, along with quarterly CWS estimates for urban areas.
The revised PLFS sample was raised to approximately
2,72,304 households
, described as about 2.65 times the earlier size.

secs.t: Key labour indicators - LFPR, WPR, UR

x: Exam angle: "percentage of employed persons in the population" =
Worker Population Ratio
Persons who are not seeking work and are not available for work, such as some students and homemakers, are outside the labour force.
UR is unemployed persons as a percentage of the labour force, whereas PU is unemployed persons as a percentage of the total population.

secs.t: Agencies and sources of unemployment data

x: The NSSO, now within the NSO, conducted the quinquennial employment-unemployment rounds and became the institutional source for PLFS from 2017.
The
Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
conducts the Employment–Unemployment Survey and the Quarterly Employment Survey of establishments.
CMIE conducts the CPHS, Employment Exchanges provide registration data, Census supplies decennial worker data, and CSO and NSSO were merged into NSO in 2019.

secs.t: AP unemployment rate in PLFS

x: Andhra Pradesh recorded an overall unemployment rate of
under UPSS in PLFS 2023–24, compared with 3.2% for India.
Andhra Pradesh recorded an LFPR of 47.5% and a WPR of 45.6%.
The female LFPR was 35.8% in Andhra Pradesh and 31.7% in India.
The cited figures show that 62.3% of rural jobs and about 55% of jobs overall were informal.

secs.t: Committees on employment statistics

x: The Expert Committee on Unemployment Estimates, popularly known as the Dantwala Committee, was constituted in 1970.
The Dantwala Committee rejected a single-number estimate and recommended separate estimates by usual, weekly and daily status, as well as by category.
The
Bhagwati Committee
, constituted in 1973, reviewed unemployment estimates and employment-oriented policies.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India shifted to monthly unemployment data based on the CWS approach from 2025.
Under the CWS approach, working for even
one hour during the reference week
is sufficient for classification as employed.
The higher unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh was attributed to
urban and youth unemployment
CMIE data are monthly and based on a larger sample, but CMIE and PLFS use different methodologies.

rows.title: Labour force participation, female LFPR, informality and the quality of employment

secs.t: Jobless growth and employment elasticity

x: The term ‘jobless growth’ was coined by
Nick Perna
in the early 1990s.
Employment elasticity equals the percentage change in employment divided by the percentage change in output or GDP.
A low or near-zero employment elasticity means that output growth is generating little additional employment and may signal jobless growth.

secs.t: Quality of employment - status shares and social security

x: The India Employment Report 2024 was associated with the International Labour Organization and the Institute for Human Development, abbreviated as
ILO-IHD
Regular wage or salaried workers constituted
of urban jobs in Q2 FY26.
The report noted that informal and vulnerable employment exists even among
educated youth
Only 14.2% of Gen Z had a formal job contract, while 20.1% had some social security.

secs.t: Sector-wise job growth

x: The listed QES sectors include manufacturing, construction, trade, transport, accommodation and restaurants, IT/BPO, education, health and financial services;
mining and quarrying
is not listed.
Agriculture’s workforce share declined from
The services sector's employment share rose from 22.82% in 1993-94 to

secs.t: Female LFPR - trend, rural vs urban, feminisation of agriculture

x: Subsistence farming, unpaid family work and distress employment were all identified as drivers of the rise in rural female workers.
The U-shaped hypothesis proposes that Female LFPR initially falls with income growth and rises later as education and service-sector opportunities expand.
Social norms, unpaid care work and unsafe transport are barriers;
expansion of service-sector opportunities
is associated with increased participation at a later stage.

secs.t: Gig and platform economy

x: The NITI Aayog projection was
2.35 crore
gig workers by 2029-30, equivalent to about 6.7% of the workforce.
Aggregators contribute
of annual turnover to a fund intended to support life and health insurance and pensions for gig workers.
The Periodic Labour Force Survey does not yet identify gig workers as a distinct category, and most gig workers remain outside e-Shram registration.

secs.t: AP female LFPR and informal workforce

x: For the 15-years-and-above population, female LFPR was 44.8% in Andhra Pradesh and 41.7% in India.
The overall LFPR in Andhra Pradesh was 47.5%, comprising 50.1% in rural areas and 41.3% in urban areas.
The rural share was 62.3% and the urban share was 45.6%; the difference was
16.7 percentage points

secs.t: Universal angles

x: PLFS 2025 reported an approximate LFPR of 59%, WPR of 57% and unemployment rate of 3%.
Direct factory employment declined from 61% to 47% between 2011 and 2023, while the share of contract workers increased to 42%.
Higher education and the lack of flexible working timings are identified as factors keeping urban young women out of the labour force in Andhra Pradesh.

rows.title: Employment generation schemes - MGNREGA, PMEGP, DDU-GKY, PM-SVANidhi, Atmanirbhar packages

secs.t: MGNREGA - Act, launch, phases, renaming, entitlement, wages

x: The programme initially covered 200 districts; 625 refers to later all-district coverage, not the initial launch.
The
Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025
, replaced MGNREGA and came into force on 1 July 2026.
Under VB-G RAM G, job cards become Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards.
MGNREGA wages are to be paid within
15 days
of the work done.
The World Bank's World Development Report 2014 called MGNREGA a “
stellar example of rural development

secs.t: MGNREGA objective and target group

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2017 - mandate = "100 days to every
household
whose adult members volunteer", not "100 days to every adult".
MGNREGA is anchored in
Article 41
, which relates to the right to work, education and public assistance in certain cases.
MGNREGA targets rural households volunteering for unskilled manual work, not urban skilled workers.

secs.t: MGNREGA features and monitoring

x: At least
one-third
of MGNREGA beneficiaries must be women, although their actual share has consistently exceeded 50 per cent of person-days.
Bhuvan, developed by ISRO, supports GeoMGNREGA geo-tagging, while NREGASoft is the programme's Management Information System.
MGNREGA converges with PMAY-G by providing 90 or 95 person-days to eligible beneficiaries through the AwaasSoft–NREGASoft link.

secs.t: Wage employment vs self-employment programmes

x: NREP and MGNREGS are wage-employment programmes, while IRDP is a self-employment programme.
The Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana, or PMRY, was intended for
educated unemployed youth
and was a self-employment programme.

secs.t: Food for Work programmes

x: The Food for Work Programme was started in 1977 by the Janata government.
NFFWP was launched on 14 November 2004 in
the 150 most backward districts
NFFWP and SGRY were subsumed into NREGA in the districts covered by NREGA from 2006.

secs.t: Scheme → ministry + target group

x: All three statements correctly describe PMEGP: its target is new non-farm micro-enterprises, its margin money ranges from 15% to 35%, and its project caps are ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for services.
PMEGP dates to 2008, DDU-GKY to 2014, National Career Service to 2015, and Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan to 2020.

secs.t: AP MGNREGA performance

x: Andhra Pradesh ranked
fourth
nationally under MGNREGS.
Andhra Pradesh pooled rural development funds to provide
125 days
in distressed rural pockets under the new Mission.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements are correct: the Supreme Court discussion concerned the relationship between the right to work and Article 21, Olga Tellis linked livelihood to Article 21, and MGNREGA is described as the only law based on the right to work.
MGNREGA is significant as a safety net during agrarian distress and emergencies such as the COVID-19 crisis, in addition to being associated with the right to work.

rows.title: Poverty eradication and livelihood programmes - DAY-NRLM, DAY-NULM, SHG movement

secs.t: Scheme renaming/restructuring chain

x: The six earlier programmes were merged into
Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana
(SGSY), launched on 1 April 1999.
SGSY was restructured as NRLM, branded as Aajeevika, in 2010 and launched in 2011; it was subsequently renamed DAY-NRLM in 2016.
SGSY
was launched on 1 April 1999 to bring assisted poor families above the poverty line through SHG-based group financing.

secs.t: IRDP and its sub-schemes

x: Exam angle: IRDP "envisages assistance to poor rural families to come above the poverty line".
IRDP combined subsidy and bank credit, aimed at taking poor rural families above the poverty line, and covered all blocks from 2 October 1980.
TRYSEM began in 1979, DWCRA in 1982, SITRA in 1992 and Ganga Kalyan Yojana in 1997.

secs.t: AP SHG movement

x: DWCRA began in 1982-83, SERP and Velugu began in 2000, Indira Kranthi Patham began in 2004-05, and MEPMA began in 2007.
Indira Kranthi Patham was formed in 2004-05 by merging
Velugu and DWCRA
and was implemented by SERP.
Velugu was a World Bank-aided District Poverty Initiatives Project begun in 2000; it later became Indira Kranthi Patham and was run by SERP.
The Vaddi Leni Runalu or Sunna Vaddi arrangement provides interest subvention when SHG loans are repaid promptly.

secs.t: DAY-NRLM

x: DAY-NRLM follows a three-tier institutional structure: Self-Help Group, Village Organisation and Cluster-Level Federation.
DAY-NRLM covers approximately 10 crore households through 91 lakh SHGs, 5.35 lakh Village Organisations and 33,558 Cluster-Level Federations.
BC Sakhis, the SARATHI app and Samaveshi Aajeevika Yojana are listed among
DAY-NRLM
initiatives; the last follows a graduation approach.

secs.t: DAY-NULM

x: Support to Urban Street Vendors
(SUSV) is a DAY-NULM component.
PAISA means
Portal for Affordable Credit and Interest Subvention Access
MEPMA
, the Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas, is the implementing agency for DAY-NULM in Andhra Pradesh.
The Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas (MEPMA) was established on
1 September 2007

secs.t: Direct attack on poverty programmes

x: Exam angle: odd-one-out puts a non-poverty programme (e.g. a crop insurance or a statistics body) beside IRDP/NREP/RLEGP/JRY.
Target-group programmes under the direct-attack strategy replaced reliance on the trickle-down approach associated with the Fifth and Sixth Plans.
NREP, RLEGP and JRY are direct-attack poverty programmes, whereas
a crop insurance programme
belongs to a different policy category.

secs.t: Women-focused livelihood schemes and SHG pioneer

x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh was established in 1993 to provide micro-credit to poor women working in the unorganised sector.
The Grameen Bank model of Bangladesh, associated with Muhammad Yunus, provided collateral-free loans particularly to poor women.
The concept of SHGs is dated to 1975 by CDI, while the Grameen project began in 1976.
SHGs became a formal poverty alleviation tool during the Seventh Five-Year Plan, covering 1985–90.

secs.t: Early anti-poverty initiatives

x: The Community Development Programme began in 1952, the Twenty Point Programme was launched in 1975, Antyodaya began in 1977, and RUDSETI was established in 1982.
RUDSETI was established at Ujire in Karnataka in 1982 and trains rural youth for self-employment.
The Community Development Programme was launched on
2 October 1952
and is described as the mother of social development programmes.

secs.t: SHG-Bank Linkage Programme

x: NABARD launched the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme as a pilot in 1992.
NABARD refinances banks and trains and promotes SHGs; it does not replace all commercial banks as direct lenders to SHGs.
SHGs can borrow collateral-free and generally obtain loans at lower interest rates under the linkage programme.
Andhra Pradesh
is reported as first in the country in SHG-bank linkage under APSES 2024–25.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Ethiopia, Tanzania, Malawi, Kenya and Rwanda
are reported to be studying the NRLM SHG model.
The multidimensional poverty ratio declined from 29.17 per cent in 2013–14 to
11.28 per cent
Uneven SHG quality, weak market links, debt stress due to poor financial literacy and political interference are identified challenges.

rows.title: Social security and DBT - PM-JDY, JAM trinity, Aadhaar-enabled transfers, pension schemes

secs.t: Pension schemes → eligibility, entry age, contribution

x: For eligible persons joining before 31 December 2015, the Government contributed
50% of the subscriber's contribution or ₹1,000 per year, whichever was lower, for five years
NPS is a defined-contribution, market-linked system open to Government, private and unorganised-sector participants; minors can participate through NPS Vatsalya.
The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (
PFRDA
) regulates NPS and administers APY under the NPS architecture.

secs.t: Insurance schemes → premium, cover, age band, enrolments

x: Exam angle: PMJJBY is "life insurance" and PMSBY is "accidental" (G2-GS 2024).
A dedicated Health Insurance Scheme for handloom weavers was introduced in 2005–06, while life cover was provided under the Converged Mahatma Gandhi Bunkar Bima Yojana.
Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana is an LIC-run life and disability insurance scheme for rural landless households aged 18–59 years.
Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana targeted
rural landless households
and provided life and disability cover through LIC.

secs.t: DBT - launch, coverage, PAHAL and Ujjwala

x: After its pilot, DBT was scaled up in 2015 using
the JAM trinity
of Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and Mobile.
The Aadhaar Payment Bridge System routes Aadhaar-linked payments, whereas the Aadhaar-enabled Payment System facilitates cash withdrawal at micro-ATMs.
Ujjwala provides free LPG connections to women belonging to BPL households, with the objective of reducing indoor air pollution.

secs.t: JAM trinity and India Stack

x: Exam angle: APPSC G1 2024 A-R: "India Stack enabled online, paperless, cashless access" was
true
, but the stated Reason was
false
The presence-less layer uses Aadhaar authentication/e-KYC; the paperless layer uses DigiLocker/eSign; the cashless layer uses UPI, AePS and IMPS; and the consent layer uses Account Aggregators.
Under JAM, Jan Dhan is the account where funds land, Aadhaar is used for biometric checking, and mobile phones provide transaction alerts.

secs.t: Aadhaar-enabled services and the Puttaswamy judgement

x: Jeevan Pramaan was launched in 2014 and enables pensioners to create a digital life certificate using Aadhaar biometrics.
Section 7 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 permits Aadhaar to be required for subsidies charged to the Consolidated Fund.
The 2017 nine-judge Bench recognised privacy under Article 21; the 2018 five-judge Bench upheld Aadhaar for welfare under Section 7 and struck down private use under Section 57.

secs.t: PM Jan Dhan Yojana

x: Phase II included the overdraft facility, a Credit Guarantee Fund for overdraft defaults and unorganised-sector pensions under Swavalamban.
PMJDY became the Jan Dhan layer of JAM, supported DBT, and shifted its coverage focus after August 2018.
The accident insurance cover attached to the RuPay debit card was raised from ₹1 lakh to
₹2 lakh

secs.t: National Social Assistance Programme

x: NSAP was launched to give effect to
Article 41
, which relates to public assistance in cases including old age, sickness and disablement.
NSAP is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for BPL households, fulfils Article 41 and has been a Core of Core scheme since 2016.
The Annapurna scheme provides
10 kg
of foodgrains per month to eligible needy elderly persons.

secs.t: Social security laws

x: The Unorganised Workers’ Social Security Act was enacted in 2008 and has subsequently been subsumed in the Code on Social Security, 2020.
The EPF and MP Act, 1952 applies to establishments with
20 or more employees
ESI covered
695 districts, 4.09 crore employees and 15.87 crore people
as on 31 March 2025.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Kerala’s decision to end doorstep pension delivery for DBT led to protests, highlighting the tension between digital transfers and doorstep delivery for the elderly.

All three statements are correct: PMAY-G completed ten years in 2026, allocations for SBM-U and PMAY-U were cut in Budget 2026–27, and 24.8 crore people reportedly escaped multidimensional poverty over a decade.

rows.title: Food security - NFSA 2013, PDS reform, buffer stocks, One Nation One Ration Card, PMGKAY
sub: Group-II M2-A-52: Food security and buffer stock policy; National Food Security Act 2013

secs.t: NFSA 2013 - coverage, entitlements, maternity benefit, State Food Commission, grievance redress

x: Exam angle: "what % of rural population" - answer
; urban
The NFSA provides
a legal and justiciable right to subsidised foodgrains
and food and nutritional security.
The NFSA provides an internal mechanism and District Grievance Redressal Officers, while State Food Commissions monitor implementation and hear appeals.
The stated aim is to remove the inequity under which smaller AAY households receive a greater quantity per person when the entitlement is fixed per household.
AAY, introduced in December 2000 for the poorest of the poor, provided 35 kg per family at ₹3 per kg for rice, ₹2 for wheat and ₹1 for coarse grains.

secs.t: Food security concept - definition, dimensions, national vs household

x: The World Food Summit definition emphasizes physical and economic access to
sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life
Both statements are true, and unequal distribution explains why aggregate surplus does not automatically ensure household food security.
FCI procures wheat and rice at the pre-announced MSP advised by CACP, and the stocks are released at lower issue prices in deficit areas or during calamities.
Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) sales are used to release food grains and help cool prices.

secs.t: Food-based safety net programmes - PDS, ICDS, Mid-Day Meal / PM POSHAN

x: PDS provides grain through Fair Price Shops; ICDS gives supplementary nutrition at anganwadis; PM POSHAN gives hot cooked meals; Food-for-Work gives grain as wages.
PM POSHAN provides hot cooked meals to Bal Vatika or pre-school children and students at the primary and upper primary levels.
NFSA provides pregnant women and lactating mothers a free meal along with a maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000.

secs.t: Entitlement approach - proponent

x: Amartya Sen
developed the entitlement approach, especially in his work Poverty and Famines (1981).
Sen argued that famine results from a collapse of people's entitlements or command over food, not merely from a decline in overall food availability.

secs.t: PMGKAY - launch, extensions, merger with NFSA

x: PMGKAY initially provided 5 kg of free food grains per person in addition to the existing NFSA entitlement.
From 1 January 2023, the entire NFSA allocation became free under the merged arrangement described as ‘One Nation–One Price–One Ration’.
The cost of the five-year extension is approximately
₹11.80 lakh crore
, borne by the Union Government.

secs.t: AP ration distribution - doorstep vehicles (MDU), rice card

x: PHH entitlement is 5 kg per unit, AAY entitlement is 35 kg per card, and wheat is supplied at 1 kg per card at Rs 16 per kg.
Mee Mart was presented as a PDS-modernisation initiative linked with NCCF; 1,000 outlets were planned, 553 were ready, and the pricing and Digital Rupee link were specified as stated.

secs.t: Food and nutrition security laws and bodies - matching purpose

x: NFSA provides the legal right to subsidised grain; the Essential Commodities Act regulates essential goods; the Food Corporations Act created FCI; and Article 47 concerns nutrition and living standards.
The Essential Commodities Act enables control over the production, supply, prices and stocks of essential goods and supports PDS control orders.
The TPDS (Control) Order, 2015 provides operational rules for ration cards and Fair Price Shops under the NFSA framework.

secs.t: NFSA grievance machinery - State Food Commission, DGRO, vigilance committees

x: Each State has a State Food Commission, an existing body may be designated to avoid new costs, and non-compliance with DGRO recommendations can attract penalties.
NFSA vigilance committees function at the
State, district, block and Fair Price Shop levels
Social audits, mandatory disclosure of PDS records and vigilance committees are all accountability mechanisms under the NFSA framework.

secs.t: Buffer stock norms - quarterly norms, strategic reserve, OMSS

x: Buffer stocks were formally introduced during the
Fourth Five-Year Plan
, covering 1969–74.
All three statements are correct: excess stocks were about 602 LMT, approximately three times the norm, and the central pool stock on 1 September 2025 was 702.03 LMT.
The central pool stock was 702.03 LMT, comprising
369.06 LMT of rice and 332.97 LMT of wheat

secs.t: Global Hunger Index and SOFI - India's rank, indicators

x: The GHI uses undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality;
maternal mortality
is not one of its four indicators.
The objections relate to the child focus of three indicators and the small opinion-poll-type sample used for the undernourishment figure.
Both statements are true, and the predominance of child-related indicators is a basis for criticism of the index's composition.

secs.t: Price interventions - Bharat Rice, Bharat Atta via NAFED, NCCF, Kendriya Bhandar

x: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold at subsidised retail prices through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets, as well as mobile vans.
NCCF was established in 1965.
NCCF functions under the
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
NCCF procures essential goods and undertakes price-stabilisation operations.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh is exploring a wider PDS basket including pulses, oil and fortified foods, along with convergence with Anganwadi and the Mid-Day Meal programme.
Climate-related food-security concerns now include an affordable, nutritious supply for about 1.4 billion people, rather than only the availability of sufficient grain.
The debate supports adding eggs, milk and dietary diversity while retaining cereal support rather than cutting it.

rows.title: Rural development - issues, programmes, rural infrastructure (PMGSY, PMAY-G, Jal Jeevan Mission)

secs.t: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

x: Srijan Pal Singh
co-authored *Target 3 Billion* with Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, in which the PURA concept was elaborated.
The mission envisages more than 300 Rurban clusters, combines the rural soul with urban amenities, and seeks to reduce distress migration.
Rurban clusters are rural areas showing urban signs, including rising population density, non-farm employment and growing economic activity.

secs.t: Rural development institutions and missions → objective

x: Mission Antyodaya
includes an annual Gram Panchayat-level ranking survey and functions as a convergence framework for rural development.
ITDA and TADP seek to improve agricultural output through modern inputs, horticulture and fruit plantations and to strengthen tribal livelihoods.
Drinking Water and Sanitation
became a separate Ministry in 2011 and has been a Department under the Ministry of Jal Shakti since June 2019.

secs.t: Evolution of rural development programmes - chronology

x: The correct sequence is Community Development Programme (1952), Food for Work (1977–78), SGSY (1999), and Bharat Nirman (2005).
The
National Extension Service
was launched in 1953, after the Community Development Programme of 1952.
The Balwantrai Mehta Committee reviewed the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service and submitted its report in
November 1957

secs.t: Scheme → launch, ministry, target

x: The Jal Jeevan Mission seeks to provide
tap water to every rural household
SBM-Gramin Phase II focuses on sustaining ODF status and managing solid and liquid waste, together described as ODF Plus.
The Vibrant Villages Programme was announced in Budget 2022–23 under the
Ministry of Home Affairs
and targets villages on the northern border.

secs.t: PMGSY - objective, connectivity norms, phases

x: PMGSY generally covers habitations with 500 or more population in plains and 250 or more in hill States, the North-East, deserts and Schedule V or tribal areas.
PMGSY-I began in 2000, PMGSY-II in 2013 focused on upgradation, and PMGSY-III began in 2019 for through routes and major rural links.
PMGSY has connected
of the targeted eligible areas according to the stated assessment.

secs.t: PMAY-G - unit assistance, beneficiary selection, target

x: PMAY-G provides assistance of Rs 1.20 lakh per house in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly or difficult terrain.
PMAY-G beneficiaries are identified using housing-deprivation data from SECC 2011, followed by verification by the Gram Sabha.
The stated progress figure is
3.13 crore
rural houses completed by mid-2026.

secs.t: Jal Jeevan Mission - FHTC target, service level, Har Ghar Jal

x: FHTC stands for
Functional Household Tap Connection
, which is intended to provide tap water to every rural household.
Har Ghar Jal certification requires tap connections for every household and institution, certified through a Gram Sabha resolution.
The Union Budget 2026–27 provided
Rs 67,600 crore
for the Jal Jeevan Mission; the corresponding figure for 2025–26 was Rs 67,000 crore.

secs.t: Rural development issues - infrastructure deficit, income gap, rurbanisation

x: Poor-quality works, irregularities, cost overruns and operation and maintenance concerns have been reported in relation to JJM implementation.
Rurbanisation is intended to bridge the rural-urban divide and reduce distress migration by bringing urban amenities and opportunities to rural areas.
MGNREGA provides up to 100 days of wage employment per household, with one-third participation intended for women, while NRLM promotes SHG-based self-employment and livelihoods.

secs.t: AP rural programmes - housing, village secretariats, JJM coverage

x: All three figures are reported for Andhra Pradesh’s JJM implementation: 112 water testing laboratories, 2,00,101 hand pumps and 70.04 lakh FHTC households.
The allocations were Rs 5,451 crore for urban and rural housing, Rs 955 crore for NRLM, Rs 1,037 crore for SBM and Rs 8,365 crore for VB-G RAM G.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh’s reported coverage was below the national level, while its State target is universal safe-water provision by 2028.
JJM 2.0 shifts emphasis from merely creating infrastructure to ensuring service delivery, including sustainable operation and maintenance.
The sequence is the original JJM deadline of 2024, launch of village and ward secretariats in 2019, the September 2025 O&M policy, and the extension to December 2028.

rows.title: Rural credit and rural non-farm sector; migration and rural distress

secs.t: Feminisation of agriculture - meaning and causes

x: Feminisation of agriculture means an increasing proportion of women among cultivators, agricultural labourers and unpaid family workers, particularly as men shift to non-farm and urban work.
Women’s work participation was high in agriculture in the 1980s, fell with mechanisation between 2004-05 and 2012, and rose again after 2020, partly due to distress.

secs.t: Rural-urban migration - push and pull factors, distress and seasonal migration

x: Crop failure, poor rural healthcare and similar rural disadvantages are push factors, while better wages and urban industry and services are pull factors.
All four statements correspond to the demographic and rural service figures cited: about 65% rural population, 26% aged 10-24, 35% lacking nearby quality healthcare and secondary dropout above 17%.

secs.t: Rural distress indicators - income gap, wages, consumption, MGNREGA demand, debt

x: All three are cited as signs of strengthening rural fundamentals: lower rural unemployment, higher consumption and rising real wages.
MGNREGA person-days fell from 389.09 crore in 2020-21 to
183.77 crore
in 2025-26 up to December 2025.
MGNREGA was stated to have been replaced by
VB-G RAM G
, expanded as Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin).

secs.t: Rural credit sources - institutional vs non-institutional

x: Tenants, sharecroppers, SHGs and JLGs are eligible under the described Kisan Credit Card framework.
The Kisan Credit Card limit is determined with reference to the
cropping pattern
, while the card covers crop, post-harvest, consumption and allied needs.
Cooperatives
provide institutional credit as well as marketing and storage support to small and marginal farmers.

secs.t: Moneylenders and informal debt - trend, interest, microfinance

x: A
debt trap
occurs when a new loan is taken to repay an old loan, causing continuing indebtedness.
The cited NSSO 77th Round figure places indebted agricultural households in Andhra Pradesh at
, the highest among major States.
The described microfinance route uses self-help groups, joint liability groups and BC Sakhis under DAY-NRLM.

secs.t: Rural non-farm sector - share, components

x: Rural industries, handloom and handicrafts, and food processing are components of the rural non-farm sector.
MSMEs account for about 31.1 per cent of GDP, provide 38.9 crore jobs, rank second to agriculture in employment generation and help reduce distress migration.
The parliamentary panel flagged
low wages and drop-outs
in relation to DDU-GKY.

secs.t: All India Rural Credit Survey Committee / NAFIS - findings

x: A.
D. Gorwala
chaired the All India Rural Credit Survey Committee.
The Committee famously concluded that rural credit had failed, but cooperation must succeed.
The State Bank of India was formed in 1955 from the
Imperial Bank
NAFIS stands for
NABARD All India Rural Financial Inclusion Survey
The first round of NAFIS was conducted in

secs.t: AP migration - distress belts and Gulf source districts

x: Rayalaseema, which is drought-prone, and north Andhra, particularly Srikakulam, are identified as the main distress-migration belts.
Gulf migration comes mainly from
YSR Kadapa and the Godavari/Konaseema districts
The AP response provided
125 days
of wage work in distressed pockets under VB-G RAM G. The other figures are not the stated duration.
The AP response covered 359 panchayats in Rurban clusters to curb migration.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The July 2026 PLFS reference highlighted a widening rural-urban gap in female labour force participation rate (FLFPR).
The stated debates concern whether rising rural female work indicates empowerment or distress, and whether falling MGNREGA demand is real or suppressed by budget constraints.
The identified migration belts, high tenancy and the 93.2 per cent indebtedness figure together describe important dimensions of rural distress in Andhra Pradesh.

rows.title: Urban development - urbanisation trends, challenges (housing, slums, transport, waste, finance)

secs.t: Urbanisation trends - Census 2011 share, most/least urbanised States, fastest growth, AP

x: All three statements are correct: cities occupy about 3% of land, generate around 60% of GDP, and the urban population is projected to reach about 60 crore by 2031.
Andhra Pradesh
, in the undivided-State comparison, had the lowest urbanisation level at about 33%, compared with Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
DEGURBA-based estimates cited by the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister put India at about
urban, much higher than the Census figure.

secs.t: Global urbanisation projections - UN World Urbanization Prospects

x: More than half of the world’s population is already living in urban areas.
India’s cities are projected to host nearly one billion people by 2050; the cited approximation is about
900 million

secs.t: Urban settlement classification - census vs statutory towns, size classes, million-plus

x: A statutory town is notified under State law and has an urban local body such as a corporation, municipality, nagar panchayat or cantonment board.

A Census town remains administratively a village but satisfies all three specified demographic and occupational conditions, including the separate requirement that 75% of male workers be non-agricultural.
A census town has a population exceeding 5,000, at least 75% of male workers engaged in non-agricultural work and a density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre.

secs.t: Urban challenges - housing, slums, transport, waste, water

x: Greater Visakhapatnam
had the highest cited slum share among million-plus cities, at approximately 44%, compared with about 41% in Greater Mumbai and Vijayawada.

About two-thirds of urban dwellers may face pluvial flooding by 2030, and the urban heat-island effect is estimated at about 3–5°C. The risks are closely connected with urban planning and infrastructure.

secs.t: Causes of urbanisation - push and pull

x: Exam angle: statement sets mixing push (rural unemployment) and pull (urban jobs, amenities) - usually all correct.
Rural unemployment and monsoon failure push people out of rural areas, while urban employment and amenities attract them to cities.
Migration
is the major component of urbanisation when natural increase in rural and urban areas is broadly similar.

secs.t: UN-Habitat and urban forums - Right to the City, APMCHUD

x: SDG 11
seeks to make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable, directly corresponding to the UN-Habitat mandate.
The Right to the City means that residents, including migrant workers, should be able to live in and participate in shaping the city.
UN-Habitat was established in 1978 after Habitat I, is headquartered in Nairobi, and adopted the New Urban Agenda at Habitat III in Quito in 2016.

secs.t: Municipal finance - own revenue, 74th Amendment, municipal bonds, Finance Commission grants

x: Property tax, advertisement tax, professional tax and income from municipal enterprises are all sources of own revenue of urban local bodies.
Water supply, public health and sanitation, slum improvement, urban poverty alleviation, fire services and vital statistics are all included among the listed municipal functions.
The Urbanisation Premium is proposed in connection with the merger of peri-urban villages into urban local governance structures.

secs.t: AP urbanisation - Capital Region, corporations, agglomerations

x: A UN-Habitat Centre of Excellence is proposed to be set up at
Amaravati
in the Andhra Pradesh Capital Region.
Swachha Andhra Corporation and the Municipal Administration and Urban Development department are promoting wastewater reuse under the 'One Water' approach.
The
Nanaghat inscription
is associated with the reference to Nigama Sabha as a city-administration institution under the Satavahanas.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Under-counting urbanisation can leave peri-urban areas outside adequate municipal planning and finance, thereby starving them of municipal funds.

The correct sequence is 1 June 1993 for the 74th Amendment provisions, 1997 for Bangalore's first municipal bond, 1998 for Ahmedabad's bond without State guarantee, and 2017 for the formation of MoHUA.

x: The 100 cities under the Smart Cities Mission were selected through
a competitive challenge
involving a two-stage selection process.
Additional sources include ULB own funds, Finance Commission grants, municipal bonds, PPP, loans and convergence.
CITIIS 2.0 covers 18 Smart Cities and focuses on integrated waste management, with AFD, KfW, the EU and NIUA as associated partners.

secs.t: Urban programmes → objective; urban or rural focus

x: Rurban Mission has a rural focus, DAY-NULM targets the urban poor, and HRIDAY is an urban heritage programme.
DAY-NULM
focuses on self-employment, skill development, shelters and support for street vendors among the urban poor.
The third pair is incorrect.

secs.t: AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0 - thrust areas, mission cities, coverage

x: AMRUT includes ULBs with population of one lakh or more, capitals, HRIDAY cities, river-stem cities, hill-state, island and tourist cities.
AMRUT’s thrust areas include water supply, sewerage and septage, storm-water drains, green spaces and parks, non-motorised transport and capacity building.
AMRUT 2.0 includes all four elements: complete sewerage and septage coverage in the 500 AMRUT cities, water-body rejuvenation, outcome-based funding and support for JJM-Urban.

secs.t: HRIDAY - heritage cities, AP town

x: HRIDAY is the
National Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana
, launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
HRIDAY promotes heritage-sensitive planning covering cultural, natural, living and built heritage.
Ajmer, Velankanni and Kanchipuram are HRIDAY cities.
Ajmer, Amritsar, Badami and Dwarka
are all included in the HRIDAY list.

secs.t: Urban Infrastructure Development Fund - budget, manager, source, eligible cities

x: UIDF is intended to support infrastructure development in
Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities
UIDF is funded from banks’ priority sector lending shortfall and is approximately Rs.
The Urban Challenge Fund provides central funding equal to
25 per cent
of the project cost, subject to the city raising at least 50 per cent through specified sources.

secs.t: Urban housing - PMAY-U verticals, PMAY-U 2.0, GHTC-India, Light House Projects

x: PMAY-U seeks to provide
pucca all-weather houses in all statutory towns
ISSR, AHP and BLC are Centrally Sponsored Schemes, whereas CLSS is a Central Sector scheme.
PMAY-U 2.0 includes BLC, AHP, Affordable Rental Housing and the Interest Subsidy Scheme.
The listed Light House Project cities are Indore, Rajkot, Chennai, Ranchi, Agartala and Lucknow.

secs.t: Urban scheme chronology - JNNURM, SBM-U, AMRUT, SCM; JNNURM features

x: JNNURM was launched in December 2005, SBM-Urban on 2 October 2014, and AMRUT and the Smart Cities Mission were launched in June 2015.
AMRUT, Smart Cities Mission and PMAY-U were launched on the same day in June 2015; among the given pairs,
AMRUT and Smart Cities Mission
are correctly paired.
JNNURM provided for reserving
25 per cent
of developed land for Economically Weaker Sections and Low Income Groups.

secs.t: AP urban schemes - TIDCO housing, Anna Canteens, Swachh Andhra

x: The
Swachha Andhra Corporation
runs the 46 ULB Project Management Units.
All three statements are correct: segregation is 96.07 per cent, 6,890 TPD is processed, and 104 STPs provide 690.90 MLD capacity.
The cited ₹19,561 crore was mobilised through AMRUT 2.0, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, the Urban Challenge Fund, UIDF and SBM 2.0.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The major criticism is that schemes are sector-specific and chronically under-utilised, while ULBs often lack the fiscal capacity to borrow.

The stated Andhra Pradesh-specific facts are four Smart Cities, Amaravati as an HRIDAY city and an MoU with UN-Habitat.

secs.t: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover, beneficiaries, features, senior citizens

x: The beneficiary base was identified using deprivation criteria from the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011.
Childhood cancer is covered, pre-existing diseases are covered from day one, and women hold approximately 49% of cards and account for about 48% of admissions.
PM-JAY was launched on
23 September 2018
and subsumed the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana.

secs.t: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP

x: PM-ABHIM aims to create pandemic-ready health infrastructure, whereas ABDM seeks an interoperable digital health ecosystem.

Sanjeevani is intended to create a health profile and ABHA for every citizen while integrating PHCs, e-Aushadhi, 108, 104, telemedicine and AI.

secs.t: Public expenditure on health - National Health Accounts, OOPE, NHP 2017

x: The missing middle consists of more than 40 crore Indians who are outside full subsidy coverage but cannot afford private healthcare.
NHP 2017 envisaged higher public health spending, a shift toward preventive and primary care, and universal health coverage.
Government health spending was stated as 1.43% of GDP against the NHP 2017 target of

secs.t: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF

x: ULLAS concerns adult literacy; DIKSHA is the digital infrastructure and e-content platform; Samagra Shiksha integrates school education; NIPUN Bharat focuses on foundational literacy and numeracy.
The cited scale is 14.71 lakh schools and 24.69 crore students; government schools constitute about 69%, and approximately 27% of the population is aged 3–18.

secs.t: Health programmes → launch year and target group

x: Janani Suraksha Yojana was launched in 2005 to provide cash assistance for institutional deliveries, with particular focus on BPL, SC and ST women.
PMSMA was launched in 2016 for pregnant women in the second and third trimesters and provides free antenatal care on the ninth day of every month.
All four pairings are correct: PMSMA concerns antenatal care, JSY institutional delivery assistance, U-WIN vaccination records, and RKSK adolescent health.

secs.t: AP healthcare - Aarogyasri / NTR Vaidya Seva, Family Physician, telemedicine, village clinics

x: Under the Family Physician concept, PHC doctors visit villages on fixed days through 104 mobile units.
The village health clinics are located at the
village secretariat level
, complementing the Family Physician system.
A total of 168 Block Public Health Units have been sanctioned in Andhra Pradesh.
Under the Family Physician concept, PHC doctors
visit village health clinics on fixed days

secs.t: Human capital formation - concept, drivers

x: Human capital formation supports inclusive growth by improving education, health and skills, thereby expanding capabilities across society.
Kerala is cited as a classic case in which
adequate basic health and education facilities
contribute to a low infant mortality rate.
The stated outcomes are an
MMR of 88 per lakh live births, stunting of 29.3 per cent and wasting of 19 per cent

secs.t: AP education schemes - Amma Vodi / Thalliki Vandanam, Nadu-Nedu, Gorumudda / PM POSHAN

x: Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu was launched in 2019, Amma Vodi in January 2020, Jagananna Gorumudda in 2020, and Thalliki Vandanam in 2025.
Nadu-Nedu was designed for school infrastructure and its model was also used for upgrading PHCs and CHCs.
Jagananna Gorumudda, introduced in 2020, is an enriched mid-day meal menu implemented under PM POSHAN.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The term ‘missing middle’ refers to approximately 40 crore people who remain inadequately covered by existing health-financing arrangements.
All four are identified concerns: declining health-budget share, weak learning outcomes despite enrolment, the missing middle and high out-of-pocket expenditure.
Kerala is presented as a classic example of health- and education-led human capital, reflected in its low infant mortality rate.

rows.title: Indian agriculture - importance, land use classification, cropping seasons and cropping pattern
sub: Group-II M2-A-43: Indian agriculture - importance, land use and cropping pattern

secs.t: AP agro-climatic zones - number, zone → districts, Planning Commission and NARP zones

x: Exam angle: matching zones to districts, e.g. Southern zone = Nellore, Scarce Rainfall zone = Kurnool/Anantapuramu.
Exam angle: answer "six" and name the Survey; count questions have changed their key over the years.
The Planning Commission identified 15 agro-climatic regions with 72 sub-zones, whereas NARP divided the country into 127 agro-climatic zones.
Older classifications and the 2017 Group-II key used seven, whereas the current AP Socio-Economic Survey gives six zones.
The North Coastal, Godavari, Krishna and Southern zones have their zonal headquarters at Anakapalle, Maruteru, Lam–Guntur and Tirupati respectively.

secs.t: AP cropping pattern - largest crop, foodgrain after paddy, commercial crops, foodgrain area

x: The recorded foodgrain production figures are 143.31 lakh tonnes, 161.86 lakh tonnes and 190.29 lakh tonnes for 2023–24, 2024–25 and 2025–26 respectively.
The foodgrain area in Andhra Pradesh in 2021–22 was approximately
41.3 lakh hectares
; an earlier examination key gave the figure as nearly 41.44 lakh hectares.
Horticulture, oil palm and aquaculture are expanding, while ragi, jowar and groundnut show declining trends; low MSP support is cited for ragi and jowar.

secs.t: Agricultural census - size classes, women's share, largest holding state, AP holdings

x: Exam angle: number-vs-area contrast (85-86% of holdings, 44-47% of area) and the census year attached to each figure.
Small and marginal farmers together comprise holdings
up to 2 hectares
: marginal holdings are below 1 hectare and small holdings are 1–2 hectares.
The references correspond respectively to 1971, 2010–11, 2015–16 and 2021–22 provisional Andhra Pradesh results.
An operational holding comprises land used for agricultural production and operated as one technical unit, regardless of title, size or location.
The
five
size classes are marginal, small, semi-medium, medium and large.

secs.t: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid

x: Kharif crops are generally sown in June–July with the onset of the south-west monsoon and harvested around September–October or October–November.
Rabi crops are sown after the monsoon withdrawal and depend substantially on
western disturbances and irrigation
Zaid is the short summer cropping window, generally extending from March to June, and it depends substantially on irrigation.
Zaid Kharif is associated with sowing in August–September and includes
rapeseed and oilseeds
, harvested around December–January.

secs.t: Crop classification - cash vs food crops, crops of both seasons

x: Paddy is grown in both seasons, with 14.04 lakh hectares in Kharif and 6.93 lakh hectares in Rabi in 2024–25.
Groundnut is an oilseed, tea is a plantation crop and fruits belong to horticulture.
Paddy, maize, jowar, bajra and pulses
are reported as grown in both Kharif and Rabi in Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Nine-fold land use classification - net sown area, forest share, cropping intensity

x: Net area sown accounted for 36.29 per cent, forests 22.63 per cent, current fallows 8.96 per cent and barren and unculturable land 8.19 per cent.
Tubewells accounted for 47.3 per cent, canals 24.7 per cent, other wells 13.2 per cent, other sources 12 per cent and tanks 2.8 per cent of net irrigated area.
The earlier APSES 2024-25 reported figure for
was 49.55 lakh hectares, or 30.4 per cent of the geographical area.

secs.t: Cropping pattern trends - rice, pulses, oilseeds, foodgrains vs non-foodgrains

x: Pulses and oilseeds have stagnant yields, while rice and wheat acreage increased in the three States in association with assured MSP procurement.
Horticulture production reached 367.72 million tonnes and overtook foodgrain production of 357.73 million tonnes in 2024-25.
The proposed shift of about 20 per cent of rice area towards pulses and legumes aims to reduce urea use and save groundwater.

secs.t: Importance of agriculture - share in GVA vs employment, growth trend

x: Agriculture contributes nearly one-fifth of national income at current prices and employs 46.1% of the workforce according to the cited recent estimates.
India's agricultural growth averaged 4.4%, compared with the global average of 2.9%, giving a difference of
1.5 percentage points
Agriculture's share in GVA is about one-fifth, while its employment share is much higher; it also supplies agro-industries and forms the base of food security.

secs.t: Agricultural sector since 1991 - liberalisation, WTO, GM crops, reforms and impacts

x: Bt cotton in 2002 remains the only major GM breakthrough, no new GM approvals have followed it with mustard and brinjal pending, and genome-edited rice varieties such as Kamala have been released.

Economic liberalisation began in 1991, the WTO Agreement on Agriculture took effect in 1995, Bt cotton appeared as the major breakthrough in 2002, and genome-edited rice varieties were released later.

x: Andhra Pradesh had sown
20.35 lakh hectares
, compared with 25.63 lakh hectares in the corresponding period a year earlier.
The planned response included shifting towards
pulses and drought-resilient crops
in view of the deficient rainfall conditions.
The listed constraints include fragmented holdings, monsoon dependence, soil-fertility loss and weak credit.
Paddy occupied 20.97 lakh hectares out of Andhra Pradesh's total foodgrain area of 37.51 lakh hectares in 2024-25.

Namami Gange is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti, has World Bank support, and Arth Ganga concerns river-linked livelihoods.

Hirakud is on the Mahanadi, Rihand is on the Rihand, the Indira Gandhi Canal originates from the Harike barrage on the Sutlej-Beas system, and Ukai is on the Tapi.

accounted for the largest share, 47.3% of India's net irrigated area in 2021–22.
Tanks are important in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu because these regions have
undulating hard-rock terrain

secs.t: PM-KUSUM - components, solar pumps

x: Component A covers 10,000 MW of decentralised grid-connected solar plants, generally of 0.5–2 MW capacity, located near substations.
Component B provides 14 lakh standalone solar pumps of up to 7.5 HP to replace diesel pumps.
PM-KUSUM seeks to de-dieselise agriculture while adding to farmers’ income through solar energy interventions.
In Andhra Pradesh, PM-KUSUM Component C covers 228 plants with an aggregate capacity of 1,162.80 MW.

secs.t: AP irrigation - Polavaram, HNSS, Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda, APMIP

Veligonda Phase-I was inaugurated at
Gantavanipalli in Markapuram district
on 31 August 2026.
The White Paper proposed completing 36 projects by December 2028 at a cost of ₹35,555 crore under an Irrigation Action Calendar.

x: The
2026 El Niño drought
has made the Irrigation Action Calendar a priority in Andhra Pradesh.
Solar pumps may reduce diesel dependence but can also encourage groundwater over-draw.
The groundwater consequences of solar pumps vary according to local hydrogeological conditions.
Rayalaseema depends on lifted Krishna and Godavari water and drip irrigation, while Andhra Pradesh ranks first in micro-irrigation.

Conservation or zero tillage, contour ploughing, mulching and crop rotation are soil-moisture practices.
Zero Budget Natural Farming promotes
mulching and contour farming
as important soil and moisture conservation practices.

was the first State to make rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory for all buildings.
APWALTA 2002 requires rainwater harvesting on plots of
200 square metres and above

x: The idea of interlinking rivers in India is traced back to
Sir Arthur Cotton
in the nineteenth century.
The Task Force on Inter-Linking of Rivers was set up in 2002 under
Suresh Prabhu
Pre-feasibility reports have been prepared for all 30 links, feasibility reports for 26, and detailed project reports for 14, including one intra-State link.

x: The National Water Resources Council is chaired by the
Prime Minister
; Chief Ministers are its members.
The policy focuses on recycling and reuse, micro-irrigation incentives and community participation, among other measures.
In May 2019, the Ministry of Jal Shakti was formed by merging the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation with the
Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation

secs.t: Priority links - Ken-Betwa, Godavari-Cauvery, Pattiseema

By taking Godavari water to the Krishna delta, the Pattiseema project helps save water stored in Srisailam for
Rayalaseema
Nagavali–Champavathi
is listed as an Andhra Pradesh intra-State link, whereas the other listed projects carry a specific progress, proposed status or quantity detail.

secs.t: Command Area Development and Water Management - launch, components, status

x: Field channels, drains, land levelling and Water Users' Associations are components of Command Area Development.
CADWM runs under PMKSY-HKKP; new approvals stopped after 2021-22, while ongoing works continue.
M-CADWM commenced from 2025-26 with an allocation of ₹1,600 crore and uses underground piped irrigation along with SCADA/IoT water accounting.
Twenty-seven CAD&WM projects under LTIF are complete, covering 22.21 lakh hectares of culturable command area.

secs.t: National Water Mission - water-use efficiency target

x: The National Water Mission has a headline target of increasing water-use efficiency by
The Bureau of Water Use Efficiency was established under the National Water Mission in
October 2022
The National Water Mission declared 75 Water Heritage Structures, which are listed on the Jal-Itihas sub-portal.
The sixth edition launched on 22 March 2025 carried the theme “
Jal Sanchay, Jan Bhagidari: Jan Jagrukta Ki Or

held the top position in the Composite Water Management Index referred to for 2026.

secs.t: Per capita water availability - thresholds and trend

x: Per capita annual water availability below 1,700 m³ is treated as
water-stressed
Availability below
per person per year is classified as water-scarce.
The chronological sequence is 1,816 m³ in 2001, 1,545 m³ in 2011, 1,341 m³ projected for 2025 and 1,140 m³ projected for 2050.

80 TMC
of Godavari water to the Krishna basin.
The diverted Krishna basin water feeds the
HNSS and GNSS
projects for Rayalaseema.
Veligonda Phase-I was inaugurated on 31 August 2026 and involves a Krishna to Nallamala Sagar transfer, with 10.7 TMC and 1.19 lakh acres associated with it.
