secs.t: Fertiliser subsidy - highest-subsidy fertiliser, NBS, DBT, neem-coated urea, nano urea/DAP, consumption

x: The listed P&K fertilisers under NBS include
DAP, MOP, SSP and complexes
NBS provides a fixed per-kilogram subsidy on nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur, announced annually.
Under fertiliser DBT, subsidy is paid to companies after the fertiliser is sold at the Point of Sale (PoS).
Neem coating slows nitrogen release and stops diversion of farm urea to industry.
A 500 ml bottle of IFFCO Nano Urea is stated to replace
one 45 kg bag of conventional urea
PM-PRANAM allows States to retain 50% of the subsidy saved through reduced chemical fertiliser consumption.
Soil Health Cards were launched in 2015, are issued free every two years, and are associated with the stated reductions in fertiliser use and increases in yields.
Nano Urea and Nano DAP are applied as
foliar spray
s, and their absorption efficiency is reported to increase by 80%.
P&K fertilisers
are covered under the Nutrient Based Subsidy regime, whereas urea is identified separately as the largest subsidy item.

secs.t: Extension services - KCC, KVK, ATMA, agromet advisories

x: Kisan Call Centres use the toll-free number 1800-180-1551, answer queries in 22 languages and operate from 17 locations.
KVKs are 100% centrally funded under ICAR and coordinated by 11 Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes (ATARIs).
SREP stands for
Strategic Research and Extension Plans
, through which ATMA plans district extension activities.
The principle “seeing is believing” is implemented through
demonstrations
, along with learning by doing.
ANGRAU
runs weather-linked SMS alerts and diagnostic apps for agromet advisories.

secs.t: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status

x: ICAR released 562 new high-yielding field-crop varieties during 2019–21.
Climate-resilient varieties of 25 crops were released in January 2026, while 3,236 HYVs had been notified since 2014 compared with 3,969 during 1969–2014.
SRR is the percentage of crop area sown with certified or quality seed.
Under the Seed Village approach, farmers receive foundation seed and produce certified seed locally.
DRR Dhan 100 Kamala was developed from
Samba Mahsuri
Pusa DST Rice 1 was developed from MTU1010 and was due for commercial launch.
The release comprised 122 cereal varieties and 24 cotton varieties, including 22 Bt cotton varieties.

x: In vermicomposting, earthworms convert organic waste into nutrient-rich manure.
Andhra Pradesh set aside
₹62.20 crore
for green manure seed for Kharif 2026.
PGS-India
is the alternative certification route mentioned alongside NPOP for organic production.
APCNF is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS) and uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham.
NMSA is one of the eight NAPCC missions, was merged into PM-RKVY from 2022–23, and includes the listed components.
The Kharif 2026 green-manure drive involves ₹62.20 crore and 91,918 quintals of sunn hemp, dhaincha and green gram seed.

secs.t: AP inputs - fertiliser consumption, Rythu Seva Kendras

x: RSKs handle inputs, soil testing, e-Panta, CCRCs, insurance and procurement.
Soil sampling initially ran through 10,778 RSKs; these were rationalised to 8,489 functional centres.
Permanent buildings for RSKs are coming up under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (
MGNREGS
AP Seeds is supplying 7.46 lakh quintals of subsidised seed through RSKs, involving ₹294 crore in 2026–27.

secs.t: Pesticides - Insecticides Act, bans, neem pesticides, IPM

x: The Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 proposes to replace the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971.
All three statements are correct: at least 66 pesticides used in India are banned elsewhere, Aldrin killed mugger crocodiles in Kota, and the Supreme Court banned Endosulfan in 2011.
IPM combines biological control, cultural control and need-based chemical control in order to reduce pesticide use.

secs.t: ICAR technology projects - NATP, NAIP

x: NATP began in 1998 with World Bank aid, while NAIP ran from 2006 to 2014 and was also World Bank-funded.
NAIP components included ICAR as a catalyst for change, production-to-consumption research, sustainable rural livelihood security, and basic and strategic research.

secs.t: Farm mechanisation - SMAM, custom hiring, Drone Didi

x: The stated SMAM figures are 27,563 custom hiring centres nationally and 239 in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26.
In 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh reported 38,610 machines, 239 custom hiring centres and expenditure of ₹169.32 crore under SMAM.
All four figures are stated for the period 2014-15 to 2025-26: ₹9,639.96 crore, 20.93 lakh machines, 646 hi-tech hubs and 25,260 farm machinery banks.

secs.t: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution

x: Although the package included HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, assured irrigation, pesticides and mechanisation, the scientific core was the use of HYV seeds.
Kalyan Sona and Sonalika
were associated with HYV wheat derived from Norman Borlaug’s Mexican dwarf wheats.
The programme became full-fledged from 1966 after the 1965-66 and 1966-67 droughts, foodgrain production fell to 72.3 and 74.2 MT, and India depended on PL-480 supplies.
The Green Revolution began in the mid-1960s after droughts in 1965-66 and 1966-67 caused foodgrain output to fall sharply.
The Second Green Revolution focuses on all the listed areas, including Shree Anna, precision technologies, resource-efficient irrigation, integrated management and climate resilience.

secs.t: Irrigation inputs - micro-irrigation, PMKSY components, PM-KUSUM, tubewell area

umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2015–16

The
Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme
(AIBP) is intended for faster completion of major and medium projects.
Har Khet Ko Pani includes CAD&WM, surface minor irrigation, repair, renovation and restoration of water bodies, and groundwater-related measures.

secs.t: Agricultural research institutes → location

x: CRRI is located at Cuttack, IARI at New Delhi (Pusa), CTRI at Rajahmundry and ICRISAT at Patancheru, Hyderabad.
The Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI) is now called the National Rice Research Institute and is located at
Cuttack
All three pairs are correctly matched.
The Indian Institute of Maize Research is located at Ludhiana.

secs.t: Farm subsidies vs public investment - classifying input subsidies, MSP, research, irrigation

x: Fertiliser subsidy is an input subsidy and represents a current transfer.
Power subsidy and interest subvention are input subsidies, while rural infrastructure is public investment.
MSP is a price support measure.
Although subsidies helped small farmers adopt high-yielding varieties, they are criticised for disproportionately benefiting prosperous regions and the fertiliser industry.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A urea-centred subsidy regime is criticised for distorting the balance among nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, expressed as the NPK ratio.
APCNF is recognised as a global natural-farming model, and RSKs deliver agricultural inputs at the village level in Andhra Pradesh.
The plan envisages entrepreneurship centres in all KVKs by December 2028, and Andhra Pradesh has sought Central assistance for drones and mechanisation.

secs.t: Revolution → product + person; Rainbow Revolution pairs

x: Rainbow Revolution is the umbrella term for the different colour revolutions and represents holistic agricultural growth across crops, livestock and fisheries.
Operation Flood began in 1970, the Yellow Revolution is associated with 1986–87, the Golden Revolution with 1991–2003, and the National Beekeeping and Honey Mission with 2020.
Pink Revolution covers meat processing, poultry, prawn, onion and pharmaceuticals; Red covers meat and tomato; Grey covers fertilisers; and Black covers petroleum.
Operation Flood was run by the NDDB from 1970 and built a national milk grid on the Anand or Amul cooperative model.

secs.t: HYV varieties - IR-8, first dwarf rice, Mexican wheat

x: Lerma Rojo 64-A and Sonora 64
were Mexican dwarf wheat varieties associated with Borlaug.
HYVs are short-statured, respond to fertiliser and water, mature faster and can therefore support double cropping.
Wheat was the first crop transformed, Punjab was the pioneer state, and TN-1 was the first semi-dwarf rice variety in India.

secs.t: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien

x: Operation Flood copied the Amul three-tier cooperative model developed at Anand in Gujarat.

Verghese Kurien worked with
Tribhuvandas Patel at Anand
in the development of the dairy cooperative movement.

secs.t: Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI)

x: BGREI is a sub-scheme of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (
RKVY
BGREI aims to raise rice-based productivity in eastern India through high-yielding varieties, irrigation, balanced nutrient use and integrated pest management.
Purvodaya follows the logic of improving rice-based productivity and shifting the rice bowl towards eastern India, as envisaged by BGREI.

secs.t: Green Revolution outcomes - crops, states, disparities, ecological costs

x: Exam angle: assertion-reason questions linking HYV + fertiliser + irrigation to both higher output and ecological damage.
The Green Revolution focused strongly on wheat and rice and contributed to the neglect of
pulses, oilseeds and millets
The intensive use of HYV seeds, fertilisers and assured irrigation explains both higher output and ecological pressures such as groundwater depletion and soil-related problems.

secs.t: Components - HYV, irrigation, fertilisers, credit, MSP; package approach, IADP, IAAP

x: The package approach combined HYV seeds with assured irrigation, chemical fertilisers, pesticides, mechanisation, institutional credit and MSP or assured procurement.
IADP began in 1960 as a pilot in seven districts of seven states, and West Godavari was Andhra Pradesh's IADP district.
IAAP was introduced in
as an extension of the intensive agricultural programme approach.
IAAP extended to 114 districts and 117 blocks in Andhra Pradesh, beginning in West Godavari.

secs.t: AP and the Green Revolution - deltas, MTU and BPT varieties

x: The Godavari and Krishna delta canals, associated with Sir Arthur Cotton's Dowleswaram barrage, helped make coastal Andhra Pradesh a rice-surplus belt.
BPT 5204 is the parent of DRR Dhan 100 Kamala; MTU 1010 is the parent of Pusa DST Rice 1; and MTU 7029 is the popular mega-variety Swarna.
MTU 1010 is a Rabi rice variety of southern states and is the parent of the genome-edited Pusa DST Rice 1.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Johl Committee proposed shifting
20 per cent
of the paddy area to address the problems associated with water-intensive rice-wheat monoculture.
The sequence is first GMO in 1973, first recombinant-DNA-produced insulin, Bt cotton as India’s first GM crop in 2002, and the proposed commercial launch of Pusa Rice DST1 in 2026.

secs.t: Foodgrain production - advance estimates, records, AP production

353.96 million tonnes in the 3rd Advance Estimate
; the final figure was later revised to 357.73 million tonnes.

283 million tonnes

The decadal average agricultural growth for FY16-FY25 was
, described as the highest ever.

Green Revolution
Crops grew by only 3.5%; fishing and aquaculture was the fastest-growing listed component at 8.8%, followed by livestock at 7.1%.

secs.t: Largest producer state → crop

Chhattisgarh
is described as the 'Rice Bowl of central India'.

secs.t: Yield per hectare - rice (AP), wheat, pulses, cotton; India vs world and China

x: The cited explanation links lower yields in major rice states with climatic stresses, while Punjab benefits from canal and tubewell irrigation despite low rainfall.
Bt cotton was associated with an increase in yield from 190 kg/ha in 2002 to
480 kg/ha
Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat
have the highest pulse yields, helped by black or semi-arid soils and high seed replacement rates.
Rabi paddy recorded a yield of
6,979 kg per hectare
in 2024–25, compared with 5,612 kg per hectare for Kharif paddy.

secs.t: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices

x: Foodgrain production in 2024–25 was a record
357.73 million tonnes
, equivalent to 3,577.3 lakh tonnes.
Horticulture production was 367.72 million tonnes, exceeding foodgrain production of 357.73 million tonnes in 2024–25.
India is both the largest producer and the largest consumer of pulses, with production of 25.68 million metric tonnes as the cited latest figure.
India ranks second globally in
rice, wheat, fruits, vegetables and eggs

India is ranked first in the world in
milk, pulses, spices, jute and millets
according to the stated comparison.

secs.t: Yield concepts and gaps - cereal yield, causes, pathways

x: Better seed quality is promoted through the Seed Replacement Rate and Varietal Replacement Rate, abbreviated as
SRR and VRR
India's yields of cereals, maize, soybean and pulses trail global averages, whereas
groundnut
is identified as an exception because of semi-arid concentration and improved varieties.
Rice is approximately 67% irrigated, pulses approximately 26% irrigated, the average holding size is 1.08 hectares, and soybean yields are below 2 tonnes per hectare in many districts.

secs.t: Area trends - stagnant or declining crops

x: Cotton
area fell by 18 lakh hectares, and its output declined to 290.91 lakh bales in 2025–26 from approximately 350 lakh bales.
The Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses has an outlay of
₹11,440 crore
The mission targets 350 lakh tonnes from 310 lakh hectares, provides 100% MSP procurement for tur, urad and masoor, and runs from 2025–26 to 2030–31.

secs.t: Total factor productivity - trend and drivers

x: Total factor productivity is the part of output growth that cannot be explained by increased use of inputs such as land, labour, capital and fertiliser.
Research, new varieties, irrigation, rural roads, markets, extension and education are stated drivers of agricultural TFP.

Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, eastern Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal

The mission targets
tur, urad and masur
and seeks to end pulse imports.

The Ashok Dalwai Committee was set up in 2016, submitted its report in 2018 and was chaired by Ashok Dalwai.

secs.t: National Missions - focus and crops covered (NFSM, NMSA/RAD, MIDH, NMEO, RKVY)

x: Exam angle: mission → crops matching; NMSA → NAPCC link; which mission was renamed NFSNM.
MIDH covers all the listed horticultural crops and products, including fruits, vegetables, spices, flowers, mushrooms, coconut, cashew, cocoa and bamboo.
NMEO-Oil Palm was launched in August 2021 with an outlay of
₹11,040 crore
and focuses particularly on the North-East and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

secs.t: Agricultural policy since 1991 - liberalisation and WTO impacts

x: Sharad Joshi
supported globalisation, whereas Tikait of BKU and Nanjundaswamy of KRRS opposed the Dunkel Draft.
Input costs for fertiliser, seed and pesticide rose by over
300 per cent
since the early 2000s, while real farm incomes stagnated.
Farmer groups fear that the India-U.S. trade deal and other FTAs may adversely affect
agriculture
through increased trade competition.

secs.t: National Agriculture Policy 2000 - growth target, key thrusts

x: The National Agriculture Policy was announced in
July 2000
The policy targeted agricultural growth in excess of 4% per annum.
The policy emphasised private participation, price protection, agricultural insurance and a broad-based Rainbow Revolution across farm sub-sectors.
Silver Revolution is associated with eggs.

secs.t: Sustainable agriculture and rainfed areas - meaning, goals, NRAA

x: Sustainable agriculture maintains the quality of land while meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.
Rainfed farming covers about 50–60% of net sown area and contributes approximately 40% of food production.
NRAA provides expert knowledge and coordinates the upgrading of dryland and rainfed areas through a watershed approach.

secs.t: Phases of agricultural development in India

x: The pre-Green Revolution phase covered 1951–68 and included land reforms, irrigation, Community Development, PL-480 imports and the droughts of 1965–67.
The Early Green Revolution phase was 1968–81 and was marked by HYV seeds, initially in wheat, along with fertiliser, irrigation and the New Agricultural Strategy.
The phases occurred in the order Pre-Green Revolution (1951–68), Early Green Revolution (1968–81) and Later Green Revolution (1987–92).

secs.t: National Commission on Agriculture and National Commission on Farmers

x: The National Commission on Agriculture functioned during 1970–76 and submitted its report in 1976 under the chairmanship of
Nathu Ram Mirdha
The National Commission on Farmers recommended MSP at C2 plus 50 per cent, while the Government MSP policy uses 1.5 times A2+FL.
The National Commission on Farmers, chaired by M.S. Swaminathan, recommended MSP at
C2 cost plus 50 percent

secs.t: Schemes for better price realisation - PM-AASHA, e-NAM, Operation Greens

x: The
Price Support Scheme
(PSS) under PM-AASHA involves procurement through agencies such as NAFED and NCCF.
Operation Greens initially focused on stabilising Tomato–Onion–Potato prices, on the lines of Operation Flood.
Operation Greens was included in Budget 2018–19 and, from 2021–22, was widened from the original TOP commodities to 22 perishables.

secs.t: AP agriculture support - agriculture budget, PM-KISAN, Annadata Sukhibhava

x: The 2026–27 Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Budget had an approximate outlay of ₹53,753 crore, included ₹12,153 crore for the Agriculture Department, and represented 33.20 per cent of GSDP.
PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme, operative from 1 December 2018, that provides ₹6,000 per year in three instalments of ₹2,000 to eligible landholding farmer families.
The cut-off date specified for identifying landholding families under PM-KISAN was
1 February 2019

secs.t: Doubling Farmers' Income - committee, sources of growth, target year

x: The seven sources include crop productivity, livestock productivity, resource-use efficiency, cropping intensity, diversification to high-value crops, better price realisation and movement to non-farm jobs.
The approach shifts from “production” to “income” through value addition, clusters, e-NAM and APMC reform, post-harvest infrastructure, livestock-fisheries integration and land-leasing laws.
The strategy identifies a shift to non-farm jobs as a source of income growth;
reduction of non-farm employment opportunities
is therefore not included.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Union Budget 2026–27 allocated
₹1.3 lakh crore
to agriculture, representing a 2.6 per cent increase.
Farm unions criticised the absence of
statutory MSP and debt relief
in the Union Budget 2026–27.
Andhra Pradesh leads India in oil palm cultivation, with 2.49 lakh hectares or 48 per cent of India’s area, and produced 22.81 lakh metric tonnes of fresh fruit bunches in 2024–25.

sub: Group-II M2-A-47: Agricultural credit - issues of adequacy, indebtedness and loan waivers
Group-II M2-A-53: Agrarian distress - causes, farmer suicides and policy response

secs.t: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs

x: All three statements are correct: India had about 146 million holdings averaging 1.08 hectares in 2015-16, while only provisional State results of the 2021-22 Census were available as stated.
The provisional Andhra Pradesh figures are an average holding size of 0.86 hectares and 96.90 lakh holdings, compared with 0.94 hectares and 85.24 lakh holdings in 2015-16.
Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming
are identified as remedies for the viability constraints of small holdings.

secs.t: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position

x: The National Crime Records Bureau publishes the report titled “
Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India
” (ADSI), which is the cited source for these suicide data.
The Tenant Farmers Association claimed that more than 300 farmers and tenants died by suicide, whereas only 112 were officially recognised.
All three statements are correct: 10,546 farm-sector suicides comprised 4,633 farmers and 5,913 agricultural labourers, representing 6.2 per cent of the total.

secs.t: National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan) - year, reports, MSP formula

x: C2 includes A2, family labour and imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital; hence all three statements are correct.
All four statements reflect the Commission’s recommendations and core vision for economically viable, ecologically sustainable farming and improved farmer welfare.
The National Policy for Farmers, 2007 drew upon the reports of the
National Commission on Farmers
chaired by M. S. Swaminathan.

secs.t: AP agrarian distress - crop holiday committee, CCRC, Licensed Cultivators Act

x: The AP Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011 provided
Loan Eligibility Cards
(LECs) to tenant cultivators.
CCR cards provide access to bank credit, insurance, input subsidy and benefits such as Annadata Sukhibhava without affecting the owner's rights.
The
requirement of the landowner's signature
is a major obstacle for tenant cultivators seeking formal credit and other benefits.

secs.t: Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households - income, debt, AP figures

x: Approximately
50 percent
of agricultural households were indebted according to the NSSO 77th Round.
The 70th Round relates to 2013, the 77th Round to 2019, the next survey is scheduled for 2026–27, and its fieldwork is scheduled from July 2026 to June 2027.
Crop failure, high input costs, unstable prices and dependence on rainfed agriculture are identified causes.
Dependence on rainfed agriculture increases vulnerability to inadequate rainfall and failed borewells, thereby contributing to agrarian distress.

secs.t: Causes of agrarian crisis - costs, prices, debt, climate, fragmentation

x: The stated cycle begins with high input costs, leads to borrowing, crop failure or low prices, non-repayment, fresh borrowing and asset sales, ultimately producing a debt trap.
Tenant farmers pay rent and bear the production risk, while often lacking land passbooks, Kisan Credit Cards and insurance coverage.
AP-specific distress is associated with higher tenant debt, non-institutional borrowing, risky cash crops and delayed procurement.
The UPPSC 2016 key identified
rural poverty
as the effective reason for slow agricultural development.

secs.t: Loan waivers - ADWDRS 2008, AP Runa Mafi, critique

x: The Agricultural Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme was announced in the
Union Budget 2008–09
The AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme was implemented through
Rythu Sadhikara Samstha
Loan waivers can exclude tenants and informal loans, and repeated waivers may weaken repayment and credit discipline.
The stated principle is that preventing the accumulation of unsustainable debt is more important than relying on repeated loan waivers.

secs.t: Crop insurance - PMFBY premium, RWBCIS, AP free crop insurance

x: PMFBY became voluntary in 2020, covers pre-sowing to post-harvest losses and localised calamities, and is a Central Sector Scheme with the Centre’s premium subsidy transferred directly to insurers.
Under Dr YSR Free Crop Insurance during 2019-24, the State paid the entire premium and CCRC holders were covered.
PMFBY was introduced in 2016, replaced NAIS and MNAIS, became voluntary for all farmers from Kharif 2020, and is a Central Sector scheme.
The farmer premium under PMFBY is 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops.
Crop insurance returned to voluntary enrolment from
, when 10.63 lakh farmers enrolled.

secs.t: Moneylenders and informal credit - interest rates, AP moneylending regulation

x: Tenant farmers had an average debt of ₹2,07,444, whereas owner farmers had an average debt of ₹76,306.
The guard-rails prescribe a maximum of three lenders per borrower and a household borrowing cap of ₹2 lakh.
Andhra Pradesh enacted the Microfinance Institutions (Regulation of Money Lending) Act in 2011, following the 2010 microfinance crisis.

secs.t: Loan waiver debate - moral hazard, credit culture, fiscal cost (RBI views)

x: Loan waivers provide immediate relief but do not permanently eliminate structural causes of agrarian distress.
Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the expectation of future waivers explains why repeated waivers can weaken repayment discipline and credit culture.
Politicised waivers, poor recovery and NPAs were associated with the bank-nationalisation era.

secs.t: Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness → chairman

x: R. Radhakrishna
chaired the Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness constituted in 2007.

secs.t: KCC coverage gap for small and marginal farmers

x: There were approximately
7.72 crore
operative KCCs in March 2025.
The comparison is between 7.72 crore operative KCCs and
146 million
agricultural holdings recorded in the 2015–16 Agricultural Census.

Formal credit commonly requires land records, so farmers with officially recorded land ownership are less affected by this particular exclusion than tenants, oral lessees and farmers without documented land rights.

secs.t: Income support - PM-KISAN, Annadata Sukhibhava, KALIA, Rythu Bandhu

x: Annadata Sukhibhava tops up PM-KISAN, and its Kharif 2026 first instalment was ₹7,000 per farmer, involving ₹3,125 crore for 46.85 lakh farmers.

ADWDRS provided full waiver to eligible overdue loans of small and marginal farmers; the AP scheme covered specified loans up to 31 December 2013; Telangana waived crop loans for more than 25 lakh families; horticulture relief was ₹10,000 per acre subject to a family ceiling.

secs.t: Farm protests - demands and outcomes

x: The listed demands were repeal of the three farm laws, legal MSP, and withdrawal of the Electricity (Amendment) Bill and the Air Quality Management Ordinance.
All three statements are correct: the SKM, comprising about 500 farm unions, held village protests from 27 to 31 May 2026 and burnt copies of the Kharif MSP order.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The opposition cited a 54.73 percent rainfall deficit affecting 653 of 685 mandals, with sowing at only 69 percent of normal, and demanded a drought emergency.
In the context of the Kharif 2026 El Nino deficit, farmer bodies demanded
loan relief
; they also highlighted the loss of insurance and credit when actual cultivators are missing from e-crop records.

secs.t: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land

x: The Act abolished
zamindari and inamdari
systems in the Andhra area and facilitated conversion to ryotwari.
Following the Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation, 1949, jagirs and Sarf-e-khas lands became Diwani, or ryotwari, lands after Police Action.
The Act clubbed the husband’s and wife’s land, treated each major son as a separate unit, and allowed an addition of one-fifth of the ceiling for each extra member.

secs.t: Koneru Ranga Rao Committee and National Land Reforms Council

x: Exam angle: "which was not a focus area" - eliminate corporate farming.
The Committee focused on assignment lands, confirmation of land rights, tenancy regulation and land records.
The AP Land Committee headed by Koneru Ranga Rao functioned during
The committee was titled “
State Agrarian Relations and Unfinished Task in Land Reforms

secs.t: Land ceiling laws - unit, limits by land class, surplus declared vs distributed

x: Pre-1972 ceiling laws generally used the individual as the unit and encouraged benami transfers to relatives; the 1972 guidelines shifted to the family unit.
Ceiling legislation developed in two major rounds, around 21 States had such laws by 2020, and less than 2% of cultivable area was redistributed.
Exemptions for plantations, orchards and mechanised farms
reduced the amount of land available for redistribution.

secs.t: Tenancy reform - Operation Barga, rent, security of tenure, ownership rights

x: Tenancy reform sought to regulate rent by limiting it to approximately
one-fourth to one-sixth of the produce
Operation Barga recorded the names of sharecroppers, known as bargadars, and thereby strengthened their rights.
Operation Barga is cited as launched in 1978; another account associates it with 1977, the year the Left Front came to power.

secs.t: Agricultural land leasing - Model Act 2016, first State

x: The Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016 was prepared by
NITI Aayog
, with inputs associated with the T. Haque Committee.
The Model Act sought to legalise leasing, facilitate credit and insurance for tenants, and protect owners’ titles.
The AP CCRC Act, 2019 provides for 11-month cards, while a proposed 2024 law concerned tenant entitlement cards.

secs.t: Cooperative and joint farming - features

x: The Nagpur Resolution of 1959 made
cooperative farming
a party goal.
Cooperative farming was captured by rich peasants, who used it to evade ceiling laws.
All four statements describe the features of joint cooperative farming: voluntary pooling, retained ownership, elected management and distribution based on land and labour contribution.
Compulsory membership is not a feature of joint cooperative farming; participation is voluntary.

secs.t: Constitutional support - Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A-31C, amendments

x: The insertion of Articles 31A and 31B and the Ninth Schedule followed the constitutional issues highlighted in
Kameshwar Singh v. Bihar
The Thirty-fourth Amendment of 1974 and the Sixty-sixth Amendment of 1990 placed additional land laws in the Ninth Schedule, including 55 State Acts, among them Acts of Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Consolidation of holdings and Bhoodan-Gramdan

x: Consolidation succeeded in
Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
, while it made little progress in southern and eastern States.
Bhoodan was initiated by Acharya Vinoba Bhave at
Pochampally in Nalgonda, Telangana
Bhoodan began at Pochampally in 1951, involved pledges exceeding 40 lakh acres, much of it barren, and subsequently led to Gramdan.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The proposal concerns decriminalising two offences among the 42 offences under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling) Act, 1973.
Leasing reform and digitisation of land records have been urged to address continuing problems in land distribution and land administration.
The Srikakulam Naxalite unrest and the droughts of 1966–69 pushed Phase II of land reforms in Andhra Pradesh.

rows.title: Land records and titling - Digital India Land Records Modernisation, SVAMITVA

secs.t: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

x: Modern record rooms, survey or resurvey, data entry, cadastral-map digitisation, State data centres, computerised registration and core GIS are DILRMP components.

Phase 1 (2008-16) focused on digitisation, resurvey, maps and registration-mutation linkage; Phase 2 (2016-26) added ULPIN, NGDRS and related integration; Phase 3 (2026-31) focuses on the GIS-based Land Stack.

secs.t: SVAMITVA - launch, ministry, drone survey, property cards, States

x: SVAMITVA expands to
Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas
SVAMITVA was launched on 24 April 2020, the occasion of National Panchayati Raj Day.
SVAMITVA uses Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS) for geo-referencing.
The target, cost and extension period are 6.62 lakh villages, ₹566.23 crore and up to 2025-26, respectively.

secs.t: ULPIN / Bhu-Aadhaar - meaning, digits

x: ULPIN means Unique Land Parcel Identification Number, or Bhu-Aadhaar.
ULPIN is based on the standards of
ECCMA and OGC
ULPIN had been rolled out in 29 States/UTs and covered 36.67 crore parcels.

secs.t: Conclusive land titling - presumptive vs conclusive, Model Act

x: In the presumptive system, registration records a transaction and title may be challenged through earlier deeds, mutation or possession.
The conclusive system provides for a single authoritative title register, unlike the separate records maintained under the presumptive system.
The Supreme Court held that registration of a transfer deed is distinct from title and did not uphold the Bihar requirement of mandatory proof of mutation.

secs.t: National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS)

x: The National Generic Document Registration System is the ‘One Nation One Registration Software’ under DILRMP, serving sub-registrars and citizens through a common configurable application.
NGDRS had been adopted by 18 States/UTs, while 12 more States/UTs shared data through the system.

secs.t: Land Records Index (NCAER N-LRSI) - AP rank

x: NCAER’s Land Records and Services Index grades States on the digitisation and quality of their land records.
The Department of Land Resources awarded the Bhoomi Samman Platinum grade to
168 districts in 16 States

secs.t: AP land records - resurvey, Webland, Mee Bhoomi, Land Titling Act, Bhu Bharathi

x: The Jagananna Saswatha Bhu Hakku and Bhu Raksha resurvey programme commenced in
December 2020
The reported scale of the resurvey is 6,901 villages and 81 lakh parcels, with approximately 86,000 boundary disputes resolved.
The new passbooks carry the State emblem; 36 lakh had been issued, 56 lakh more were planned by March 2027, and the coverage is 8,232 villages.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Clear titles improve the ability to use land as collateral and can reduce litigation.
Karnataka's Bhoomi project was launched in 2000 and is recognised as a pioneer in computerised Records of Rights, Tenancy and Crops (RTCs).
The National Digital Land Initiative or Land Stack is described as a cloud GIS system with Bhu-Aadhaar assigned to every parcel.

rows.title: Agricultural credit - institutional structure, NABARD, Kisan Credit Card, priority sector lending, interest subvention
sub: Group-II M2-A-46: Agricultural finance - institutional structure, NABARD, Kisan Credit Card and priority sector lending

secs.t: NABARD - committee, year and Plan, HQ, bodies merged, refinance role

x: NABARD took over the RBI's Agricultural Credit Department, Rural Planning and Credit Cell, and the Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation.
NABARD primarily functions as a refinance institution for rural financial institutions rather than lending directly to individual farmers.
NABARD supervises RRBs and cooperative banks and operates the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, but it does not lend directly to farmers as its primary function.
RIDF is funded from deposits made by banks that fall short of their priority-sector lending obligations.

The Warehouse Infrastructure Fund was established in 2013-14 with ₹5,000 crore, the Food Processing Fund in 2014-15 with ₹2,000 crore, the Micro Irrigation Fund is associated with NABARD, and LTIF operates under PMKSY.

secs.t: Agricultural credit trends - agency shares, post-1991 flow, credit target

x: Ground Level Credit quadrupled during FY 2014-FY 2024, recording a CAGR of about
13.06 per cent

The South accounts for about 48 per cent of credit against 17 per cent of cropped area; the East and Central regions account for about 8.2 per cent and 13.7 per cent respectively, while around 60 per cent of credit is short-term.

All three statements are correct: FY25 ground-level credit was ₹28.69 lakh crore against ₹27.50 lakh crore, representing 104 per cent achievement, and credit quadrupled during FY14–FY24 at a 13.06 per cent CAGR.

secs.t: Institutional structure - cooperatives, LDBs, RRBs, direct lenders

x: PACS operate at the village level and lend directly to farmers; DCCBs operate at the district level and finance PACS; StCBs are state apex institutions; Land Development Banks provide long-term credit.
Commercial banks directly lend through rural branches, NABARD provides refinance and development support, and the cooperative structure descends from StCB to DCCB to PACS.
The first land development bank at Jhang was established in 1920, bank nationalisation and the Lead Bank Scheme began in 1969, RRBs were established in 1975, and NABARD was established in 1982.

secs.t: Kisan Credit Card - year, committee, purposes, allied extension

x: The KCC model scheme was prepared by NABARD on the recommendation of the
R.V. Gupta Committee
KCC covers crop cultivation, post-harvest and marketing loans, household consumption, maintenance of farm assets and investment credit for allied activities.
There were 7.72 crore operative KCCs and outstanding KCC short-term credit of ₹10.20 lakh crore as of March 2025.
The revised directions increase the maximum KCC tenure to six years from the earlier five years, for loans from 1 January 2027.
The Andhra Pradesh Pashu KCC provides up to ₹1.60 lakh without collateral at 7 per cent, reduced to 4 per cent on prompt repayment.

secs.t: Interest subvention - MISS, prompt repayment incentive, Kisan Rin Portal

x: Post-harvest loans are available at 7 per cent for up to six months against negotiable warehouse receipts recognised under WDRA, particularly for small and marginal farmers.
Before the Kisan Rin Portal, manual claims under the interest-subvention and prompt-repayment incentive schemes were submitted to
the concerned banks
The portal flagged ₹1,080.88 crore in duplicate or excess claims out of total claims of

secs.t: Rural credit milestones chronology

x: NABARD’s SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, launched in 1992, is regarded as
the world’s largest microfinance programme
Bank nationalisation involving 14 banks was undertaken during the Fourth Plan.

secs.t: Priority sector lending - agriculture target, small and marginal sub-target

x: Priority sector lending norms apply to commercial banks, RRBs, SFBs, Local Area Banks and primary urban cooperative banks.
PSLCs enable banks to buy certificates representing priority sector lending so that they can meet prescribed targets; they do not eliminate the priority sector framework.
The EAC-PM paper reported the concentration of PSL credit in a small share of districts, criticised reliance on PSLCs and called for a review of the 40 per cent target.

secs.t: AP agricultural credit - Annual Credit Plan, tenant credit, JLGs

x: The agricultural target under the AP Annual Credit Plan for 2025–26 was
. ₹2,96,764 crore was the amount disbursed, while ₹2,64,000 crore was the earlier 2024–25 target.
CCRC holders received ₹3,768 crore, while bankers reported ₹1,490 crore to tenants under the 2025–26 Annual Credit Plan.
AP ranks first in SHG-Bank Linkage, contributes approximately 36 per cent of national disbursement and records 99.99 per cent recovery.

secs.t: Rural credit committees → chairman

x: The All India Rural Credit Survey was chaired by A.D. Gorwala, the Working Group on Rural Banks by M. Narasimham, CRAFICARD by B. Sivaraman, and the Agricultural Credit Review Committee by A.M. Khusro.
The All India Rural Credit Survey was chaired by A.D. Gorwala, CRAFICARD by B. Sivaraman, the 2004 Task Force by A. Vaidyanathan and the 2013 Expert Committee by Prakash Bakshi.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The AP Pashu Kisan Credit Card provides collateral-free credit up to ₹1.60 lakh at 7 per cent, with a 3 per cent subvention for timely repayment.
The central region accounts for 30 per cent of gross cropped area but receives only 14.7 per cent of MISS benefits, indicating regional unevenness.

rows.title: Agricultural marketing - APMC system, e-NAM, contract farming, model acts, FPOs, warehousing
sub: Group-II M2-A-48: Agricultural marketing in India - APMC system, problems and reforms
Group-II M2-A-49: Agricultural marketing initiatives - e-NAM, FPOs, contract farming and warehousing

secs.t: Grading and standardisation - AGMARK, Central Agmark and CQC Laboratories

x: AGMARK certification is administered by the
Directorate of Marketing and Inspection
(DMI) under the Ministry of Agriculture.
State grading laboratories grade produce for packers under Agmark, and DMI administers certification.
AGMARKNET was launched in 2000 by the
National Informatics Centre
(NIC) to provide mandi price information.
The proposal seeks to end the dual certification arrangement involving BIS and AGMARK through a single regulatory framework.

secs.t: e-NAM - launch, agency, State reforms, advantages, AP mandis

x: Exam angle: "which reform is required of states" and statement pairs on e-NAM's advantages.
The
Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium
(SFAC) is the lead implementing agency for e-NAM.
e-NAM promotes transparent price discovery, brings more buyers, reduces information asymmetry and enables direct payment to farmers’ accounts.
Warehouse trading with electronic negotiable warehouse receipts (e-NWRs) enables produce stored in WDRA warehouses to be sold through e-NAM.
The listed Andhra Pradesh commodities include castor, ajwain and lemons, along with dry chillies, cotton, turmeric, onions, tomatoes, groundnut and others.
A single-point levy avoids multiple fee points; a single State-wide licence provides wider access; e-NWRs permit warehouse trading; and direct payment reaches the farmer’s account.
Online payments amounted to only Rs 26.88 lakh, and just 11 mandis traded across mandi boundaries, involving Rs 13.98 crore.

secs.t: Farmers' markets → State; AP Rythu Bazar

x: Rythu Bazar facilitates direct sale by farmers to consumers, thereby avoiding commission agents.
Rythu Bazars operate outside the purview of
Agricultural Market Committees
The cited 2025–26 status records 129 functional Rythu Bazars and 10 under construction.
Krishi UDAN facilitates air transport of agricultural produce, especially perishables, helping farmers obtain better prices and higher incomes.

secs.t: APMC system - law, regulated markets, fee, commission agents, problems

x: The market system is supervised at the district level by the DATMO, the
District Agricultural Trade and Market Officer
Regulated markets provide open auctions, standard weights, recorded prices and licensed buyers; they do not require sale to unlicensed buyers.
Cartels of licensed traders, market and licence fees, commission charges, too few mandis and dependence on approved middlemen are identified problems.

secs.t: Marketing agencies and private channels

x: e-Choupal consists of
ITC
’s Internet kiosks linking farmers with markets.
Under this model, neighbouring small farmers pool their holdings and operate them as one large field to obtain scale in inputs and marketing.
Punjab
is identified as the pioneer of contract farming in this context, with PepsiCo in the late 1980s.

secs.t: Farm laws 2020 - three Acts, provisions, repeal

x: Stock limits on cereals, pulses, oilseeds, edible oils, onion and potato could be imposed only in
extraordinary situations
Trade in the specified trade area was outside APMC yards and without State market fee; the Act did not mention MSP.
After repeal of the 2020 Acts,
the AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966
remains the operative framework in Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

x: The Model APLM Act, 2017 proposed warehouses as market yards, a single-point market fee, a unified licence and e-trading.
The 2018 model act keeps contract farming outside the APMC Act, recognises the farmer as the weaker party and covers livestock and services.
Contract Farming Facilitation Groups (CFFGs) are envisaged at the
village or panchayat level
, enabling local facilitation and dispute settlement.
Contract farming involves an agreement with an agri-business firm concerning the price, quantity and/or time of sale in advance.
Under the Small Farmer Large Field model, marginal farmers organise into groups and synchronise and harmonise operations so that the group functions like one large field.

secs.t: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

x: NCDC
promotes cooperative-sector FPOs, with a target of 1,100 FPOs through Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS).
The scheme provides for one FPO per block and promotes linkage with One District One Product (ODOP) and ONDC.
Andhra Pradesh reported 455 registered FPOs, 99 seed licences, 97 fertiliser licences, 98 pesticide licences and 207 FPOs on ONDC.

secs.t: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

x: e-Kisan Upaj Nidhi, a WDRA digital gateway, was launched on
4 March 2024
CWC was established on 2 March 1957 under the
Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956
The plan converges eight schemes, including the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund and Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure scheme, to create PACS-level facilities.
The effective interest falls to 1% through the revised AMI support combined with 3% AIF subvention and NABARD refinance.

secs.t: Cooperative marketing - NAFED, apex cooperative, State marketing federations

x: NAFED is the
apex agricultural cooperative marketing body
and was set up in 1958.
From 2024-25, procurement under the Price Support Scheme is permitted up to
of production.
AP DCMS recorded a 2025 turnover of ₹13,391.12 lakh and a profit of ₹720.29 lakh.
PM-AASHA's Price Support Scheme procures
pulses, oilseeds and copra
at MSP through NAFED and NCCF.

secs.t: Problems - intermediaries, price spread, distress sale, poor storage, market density

x: Middlemen and brokers can raise consumer prices and add red tape to the marketing process.
About
of built storage lies idle, which contributes to distress sale by limiting usable storage access.
The National Commission on Farmers suggested a regulated market within about
5 km
of farmers.

secs.t: Farmer's share in consumer rupee - price spread studies

x: Price spread measures the difference between the consumer price and farmer's price, reflecting
marketing margins and the share of middlemen

secs.t: Operation Greens - announcing budget, TOP to TOTAL, subsidy pattern

x: Operation Greens initially covered
Tomato, Onion and Potato
, commonly referred to as TOP.
Tomato, onion and potato are grown seasonally and regionally but are consumed throughout the year, creating price fluctuations.
Operation Greens uses FPOs, agri-logistics, processing and professional management to address price volatility; abolition of all agricultural markets is not an objective stated for the scheme.

secs.t: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund - size, interest subvention, eligible projects

x: The AIF is a
₹1 lakh crore
medium- and long-term debt-financing facility launched in 2020 for post-harvest infrastructure and community farming assets.
Eligible AIF projects include cold stores, custom hiring centres, sorting and grading units, warehouses, processing units and supply chains.
Custom hiring centres
were the largest sanctioned category under the AIF, numbering 32,560 projects.

secs.t: Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs) and rural haats

x: The Union Budget 2018-19 announced the upgrading of 22,000 rural haats into Gramin Agricultural Markets.
GrAMs were announced in the Union Budget 2018-19, were proposed to be exempt from APMC regulation and were to be linked with e-NAM.
Rythu Bazars were introduced in 1999, the GrAM announcement was made in 2018-19, AIF was launched in 2020, and e-NAM completed ten years in April 2026.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Operation Greens and PM-AASHA
complement e-NAM as components of the price-realisation toolkit.
Operation Greens initially focused on
Tomato, Onion and Potato
, commonly referred to as TOP.
NAFED and NCCF
undertook discounted sales during the onion price spike.
The 2020 repeal left agricultural marketing reform to
the States
, reflecting the continuing debate between APMC monopoly and farmer choice.

rows.title: Minimum Support Price - mechanism, CACP, crops covered, procurement, criticism; PM-AASHA
sub: Group-II M2-A-50: Agricultural pricing and policy - MSP, CACP and the price policy debate

secs.t: MSP mechanism - approving authority, recommending body, cost concepts (A2, A2+FL, C2)

x: Exam angle: "MSP = 1.5 × C2" is the trap; the actual formula is 1.5 × A2+FL.
When the market price falls below MSP, government agencies procure the stock offered, providing a safeguard against distress sales.
A2 covers paid-out costs; A2+FL adds the imputed value of family labour; C2 further adds rent on owned land and interest on fixed capital.
The current policy fixes MSP at least 1.5 times
A2+FL
, representing a 50 per cent return over that cost concept.
The MSP hikes were ₹254 for groundnut, ₹380 for soyabean, ₹622 for sunflower seed and ₹500 for sesamum.

secs.t: PM-AASHA - components (PSS, PDPS, PPSS), target group, financial outlay

x: PM-AASHA seeks to make MSP reach farmers, including small and marginal farmers.
The Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (
PDPS
) makes a cash payment equal to the gap between MSP and the market price, mainly for oilseeds, without physical purchase.
PPSS was part of the original 2018 design as a pilot in which private stockists procured oilseeds at MSP.
MIS covers specified perishables not covered under MSP, including
onion
, tomato, apple, chillies, grapes and garlic.
The pulses mission promises 100% procurement at MSP for four years for
tur, urad and masoor
through NAFED and NCCF under PSS.
PSS procured
61.87 lakh metric tonnes
of oilseeds, pulses and copra during 2024-25.

secs.t: MSP hike trend - kharif and rabi MSP for paddy and wheat by year

x: The common paddy MSP for Kharif 2025-26 was
₹2,369 per quintal
. ₹2,441 was the common paddy MSP for Kharif 2026-27.
All three statements are correct: common paddy was fixed at ₹2,441, Grade A at ₹2,461, and the common variety received a ₹72 increase.
Cotton MSP was ₹8,267 per quintal for medium staple and ₹8,667 per quintal for long staple cotton.

secs.t: Crops covered - mandated crops list, kharif/rabi/commercial split

x: The stated split is 14 kharif crops, 6 rabi crops and 2 commercial crops, totalling 22 mandated crops.
The seven cereals are
paddy, wheat, maize, jowar, bajra, ragi and barley
Potato
is not among the mandated MSP crops and falls under the category of perishables addressed through MIS.
Cotton, sugarcane, tobacco and oilseeds
are classified as cash or commercial crops grown mainly for sale.

secs.t: Sugarcane pricing - FRP, Statutory Minimum Price vs State Advised Price

x: FRP is fixed under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
FRP replaced the Statutory Minimum Price from the sugar season
The measure concerned duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar, and FRP was raised by ₹10 per quintal for 2026–27.

secs.t: Procurement - open-ended vs limited procurement crops, decentralised procurement states, AP paddy procurement system

x: FCI and State agencies procure all wheat and paddy that meets specifications at MSP, making procurement effectively open-ended.
The prescribed window for DBT to farmers in the Andhra Pradesh paddy procurement system is
48 hours
DCMS societies participate in paddy procurement to ensure that farmers actually obtain the MSP.
More than 35 million tonnes of wheat were procured during RMS 2026–27, exceeding the 34.5 million tonne target.

secs.t: Price support beyond MSP - Price Stabilisation Fund, state MSP for fruits and vegetables

x: The Price Stabilisation Fund was set up in 2014–15 to hold buffers of onion, potato and pulses and release them to curb sharp price increases.
MIS provides price support for perishable commodities that are not covered under MSP.
Cotton is procured through the
Cotton Corporation of India
(CCI), unlike wheat and paddy, which are procured by FCI and State agencies.

secs.t: CACP - year set up, earlier name, factors considered

x: Exam angle: "recommending vs approving body" (CACP vs CCEA) is the favourite trap.
CACP recommends FRP, but the
Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs
fixes it.
The CACP considers all the listed factors, along with the likely effect on consumers and the objective of providing a minimum 50 per cent margin over cost.

secs.t: Criticism - regional and crop bias, Shanta Kumar Committee findings, legal guarantee demand

x: The Shanta Kumar Committee estimated that only about
6 per cent
of farmers sell their produce to procurement agencies at MSP.
MSP is announced for these crops, but actual procurement is limited, making the support largely symbolic in practice.
Economists warn that a legal MSP guarantee could distort trade, reinforce monoculture and create WTO-related concerns.

secs.t: Phases of Indian agricultural development

x: HYV wheat and rice marked the Green Revolution phase; PDS distribution at issue price marked the price-support and procurement phase; and PM-KISAN belongs to the post-1991 reform phase.
The Pre-Green Revolution phase began in 1950, APC and FCI were set up in 1965, the Wheat Revolution stamp was released in July 1968, and India became a WTO member in 1995.

secs.t: MSP debate - legal guarantee, Swaminathan formula, concentration, export bans

x: Economists have warned that a legal MSP may distort trade, encourage monoculture and breach WTO norms.

The suggested approaches include wider procurement, price-deficiency payments through PM-AASHA, direct income support through PM-KISAN, decentralised procurement and digital procurement through e-NAM.
The Economic Survey 2025–26 suggested using procurement-efficiency savings to fund
voluntary crop diversification away from water-guzzling rice and wheat

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Kharif 2026–27 MSPs were notified in May 2026, with paddy MSP fixed at ₹2,441 per quintal.
Wheat procurement was reported to have crossed 35 million tonnes, constituting a record figure.
The protests in Andhra Pradesh sought MSP procurement for maize, pulses, cotton and tomato.
The central debates concern the appropriate cost base, legal enforceability, WTO constraints, fiscal cost and regional imbalance in procurement.

rows.title: Public distribution, procurement and buffer-stocking; food subsidy and FCI reform
sub: Group-II M2-A-51: Procurement, issue price and public distribution; food subsidy and FCI reform

secs.t: FCI - year set up, Act, recommending committee, missions and functions, digital systems (OSM, Anna Darpan)

x: FCI is the nodal agency for procuring wheat and paddy under price support, with State agencies functioning alongside it.
All four statements describe the missions of FCI: procurement at MSP, storage and distribution, maintenance of operational and buffer stocks, and access to foodgrains through TPDS.
SARTHAK-PDS
digitally tracks grain from procurement to the Fair Price Shop and monitors stocks in real time to help prevent leakage.
Rising operating costs, excess stocks and wastage, and falling issue-price earnings are identified challenges of FCI.

secs.t: TPDS evolution - PDS, RPDS, TPDS, AAY (launch sequence), leakage estimates, reforms (ePoS, Aadhaar seeding, DBT)

x: ONORC permits a migrant to lift the full or partial entitlement at an ePoS-enabled fair price shop after biometric or Aadhaar authentication; the family can draw the balance at the original location.
SARTHAK-PDS is an umbrella scheme covering SMART-PDS, intra-state movement and FPS dealer margins, with AI/ML, blockchain and NLP proposed for monitoring and grievances.
The Andhra Pradesh e-PDS system has 1.44 crore rice cards, 100 per cent Aadhaar seeding, 29,783 FPS serving 4.3 crore people, and biometric transactions with in-State portability.
The recommendations included reviewing DBT against physical supply before expansion, raising FPS margins and linking ePoS devices to e-weighing scales.
PDS-supplied fortified rice contains
iron, vitamin B12 and folic acid
and is intended to combat micronutrient deficiency.
PMGKAY relates to the COVID-19 period and the subsequent five-year NFSA grain provision, while Annapurna and Antyodaya have the stated entitlements.

secs.t: Price concepts - MSP vs procurement price vs issue price, components of FCI economic cost

x: States fix the retail price at Fair Price Shops and perform the operational role in the PDS.
The pooled cost of grain, consisting of MSP plus State bonuses, is about
two-thirds
of the economic cost.
Food subsidy equals the economic cost minus the Central Issue Price.
Food subsidy is reimbursed to FCI and, in DCP States, to the concerned State governments.
The procurement price was earlier announced separately at harvest; subsequently, it was merged into one price.

secs.t: Food management objectives - procurement, buffer stocks, distribution, PDS objectives

x: The Department works through procurement, storage and movement, public distribution, and maintenance of buffer stocks.
All three statements describe PDS objectives: minimum affordable availability for low-income groups, equitable distribution and control of price swings.
Both statements are true, and the listed domestic food-management functions explain why export of foodgrains is not treated as an objective of food management.

secs.t: Storage - CAP storage, silos under PPP, Indian Grain Storage Management and Research Institute, warehouse capacity

x: Steel silos under PPP are intended to
modernise bulk storage of foodgrains
The plan includes silos of 50, 100 and 200 MT, procurement centres, FPS, processing units and custom hiring centres.
PACS are selected by District Cooperative Development Committees, while the National Cooperative Development Corporation implements the plan.
The Indian Grain Storage Management and Research Institute is located at
Hapur

secs.t: Food subsidy - Union Budget allocation trend, CAG findings, NSSF loans issue

x: Fortified-rice supply under PMGKAY is scheduled to run until
December 2028
NSSF loans met FCI's funding gap, kept the subsidy off-budget, and the Budget 2021-22 brought it back into the budget.
The total food subsidy declined from ₹2,72,501.70 crore in 2022-23 to ₹2,11,393.85 crore in 2023-24 and ₹1,99,500.00 crore in 2024-25.

secs.t: Shanta Kumar High Level Committee - FCI restructuring recommendations

x: The High Level Committee on FCI restructuring was chaired by
Shanta Kumar
The committee proposed that procurement in surplus States such as Punjab, Haryana and Andhra Pradesh be handled by those States, allowing FCI to focus on the
eastern States
The committee proposed reducing NFSA coverage from 67% to about
40% of the population

secs.t: Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) and Decentralised Procurement scheme - purpose, adopting states

x: Under OMSS(D), FCI sells wheat and rice from the Central Pool at predetermined prices to moderate market prices.
Under DCP, designated States procure, store and distribute grain for TPDS themselves.
The stated objectives are to assure MSP, provide grain for weaker sections under PMGKAY and intervene in markets to moderate prices.

secs.t: AP PDS network - fair price shops, MDU door delivery, rice cards

x: Mee Mart is an initiative of the AP Civil Supplies Department with NCCF to modernise FPSs; its first outlet opened at Lalupuram near Guntur.
Mee Mart proposed 1,000 outlets, of which 553 were ready; outlets were to stock over 250 products and be linked to the Digital Rupee (CBDC).
The AP e-PDS system includes 100% Aadhaar seeding of rice cards, biometric transactions and intra-state portability.

secs.t: PMGKAY and leakages - free foodgrain extension, NSS leakage estimates

x: The COVID-era PMGKAY provided 5 kg of foodgrain per month free of cost in addition to the regular NFSA entitlements.
Aadhaar-enabled e-PoS devices and ONORC are associated with reducing PDS leakages.
The free distribution of NFSA foodgrains under PMGKAY, beginning on 1 January 2023, has been extended up to
31 December 2028

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The sequence is: the LENS proposal in September 2025, SARTHAK-PDS approval on 28 May 2026, Mee Mart launch in July 2026, and the cooperative grain storage plan on 6 September 2026.
The correct matching is Fair Price Shops—29,796; beneficiaries—1.48 crore; Mobile Distribution Units—9,260; and rice—fortified.
All three are recognised issues in the PDS debate: rising economic cost, leakage, and the choice between DBT and distribution of grain in kind.

rows.title: Malnutrition and food security - indicators, POSHAN Abhiyaan, fortification, PM POSHAN

secs.t: Malnutrition indicators - stunting, wasting, underweight, undernutrition vs overnutrition, anaemia, NFHS India and AP

x: Stunting, measured as low height-for-age, reflects
chronic undernutrition
Wasting is low
weight-for-height
and is an indicator of acute undernutrition.
Undernutrition encompasses protein-energy malnutrition, micronutrient deficiency, stunting, wasting and underweight, whereas overnutrition includes overweight and obesity.
The coexistence of undernutrition and overnutrition in the same population is called the
double burden of malnutrition

secs.t: National nutrition programmes - launch year and ministry

x: ICDS was launched on
2 October 1975
during the Fifth Five-Year Plan.
The National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme (
NIDDCP
) is administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
The idea of the Mid-Day Meal initiative started in
Tamil Nadu
; the national programme was launched on 15 August 1995.
MAA is a
breastfeeding
promotion programme launched in 2016.

secs.t: Causes of malnutrition burden - diet, food insecurity, water and sanitation

x: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity
are identified as the biggest factors contributing to the malnutrition burden.
Malnutrition is multi-causal, and unsafe water and sanitation can lead to disease and nutrient loss; therefore nutrition measures need to be combined with WASH interventions.

secs.t: POSHAN Abhiyaan / Mission Poshan 2.0 and Anaemia Mukt Bharat - objectives, targets, interventions, ICDS services

x: POSHAN Abhiyaan aims to achieve a
Suposhit Bharat
through convergence, technology and a Jan Andolan.
POSHAN Abhiyaan targets reductions in stunting, undernutrition or underweight, anaemia and low birth weight.
Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation, abbreviated
WIFS
, covers adolescents aged 10–19 years under Anaemia Mukt Bharat interventions.
Anaemia Mukt Bharat uses IFA tablets, deworming and outreach directed at six target groups.

secs.t: State-wise malnutrition - highest-burden states

x: Uttar Pradesh
had the highest reported stunting burden at 48.8%; Jharkhand, Assam, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh were each above 42%.
Goa, Sikkim, Manipur, Himachal Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
were identified as better performers.

secs.t: Food fortification - fortified rice distribution phases, FSSAI logo, double-fortified salt

x: Phase I in 2021-22 covered ICDS and PM POSHAN, Phase II in 2022-23 added 291 districts under TPDS, and Phase III in 2023-24 covered all districts under TPDS.
The correct sequence is the 2019 pilot, Phase I in 2021-22, Phase II in 2022-23 and Phase III in 2023-24.
Supply continues under PMGKAY/OWS up to
December 2028

secs.t: AP nutrition schemes - YSR Sampoorna Poshana / Gorumudda, Anna Amrutha Hastham

x: The plain-area Bala Sanjeevani package provides take-home ration comprising rice, dal, oil, ragi and chikki, together with a Rs.250 monthly nutrition kit for pregnant and lactating women.
The package includes 3 kg rice, 1 kg dal, 500 ml oil and a monthly nutrition kit worth ₹250, along with ragi flour, chikki, jaggery and dates.
Children aged 36–72 months receive
a hot cooked meal, one egg and 100 ml milk
under the plain-area package.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The cereal-centric nature of the PDS is criticised for not adequately ensuring dietary diversity.
The cited policy debate concerns the ban on HFSS foods within
50 metres
of schools.

All three statements reflect the Andhra Pradesh-specific aspects: Bala Sanjeevani packages, adolescent-girl coverage in three districts and continuing last-mile gaps in tribal hamlets and Rayalaseema.

rows.title: Allied sectors - horticulture, animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries (PMMSY), agro-processing
sub: Group-II M2-A-54: Allied sectors - horticulture, dairy, poultry and fisheries

secs.t: Fisheries - PMMSY and PM-MKSSY, MPEDA, fisheries growth rate, AP rank in aquaculture and shrimp

x: The
National Fisheries Development Board
(NFDB) handles training and capacity building under PMMSY.
PM-MKSSY, or Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana, is a Central Sector sub-scheme under PMMSY aimed at formalising the fisheries sector and supporting fisheries micro-enterprises.
FIDF supports fisheries and aquaculture infrastructure, particularly
fishing harbours and landing centres
Fisheries
has been the fastest-growing allied sub-sector, recording growth of about 9.08% annually since 2014-15.
Fish production rose by about 103%, from 95.79 lakh tonnes in 2013-14 to approximately
195 lakh tonnes

secs.t: Horticulture - MIDH and NHM, fruit largest producer state, export mango varieties, Indo-Israel CoEs in AP

x: Horticulture output was 367.72 million tonnes, above foodgrain output of 357.73 million tonnes, contributed about 33% of agricultural GVA and used under 14% of cropped area.
Andhra Pradesh
horticulture covers 46.43 lakh acres and produces 406.38 lakh metric tonnes
The identified activities include banana, oil palm, cashew, coconut and Araku coffee.
Eight refrigerated banana trains from Tadipatri transported
to the Gulf in three months.

secs.t: Food processing - Operation Greens, PM Kisan SAMPADA, mega food parks, processed food export share, PMFME and ODOP

x: The scope of Operation Greens was later widened from TOP crops to all fruits and vegetables.
PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana is the umbrella scheme of the
Ministry of Food Processing Industries
Mega Food Parks use a cluster approach that links farms to processing facilities and then to markets.
PMFME formalises micro food-processing units under the
One District One Product
(ODOP) approach.

secs.t: Animal husbandry - Credit Guarantee Scheme for Livestock, Rashtriya Gokul Mission, NLM, Livestock Census

x: The National Livestock Mission covers livestock productivity, feed and fodder, health and entrepreneurship;
urban metro-rail infrastructure
is unrelated.
The 10,606 Rythu Seva Kendralu, formerly RBKs, function as
one-stop livestock platforms
Rashtriya Gokul Mission concerns indigenous bovine breeds; NLM covers productivity and related areas; AHIDF is the infrastructure fund; LHDCP uses prophylactic vaccination.

secs.t: Sericulture and apiculture - revolution names, leading state by silk type, AP sericulture districts

x: India is the only country that commercially produces all five known varieties of silk—mulberry, tropical tasar, oak tasar, eri and muga.
The principal sericulture belt lies in Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur, particularly around Hindupur, and in Chittoor.
Andhra Pradesh
is the leading state in egg production, contributing about 18.37 per cent, followed by Tamil Nadu, Telangana, West Bengal and Karnataka.

secs.t: Dairy - Operation Flood, NDDB, India's rank, top states, per capita availability

x: Operation Flood built a national milk grid, followed the Amul cooperative model and helped India become the world's largest milk producer.
The current per capita availability of milk is
471 grams per day
; 394 grams is an older figure.
Andhra Pradesh ranked seventh with 139.94 lakh MT, while Chittoor is the leading dairy district and faced the stated fodder and rainfall crisis.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The five-year review highlighted in September 2026 concerned the
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana
(PMMSY).
NABARD’s 2026-27 plan allocated
₹21,098 crore
to fisheries in Andhra Pradesh.
The allocation for animal husbandry under NABARD’s 2026-27 plan was
₹34,972 crore
Andhra Pradesh ranks first in eggs, second in sheep numbers, second in poultry numbers and first in oil palm.

rows.title: Indian industry - structure, growth and contribution; IIP; public sector role and performance
sub: Group-II M2-A-55: Industrial development in India - patterns, growth and structural problems
Group-II M2-A-58: Public sector enterprises - role, performance and reform

secs.t: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy

x: The ratna categories grant high-performing CPSEs
greater financial and operational autonomy
, including the ability to invest, form joint ventures and compete globally with fewer approvals.
Maharatna eligibility requires existing Navratna status, the scheme was introduced in 2009 with first grants in 2010, and investment autonomy extends up to ₹5,000 crore in one project.

All four statements correctly state the conditions listed for Navratna eligibility: introduction in 1997, Miniratna-I and Schedule 'A' status, the MoU performance requirement and the six-parameter score of 60 or more.

Maharatna corresponds to ₹5,000 crore in one project; Navratna to ₹1,000 crore or 15% of net worth; Miniratna-I to ₹500 crore or equal to net worth; and Miniratna-II to ₹300 crore or 50% of net worth.
Miniratna-I requires profits in the last three consecutive years, pre-tax profit of at least ₹30 crore in at least one year and positive net worth.
HAL is a Maharatna CPSE, while Bharat Electronics Limited is a Navratna CPSE; BEL received Navratna status in June 2007.

secs.t: Eight core industries - list, combined weight in IIP, highest weight sector

x: The eight core industries together accounted for
40.27 per cent
of the IIP in the old 2011-12 series.
In the old series, refinery products had the highest weight at 28.04 per cent, followed by electricity at 19.85 per cent, steel at 17.92 per cent and coal at 10.33 per cent.
Iron ore
drove the June 2026 ICI growth, recording an increase of 43.9 per cent.
The IIP measures short-term changes in industrial production relative to a base period and covers mining, manufacturing and electricity.
The IIP use-based groups include primary goods, capital goods, intermediate goods, infrastructure and construction goods, consumer durables and consumer non-durables.
The eight core industries accounted for
of the IIP weight under the old series with base year 2011–12.
The revised series added iron ore, making nine sectors, and removed double-counting in steel and coal.
The tenth IIP revision uses 2022–23 as base year, covers 1,042 products in 463 groups, assigns manufacturing a 76.1% weight, and is compiled by NSO under MoSPI.
The revised IIP weights are manufacturing 76.1%, mining 11.1%, electricity and gas 10.9%, and water supply 2.02%.

secs.t: Industrial structure changes since 1991 - share of industry in GDP, manufacturing vs construction, private sector share

x: After 1991, the services sector gained the most share in GDP.
Industry accounts for approximately
25.3 per cent
of GVA.
The decline in manufacturing's nominal GVA share was attributed to relative price changes.
The public sector contributes about
13–14 per cent
of GDP.
About
57 lakh
jobs were added in organised manufacturing between 2015-16 and 2024-25.
Total employment was reported at approximately
56.2 crore
in Q2 FY26.

secs.t: PSU performance - top profit-making and loss-making CPSEs, Public Enterprises Survey, number of PSUs over time

x: The Department of Public Enterprises assesses CPSE performance through annual MoUs agreed between each CPSE and its ministry.
All three statements are correct: operating CPSEs number more than 250, their combined net profit exceeds ₹3.43 lakh crore, and they employ about 9–10 lakh people.
Operating CPSEs spend over ₹10,800 crore on research and development and about ₹5,000 crore annually on CSR.

secs.t: Evolution of modern industry - first cotton, jute, textile mills and sugar units (chronology)

x: The correct sequence is the cotton mill in 1854, the jute mill in 1855, TISCO in 1907, and tariff protection for sugar in 1932.
The correct order is Bombay Dyeing (1879), Lakshmi Mills (1910), Raymond (1925), and Grasim (1947).
Munagala Raja's textile unit at Vijayawada
, established in June 1906, was the first of its kind in the Madras Presidency.
Sindri Fertilizers, Chittaranjan Locomotives, Integral Coach Factory, HMT, ITI and Hindustan Cables formed part of the early public-sector industrial base.

secs.t: IIP - base year, compiling agency, sectors included and excluded, weights, use-based classification

x: The weights in the new IIP series are derived from the sectoral shares of
Gross Value Added in 2022-23
The use-based categories are primary goods, capital goods, intermediate goods, infrastructure and construction goods, consumer durables and consumer non-durables.
The old IIP manufacturing basket contained 809 items classified into 405 groups.

secs.t: Sector profiles - steel, automobile, pharmaceuticals, PSU foreign collaborations (BHEL)

x: BHEL is a Maharatna CPSE with a dominant share in heavy electrical equipment, including boilers, turbines and transformers.
BHEL's first plant at Bhopal was built with British collaboration, specifically involving AEI.
Hindustan Aircraft, Sindri Fertilizers and Chittaranjan Locomotive were among the early public-sector units.
The Second Plan period, 1956–61, saw the establishment of
Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur
with foreign assistance.
Bhilai was established in 1957, Rourkela and Durgapur in 1959, and Bokaro in 1964.
Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela and Bokaro
are among the listed SAIL plants.

secs.t: Industrial growth phases since independence - phase boundaries and growth rate

x: The sequence is 1951–65 rapid industrialisation, 1965–80 deceleration, the 1980s recovery and 1991 onward liberalisation.
The 1951–65 phase witnessed rapid, public-sector-led heavy industrialisation, with growth of approximately 7–8 per cent.
The period
was marked by deceleration and licence-raj stagnation, with industrial growth of about 4 per cent.
The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 reserved 17 industries for the public sector, while the 1991 policy reduced the number to 8.

secs.t: AP industrial profile - GSVA share of industry, major industrial clusters

x: By December 2024, 10 large and mega industries had been set up in Andhra Pradesh with ₹12,830 crore investment and 11,925 jobs.
The policy targets ₹30 lakh crore investment, 175-plus industrial parks and doubling exports from $20 billion to $40 billion.

secs.t: Structural problems - under-utilisation, concentration, capital intensity, jobless growth

x: Deficient basic infrastructure
is identified as the main cause of capacity under-utilisation, although weak demand also contributes.
Industrial activity is regionally concentrated in
Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
, while eastern and central States lag behind.
Import dependence in electronics, solar panels and APIs and low R&D spending are structural weaknesses.

secs.t: Major industries profile - textiles, steel, auto, pharma

x: Cotton textiles comprise the
mill, powerloom and handloom
segments.
India produced
149.4 million tonnes
of crude steel in 2024 and ranked second after China, which produced 1,005.1 million tonnes.
China led crude steel production in 2024, about 93 per cent of planned ironmaking was coal-based, and coking coal was the main imported input.

secs.t: Phases of industrial growth in the planned era - deceleration, premature deindustrialisation

x: The planned-era sequence is rapid build-up from 1951–65, deceleration from 1965–80, recovery in the 1980s and liberalisation from 1991 onward.
Premature deindustrialisation occurs when manufacturing's share of output or employment peaks at a lower income level than it did in early industrialisers.
Cheap imports after 1991 contributed to
the closure of many small industrial units
, a feature linked with premature deindustrialisation.

secs.t: Growth in number of central PSUs - Public Enterprises Survey

x: The number of Central Public Sector Enterprises increased from 5 at the beginning of the First Plan to 244 by 1990.
The Public Enterprises Survey is presented annually to Parliament, covers CPSEs with over 50 per cent Government of India equity, and excludes departmental undertakings, banks and insurers.
A CPSE is defined as a company or statutory body having not less than 51 per cent Central Government share capital.

secs.t: Role of public sector - commanding heights, infrastructure, regional balance

x: The public sector occupied the commanding heights by entering capital-heavy and long-gestation sectors that private capital was reluctant to undertake.
Bhilai, Rourkela and Bokaro developed as public-sector townships, while Neyveli became associated with NLC and Vizag with RINL-led heavy industry and port development.
RINL helped transform
Visakhapatnam
into a major heavy-industry and port hub.

secs.t: Autonomy and reforms - MoU system, BRPSE, closure of sick units

x: The committees were appointed in 1984, 1993 and 2012 respectively: Arjun Sengupta, Rangarajan and Vijay Kelkar.
The MoU is an annual target-setting agreement, applies to all CPSEs including subsidiaries, and is administered through a High Power Committee.

Arjun Sengupta dealt with PSU autonomy; Rangarajan recommended up to 49% disinvestment; the Disinvestment Commission proposed strategic sales; and Vijay Kelkar addressed fiscal consolidation and faster disinvestment.

secs.t: Department of Public Enterprises and Public Enterprises Selection Board

x: The Department of Public Enterprises is presently under the
Ministry of Finance
DPE evaluates MoUs, classifies CPSEs into four schedules, grants Ratna status and deals with pay and dispute-related policies.
DPE classification of CPSEs into four schedules is linked to the pay structure of their chief executive officers.
PESB selects board-level executives for Central Public Sector Enterprises.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Iron ore
was added as the ninth and newest industry in the revised core-industries index.
Andhra Pradesh has 123 State Level Public Enterprises, and APSRTC recorded a profit of Rs 1,524.32 crore in 2024-25.
The 2026 amendment requires every CPSE to settle MSME invoices on the Trade Receivables Discounting System, or
TReDS
