rows.title: Primary and secondary markets; stock exchanges, indices, IPO process, derivatives

secs.t: Stock indices - exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

x: Exam angle: "Free-float market capitalisation weighted" - answer NIFTY or SENSEX (both use it).
SENSEX comprises 30 blue-chip stocks listed on the BSE and is calculated using the free-float market capitalisation method.
NIFTY 50 consists of 50 stocks from 13 sectors, uses free-float market capitalisation and was launched in 1996.
NIFTY is managed by IISL, now known as NSE Indices Ltd., a subsidiary of NSE.

secs.t: Stock exchanges - year, location, promoters

x: The BSE was promoted by the
Native Share and Stock Brokers’ Association
The
Metropolitan Stock Exchange
began in Mumbai in 2008 as MCX-SX and was renamed in 2015.
Exchanges in an IFSC are regulated by the International Financial Services Centres Authority (
IFSCA
BSE is Asia’s oldest exchange, NSDL was India’s first depository, and India INX was India’s first international exchange.

secs.t: Primary vs secondary market

x: Primary-market issues include IPOs, FPOs, rights issues and private placements, with funds going to the issuer.
In an offer for sale, existing owners sell their holdings and receive the proceeds; proceeds from a fresh issue go to the firm.
Promoters, PE and VC investors accounted for 84% of OFS proceeds, or ₹10,696 crore, in the stated period.

secs.t: Market participants and terms

x: A
stag
applies for IPO shares with the intention of selling them soon after listing.
In short selling, borrowed shares are sold first and are bought back later, ideally at a lower price.
A circuit breaker temporarily halts trading when the movement in an index or stock exceeds specified limits.
Sweat equity is issued to employees or directors for
know-how or services
, often at a discount.

secs.t: Investor claims and instruments

x: Convertible bonds or debentures are debt instruments that may carry an equity-conversion feature, making them hybrids of
debt and equity
Asset tokenisation digitally represents ownership or claims such as bonds, fund units and receivables on a programmable ledger.
Asset tokenisation can enable faster settlement, make assets pledgeable and improve access to credit for MSMEs.

secs.t: Derivatives - types; India's options market

x: A futures contract creates an obligation to buy or sell at a fixed future price.
Swaps involve exchanging cash flows; a common example is exchanging fixed-rate interest payments for floating-rate payments.
The Forward Markets Commission merged with SEBI in 2015, bringing commodity derivatives under SEBI’s regulatory framework.
Budget 2026–27 raised the STT on futures from

secs.t: IPO process - book building, anchors, ASBA, SME IPO, listing

x: In book building, investors submit bids within a price band extending from the floor price to the cap price.
Anchor investors are QIBs who bid before the issue opens for general subscription, and their investment is subject to a lock-in.
SME IPOs are listed on dedicated SME platforms, notably
BSE SME and NSE Emerge

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The STT hike on F&O in Budget 2026–27 was aimed at curbing speculation.
SEBI is still studying losses associated with short-tenure options
The number of unique investors crossed
12 crore
according to the Economic Survey 2025–26.

rows.title: SEBI - establishment, powers and functions; investor protection and market regulation

secs.t: SEBI - establishment, statutory basis, HQ, chairperson, role

x: Tuhin Kanta Pandey
took charge as SEBI Chairperson in 2025.
The stated composition includes the Chairperson, two ministry representatives, one RBI representative and five other members, with at least three of the latter being whole-time members.
SEBI undertakes registration, fee collection, investor education and inspection or audit;
issuing currency notes
is not its function.

secs.t: SEBI regulatory scope - entities regulated

x: Stock exchanges
, clearing corporations and depositories are identified as Market Infrastructure Institutions regulated by SEBI.
Stock brokers, merchant bankers, registrars and investment advisers are among the listed SEBI-regulated intermediaries;
commercial tax officers
are not.
Online Bond Platform Providers are referred to as
OBPPs
and fall within the securities-market regulatory discussion.

secs.t: Recent SEBI reforms - T+0, ESG/BRSR, SME IPOs, finfluencers

x: T+0 is an optional same-day settlement mechanism alongside T+1, intended to improve liquidity, efficiency and risk management, including lower settlement and counterparty risk.
The assessment identifies the SME market as under-scaled and lacking
intermediaries
; it does not state that the market lacks regulation altogether.
SEBI's position is that
regulated entities cannot work with unregistered finfluencers
; stock tips and return claims may constitute advisory work.

secs.t: SEBI-appointed committees - subject

x: Uday Kotak dealt with corporate governance and board independence; K. M. Birla led to Clause 49; T. K. Viswanathan examined fair market conduct; Sodhi dealt with principle-based insider-trading regulations.
The 2017 T. K. Viswanathan Committee addressed
fair market conduct, including insider trading
, and proposed two codes for listed companies and intermediaries.

secs.t: Scams that shaped regulation

x: The Ketan Parekh scam was associated with the ending of badla and the move to rolling settlement.
The Satyam scandal led to audit and board reforms in the Companies Act, 2013 and the establishment of the National Financial Reporting Authority.
The Sahara OFCD matter was associated with limiting private placement to 50 investors and recognising SEBI's authority over deemed public issues.

secs.t: SEBI powers - quasi-legislative, quasi-judicial, investigation; SAT

x: Passing orders, imposing penalties and ordering disgorgement
are examples of SEBI's quasi-judicial functions.
Inspection, search and seizure are
investigative powers
exercised by SEBI.
SAT hears appeals against SEBI and exchanges, and a further appeal from SAT lies to the Supreme Court.
The settlement total was
₹1,492 crore
, comprising ₹1,224 crore and ₹268 crore.

secs.t: Investor protection - IEPF, SCORES, insider trading and PFUTP

x: The IEPF Authority promotes investor awareness and facilitates the refund of unclaimed dividends and shares.
The 2025 PIT amendment widened UPSI, while PFUTP Regulations address fraudulent and unfair trade practices; both support investor protection.
The initiatives include a new UPI address structure for intermediaries, SEBI Check, the SEBI vs SCAM campaign, and Mission Jagrook, which was launched on SEBI’s 38th Foundation Day.

secs.t: Commodity market regulation - Forward Markets Commission

x: The Forward Markets Commission was merged with SEBI in 2015.
Following the merger, brokers, NSE, BSE, FPIs and Category III AIFs were allowed in commodity derivatives.

The Forward Contracts (Regulation) Act dates to 1952, the FMC-SEBI merger occurred in 2015, and the campaign and Mission Jagrook are later initiatives, with Mission Jagrook linked to SEBI’s 38th Foundation Day.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The ₹1,492 crore SEBI-NSE settlement closed
the co-location case
The settlement was reported on 4
September 2026
as closing the co-location case.
The
AP MSME Development Corporation and NSE
jointly conducted the SME IPO awareness programme in Vijayawada.
The reported figures for December 2025 were
21.6 crore demat accounts and 5.9 crore mutual fund investors

rows.title: Financial instabilities - crises, systemic risk, shadow banking, macroprudential regulation

secs.t: Financial crises and scams - cause and India impact

x: The crisis caused FPI outflows and a market crash in India, followed by Basel III measures and the setting up of FSDC in December 2010 under the G-20 push.
Defaults by IL&FS, an infrastructure NBFC, triggered an NBFC liquidity crisis and led to tighter NBFC regulations.
Prashant Kumar
served as Yes Bank's CEO from March 2020 and was replaced by Vinay Tonse on 6 April 2026.

secs.t: FSDC and stability bodies

x: FSDC monitors macroprudential supervision and inter-regulatory coordination, and its sub-committee is chaired by the RBI Governor.
The RBI publishes the Financial Stability Report half-yearly, generally in June and December.
The December 2025 FSR discussed external and geopolitical risks and reported that macro stress tests showed banks and NBFCs to be resilient.

secs.t: Sub-prime crisis - teaser loans, defaults, securitisation

x: Teaser loans offer a low fixed rate in the early years and a higher rate later, creating future default risk for banks.
The sequence was weak-borrower lending, securitisation and sale of mortgage-backed securities, rising rates, home-loan defaults and failure of US banks.
A Credit Default Swap is an insurance-like derivative on bonds; the seller pays when default occurs, and the contract carries counterparty risk.

secs.t: Shadow banking - NBFC liquidity crisis, ALM mismatch

x: NBFCs are registered under the Companies Act and cannot take demand deposits, issue cheques or join the payment system; their deposits are not covered by DICGC.
NBFCs borrowed through short-term commercial paper and mutual fund money while lending for long-term infrastructure and housing, creating an asset-liability mismatch exposed by the IL&FS default.

secs.t: Systemic risk - D-SIBs, G-SIBs, too-big-to-fail

x: RBI-designated D-SIBs include SBI, ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank, which face an extra CET1 surcharge.
LIC, GIC Re and New India Assurance are D-SIIs identified by IRDAI.
A too-big-to-fail institution is systemically important because its failure could disrupt the whole system; consequently, it receives closer supervision and higher governance norms.

secs.t: Cooperative bank failures - PMC Bank, BR Amendment 2020

x: PMC Bank had hidden exposure to one realty group, while dual control by the RBI and state Registrars weakened oversight.
The 2020 amendment brought
urban and multi-state cooperative banks
under RBI supervision.
Deposit insurance is available up to
₹5 lakh per depositor per bank
through DICGC.

secs.t: Stress tests and early warning - RBI supervisory framework

x: PCA monitors capital, asset quality including NPAs, and leverage, and may impose restrictions on lending, branches and dividends.
PCA can impose restrictions on lending, branch expansion and dividend payments, depending on the bank's weakness.
GNPA was 2.2 per cent and NNPA 0.5 per cent in September 2025, while CRAR was 17.3 per cent in March 2025; the GNPA and NNPA levels were multi-decadal lows.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The June 2026 Financial Stability Report flagged risks associated with unsecured lending through fintech platforms.
The report highlighted risks arising from fintech
unsecured lending
, rather than from secured housing finance or the other listed areas.
The RBI regulates banks and NBFCs, IRDAI regulates insurers, and the Financial Stability and Development Council coordinates among the financial regulators.

rows.title: Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI, WPI, core inflation), effects and control measures
sub: Group-II M2-A-29: Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI and WPI) and remedies

secs.t: Inflation types - definition and causes

x: The CFPI classification contains 10 sub-groups: cereals, meat and fish, egg, milk, oils, fruits, vegetables, pulses, sugar and spices.
Cost-push inflation
results from increasing input costs such as wages, raw materials and fuel, which put upward pressure on prices through the supply side.
Erratic monsoons, El Niño, crude oil price increases and rupee depreciation can create supply-side inflationary pressures.
The West Asia conflict in 2026 pushed up fuel and input costs, thereby creating cost-push inflationary pressure.
Skewflation
describes a situation in which prices rise sharply in a few items while prices of other items remain stable and overall inflation is low.
Bottleneck inflation
is caused by structural supply constraints, including poor farm productivity and inadequate storage and distribution.
Creeping inflation is below 3 per cent, walking or trotting inflation is around 3–10 per cent, and galloping inflation precedes hyperinflation in severity.
The stated assessment was that
Bharat Atta helped ease cereal prices
, thereby moderating cereal-price pressure.

secs.t: Effects of inflation and deflation

x: Debtors repay loans in money with lower real value, while holders of real assets may benefit from rising prices.
Food inflation is regressive because poorer households spend a larger share of their income on food.
Inflation creates menu costs, shoeleather costs and uncertainty that can discourage investment.
During deflation, consumers may postpone purchases, causing profits and production to fall; unemployment can rise and the real burden of debt increases.

secs.t: Price indices - publisher, base year, weights

x: National income and GDP estimates are published by the NSO, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation; the table also identifies the earlier CSO association.
IIP is published by NSO, released monthly on the 28th, and draws on 14 source agencies.
The CPI for Rural, Urban and Combined sectors is published by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
The new CPI basket contains 358 items, comprising 308 goods and 50 services.
Rural house rent and 12 online platforms
were added to the new CPI series.
The current WPI series has
as its base year and replaced the earlier 2011-12 base.
The
GDP deflator
is the broadest measure because it covers all goods and services produced in the economy, including services.
GDP deflator equals nominal GDP divided by real GDP, multiplied by 100.
An increase in the GDP deflator reflects a rise in the general price level and therefore reduces the
purchasing power of money

secs.t: Index used for measuring inflation - headline measure and the switch

x: The sequence is CPI adoption in April 2014, the February 2015 Monetary Policy Framework Agreement, the 2016 RBI Act amendment and the first invocation in 2022.
Section 45ZN requires a report when the inflation band is breached for three consecutive quarters.
The debate is whether policy should target headline or core inflation; core inflation is considered stickier and more responsive to policy.

secs.t: Relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation

x: In May 2026, food inflation was 4.85%, headline inflation was 3.93% and core inflation was 3.73%, giving the order
Food > Headline > Core
Headline CPI inflation reached 4.38% in June 2026, marking the first breach of the 4% target.
In July 2026, headline CPI inflation was 4.45%, rural food inflation was 5.79%, and core inflation was below 3% when precious metals were excluded.
WPI inflation was 9.87% in June and 9.78% in July 2026, far above CPI inflation mainly because of fuel costs associated with the West Asia conflict.

secs.t: Phillips curve - inflation-unemployment trade-off

x: A.W. Phillips
established the inverse relationship between unemployment and wage inflation in 1958.
The long-run vertical curve indicates that there is no lasting trade-off between inflation and unemployment, making statement 3 false.
India’s relatively flat Phillips curve is linked to the large informal workforce, estimated at about 92%, whose weak wage-bargaining power prevents wages from responding strongly to output changes.

secs.t: Control measures - monetary, fiscal, supply-side

x: OMSS sales by FCI, PSF buffers and subsidised Bharat-branded food sales are supply-side responses to food inflation.
NCCF and NAFED
released 47,786 metric tonnes of onion from the PSF buffer up to 8 October 2025.
Bharat Chana Dal was introduced in July 2023, the onion export ban was lifted on 4 May 2024, and the MEP was removed with duty reduced on 13 September 2024.
The repo rate influences aggregate demand and liquidity, but it cannot directly remove supply shocks such as sudden increases in onion or crude-oil prices.

secs.t: Committees on price indices

x: The Urjit Patel Committee recommended a monetary policy framework centred on CPI as the nominal anchor and flexible inflation targeting.
Urjit Patel was associated with the monetary policy framework; Abhijit Sen with the 2004–05 WPI revision; and Saumitra Chaudhuri with the 2011–12 WPI revision.

secs.t: Inflation-indexed bonds

x: In inflation-indexed bonds, the principal and/or interest payments are linked to an inflation index, protecting the investor’s real return.
Inflation-indexed bonds provide a real-return hedge, can widen the investor base and may shift savings from gold.
Inflation-indexed bonds protect real returns, signal an anti-inflation commitment and offer an alternative to gold savings.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Low and stable inflation protects poorer households, supports confidence in the rupee and helps anchor foreign portfolio investment.
A key criticism is that headline CPI may reflect supply shocks that interest rates cannot quickly resolve, while policy transmission may also be slow.

AP inflation was 4.9% against India’s 3.9%; rural inflation was 5.09% against urban inflation of 4.61%; it exceeded the national rate for the fifth straight month and was placed under a ‘Needs Attention’ watch.

rows.title: Indian tax system - direct and indirect taxes, tax buoyancy, tax-GDP ratio, progressivity
sub: Group-II M2-A-34: Indian tax structure - direct and indirect taxes; tax-GDP ratio and buoyancy

secs.t: Direct vs indirect taxes - classification and base

x: Exam angle: "which is a direct tax" lists; STT is a direct tax even though collected by the exchange.
STT is classified as a direct tax and is levied on the
value of securities traded on stock exchanges
GST, an indirect tax on the supply of goods and services, came into effect on
1 July 2017
Direct taxes are generally considered non-inflationary, while indirect taxes can raise prices because their burden is incorporated into the prices of goods and services.
Wealth tax, gift tax and estate duty
are referred to as ‘paper taxes’ because they historically yielded little revenue.

secs.t: Tax sources ranked in Centre's and States' revenue - direct vs indirect share

x: Exam angle: "largest source of Centre's receipts" = borrowings; "largest tax" = income tax (2026-27).
Indirect taxes dominated until the late 2000s, but direct taxes now exceed indirect taxes, reflecting a shift towards a more progressive tax structure.
The 2026–27 Budget Estimate places direct taxes at 61.2% and indirect taxes at 38.8%, while the FY22–FY25 average direct-tax share was 55.5%.
SGST
is the largest own-tax source of Andhra Pradesh, yielding ₹36,296 crore or 38% of its own-tax revenue of ₹94,967 crore.
The 80th Amendment, enacted in 2000, operated retrospectively with effect from
1 April 1996
in relation to the sharing of Union tax revenues with the States.

secs.t: Tax-GDP ratio - Centre, States, combined; falling ratio; peers

x: The tax-GDP ratio is
total tax revenue divided by nominal GDP
A low tax-GDP ratio may reflect a large informal sector or high tax evasion, thereby limiting fiscal capacity.
The World Bank benchmark is 15 per cent, and India's 2001–2022 average was 16.36 per cent.
The combined tax-GDP ratio of the Centre and States was approximately
19.6 per cent
A falling ratio indicates that tax revenue is growing more slowly than GDP.
A tax buoyancy value above one means that tax revenue increases at a faster rate than GDP.

secs.t: Tax, cess, surcharge and fee - distinction

x: Exam angle: "pecuniary burden imposed by legislative authority to support government" =
Tax
A tax is a compulsory pecuniary contribution imposed under the authority of law to finance government, without a direct quid pro quo.
The Clean Energy Cess on coal, introduced under the Finance Act, 2010, was renamed the
Clean Environment Cess in Budget 2016–17
The Chelliah approach favours base widening through more taxpayers and fewer exemptions, together with lower rates rather than rate hikes.

secs.t: Tax concepts in national income - disposable income, demand, productivity

x: Revenue is zero at the two extreme rates in the model, producing the inverted-U relationship between tax rates and revenue.
Arthur Laffer popularised the Laffer curve in 1974, and the term was coined by
Jude Wanniski

secs.t: Progressive, proportional, regressive taxes

x: Income tax
is progressive because the rate generally rises with income, reflecting the ability-to-pay principle.
A degressive tax is progressive up to a point and then becomes flat, as in a capped slab structure.
India's tax structure combines progressive direct taxes with regressive tendencies in indirect taxation, and a higher direct-tax share can improve progressivity.

secs.t: Tax reform committees - chairperson and focus

x: The Indirect Taxation Enquiry Committee headed by
L.K. Jha
in 1976 suggested VAT for India.
The Parthasarathi Shome Committee in 2012 dealt with GAAR and recommended scrapping retrospective tax provisions.
MODVAT was introduced on 1 March 1986, CENVAT on 1 April 2000, Haryana adopted VAT on 1 April 2003, and State VAT became nationwide on 1 April 2005.

secs.t: Constitutional basis of taxation

x: The Union, State and Concurrent Lists contain 15, 20 and 3 taxing entries respectively, while residuary taxing power, including taxes such as gift and wealth taxes, rests with Parliament.
Income from nursery saplings
is treated as agricultural income and is exempt under Section 10(1); poultry and dairy income are not treated as agricultural income for this purpose.

secs.t: Tax buoyancy vs tax elasticity

x: Tax buoyancy is the percentage change in tax revenue divided by the percentage change in GDP, including the effects of discretionary changes in tax rates or the tax base.
Tax elasticity measures the response of tax revenue to changes in GDP after excluding discretionary changes in tax rates or the tax base.

secs.t: Taxable event for each tax

x: The taxable event for sales tax or VAT is the sale of goods.
GST is levied on the
supply of goods or services
, replacing the earlier tax-event distinction based mainly on manufacture, sale or provision of service.

secs.t: Historical composition - early planning vs now

x: Excise, customs and sales taxes dominated during the early planning decades, whereas direct taxes have become dominant in the recent period.
Direct taxes accounted for approximately
of total tax revenue in FY 2024–25.
Income tax
was identified as the single largest tax source in the 2026–27 Budget Estimate.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Centre’s gross tax revenue grew by only
in the first quarter of 2026–27.
PAN-based data can attribute direct taxes to the headquarters of companies rather than to the locations where the income actually arises.
The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance, chaired by Bhartruhari Mahtab, criticised punitive
income-tax enforcement

rows.title: Direct tax reforms - income tax slabs, corporate tax cuts, faceless assessment, DTC debate
sub: Group-II M2-A-35: Direct tax reforms - income tax, corporate tax and administration reforms

secs.t: Income tax regimes - slabs, rebate, standard deduction, surcharge

x: Under the revised slabs, income up to ₹4 lakh is taxed at nil rate; the subsequent rates are 5%, 10% and 15% for the next three slabs respectively.
All three statements are correct: the Section 87A rebate makes income up to ₹12 lakh tax-free, and the ₹75,000 standard deduction raises the effective salaried threshold to ₹12.75 lakh.
The initial regime had a nil slab up to ₹2.5 lakh, the 2023-24 structure raised it to ₹3 lakh, and Budget 2026-27 retained the 2025-26 slabs.

secs.t: Special direct taxes - meaning and introducing Budget

x: Expenditure tax was introduced in 1958, wealth tax in 1957, gift tax in April 1958 and estate duty in 1953.
MAT taxes so-called zero-tax companies on their book profits, ensuring a minimum tax liability despite low or nil regular income-tax liability.
The 2019 amendment reduced the rate for eligible domestic companies without exemptions to
, with the effective rate becoming approximately 25.17% after surcharge and cess.
New manufacturing companies were offered a
tax rate, with an effective rate of approximately 17% after surcharge and cess; MAT did not apply to companies opting for this provision.
Indexation uses the Cost Inflation Index notified by the CBDT, and the stated base year is 2001-02.
DDT was abolished by Budget 2020-21 with effect from 1 April 2020; dividends thereafter became taxable in the hands of shareholders.
From Budget 2026-27, share buybacks are taxed as capital gains; the stated effective rates are 22% for promoters and 30% for non-corporate taxpayers.

secs.t: Direct tax committees - chairperson and focus

x: Nicholas Kaldor focused on expenditure, wealth and gift taxes; K.N. Raj on agricultural wealth and income; Wanchoo on black money and tax evasion; and Raja Chelliah on lower rates and a broader tax base.
The Kelkar Task Force dealt with direct and indirect taxes in 2002, FRBM implementation in 2004, and tax simplification.
The Vijay Kelkar Task Force was constituted in 2002 and addressed direct and indirect tax reforms, including a roadmap for GST.

secs.t: Black money disclosure schemes

x: The Income Declaration Scheme, 2016 operated from 1 June to 30 September 2016 and imposed a total levy of 45%, comprising tax, surcharge and penalty.
Vivad se Vishwas is a direct-tax dispute resolution scheme under the Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act, 2020; a second scheme was introduced in 2024.
FAST-DS imposes 30% tax plus an equal additional amount, producing an effective 60% burden.
For previously taxed but unreported assets, FAST-DS provides a ₹1 lakh fee and uses fair market value as on 31 March 2026.

secs.t: Cross-border and digital taxation

x: The Parthasarathi
Shome Committee
advised scrapping retrospective taxation in the context of indirect transfers.
All four statements are correct: the 6% online advertising levy dates from 2016, the 2% e-commerce levy from 2020, the latter was dropped in 2024, and the former was abolished from 1 April 2025.
BEPS is an OECD/G20 project comprising 15 actions aimed at combating base erosion and profit shifting.
The 2026 amendment provides tax exemption till 2041 for
foreign rough-diamond and electronics-component firms using bonded warehouses

secs.t: Direct Taxes Code and Income-tax Act 2025

x: The draft Direct Taxes Code was released in 2009, the Bill was introduced in 2010, it lapsed in 2014, and the Akhilesh Ranjan task force submitted its report in 2019.
The Act introduces a single 12-month ‘
Tax Year
’ beginning on 1 April, replacing the separate Assessment Year and Previous Year terminology.

secs.t: Tax administration - PAN, faceless, AIS, TDS/TCS, Charter

x: AIS shows all reported transactions and, from 2021, widened the information earlier available through Form 26AS for pre-filled income-tax returns.
The provision allows resident buyers of property from non-residents to deduct TDS using
PAN instead of TAN
CBDT is the statutory apex direct-tax body under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963, located in the Department of Revenue and serving as cadre controller of the IRS.

secs.t: Corporate tax cuts - 2019 (Sections 115BAA, 115BAB)

x: Section 115BAB provides a 15 per cent corporate tax rate for eligible new manufacturing companies incorporated after 1 October 2019; the effective rate is approximately 17.01 per cent.
The Economic Survey 2025-26 described the 2019 corporate tax reduction as the
first pillar of tax reform
, followed by personal income-tax reform and GST 2.0.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance was chaired by
Bhartruhari Mahtab
and sought data on the Act’s impact on collections, assessees and litigation.
Simplification and lower rates are intended to widen the tax base and encourage voluntary compliance.
Critics have described enforcement as punitive, while retrospective taxation has been criticised for damaging investor confidence.

rows.title: Goods and Services Tax - structure, slabs, GST Council, IGST settlement, compensation cess
sub: Group-II M2-A-36: Goods and Services Tax - structure, rates, GST Council and revenue sharing

secs.t: Constitutional amendment for GST - Bill, Act, rollout, first State

x: Exam angle: Bill number (122nd) vs Act number (101st) is the classic trap.
The 101st Amendment created the GST constitutional framework, omitted Article 268A, amended the relevant Schedules and provided for compensation to States for revenue loss.
Article 246A gives Parliament and State Legislatures concurrent GST legislative power, but Parliament alone legislates in relation to
inter-State
supplies.
Article 269A
provides for the levy and collection of IGST on inter-State supplies by the Union and its apportionment between the Union and the States on the recommendation of the GST Council.

secs.t: GST Council - Article 279A, composition, voting, nature

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 and G1 2024 tested "269A vs 279A" and "statutory then constitutional" - both statements are false.
The GST Council recommends rates, exemptions, thresholds, model laws, revenue-sharing arrangements and dispute-resolution mechanisms.
In
Union of India v. Mohit Minerals
(2022), the Supreme Court held that GST Council recommendations are persuasive and not binding on Parliament or State Legislatures.
The GST Council brings the Union and the States together for decisions on taxation and is regarded as an institution of
cooperative federalism

secs.t: Taxes subsumed vs retained; objectives

x: Central Excise Duty
was subsumed into GST.
Entertainment Tax was subsumed into GST except when levied by local bodies.
Purchase Tax, Luxury Tax and Entry Tax
in all forms were subsumed into GST.
The conventional classification identifies eight Central taxes and nine State taxes as subsumed into GST.
The concept of
declared goods of special importance
was dropped under the GST framework.

secs.t: GST mechanisms

x: Under reverse charge, the recipient, rather than the supplier, pays GST on specified supplies.
Section 171 requires the benefit of a rate reduction or input-tax credit to be passed on to consumers through commensurate reduction in prices.
From 1 October 2024, the Principal Bench of GSTAT handles anti-profiteering cases.
An e-way bill is an electronic document for movement of goods valued above ₹50,000, with validity of one day per 200 kilometres.
E-invoicing helps check fake invoices, while HSN and SAC are classification codes for goods and services respectively.

secs.t: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated

x: The five petroleum products are crude oil, petrol or motor spirit, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel.
Electricity, real estate transactions subject to stamp duty, alcoholic liquor for human consumption and aviation turbine fuel are outside the current GST levy.
Nil-rated supplies attract a zero rate, exempt supplies are notified out of tax, and zero-rated supplies include exports and SEZ supplies with full ITC refund.

secs.t: GST compensation - Act, cess, period, end

x: Higher excise was imposed on tobacco under the Central Excise (Amendment) Act, 2025, while Health Security se National Security Cess was imposed on pan masala units.
Although the cess was withdrawn for most goods from 22 September 2025 and retained for tobacco, the compensation cess ended on
31 March 2026

secs.t: Committees on GST design

x: The Kelkar Task Force was chaired by Vijay Kelkar, the Empowered Committee by Asim Dasgupta, and the Revenue Neutral Rate Committee by Arvind Subramanian.
The roadmap was issued in 2008, the commitment to 1 April 2010 was made in July 2009, the First Discussion Paper appeared in November 2009, and GST was rolled out on 1 July 2017.

secs.t: Dual GST components, IGST settlement, GSTN

x: For an intra-State supply, CGST is levied by the Centre and SGST by the State in equal halves of the applicable GST rate.
GSTN supports GST registration, return filing and input-tax-credit matching; AI tools are also being used for scrutiny.
The GST Council approved the structure in September 2025, with 5 per cent and 18 per cent slabs, a 40 per cent slab for sin and luxury goods, and implementation from 22 September 2025.

secs.t: Rate-change procedure - notification vs Parliament, ceilings

x: The IGST Act provides a ceiling of
, while the CGST ceiling is 20%.
Rates are normally changed through government notification on the recommendation of the GST Council, rather than by amending the Acts each time.

secs.t: GSTN, e-way bill, e-invoicing

x: An e-way bill is mandatory for moving goods worth more than
The e-way bill is valid for
one day for every 200 km
of movement.
E-invoicing digitally reports invoices, helps curb fake invoices and supports verification of input-tax credit.
Low-risk applicants with a monthly tax liability up to
₹2.5 lakh
are eligible for the automated registration facility within three working days.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: GST is considered the biggest indirect tax reform since Independence because it established a unified framework for indirect taxation by subsuming several indirect taxes.
Monthly GST collections provide timely information on economic activity and government tax revenue, making them a useful macroeconomic indicator.
The GST framework led States to give up some independent indirect-tax powers, cesses remain outside the divisible pool, and Tamil Nadu raised the issue of fair devolution through a resolution.

rows.title: Impact of GST on commerce, industry and state finances; unresolved GST issues
sub: Group-II M2-A-37: GST - impact on commerce, industry and state finances; unresolved issues

secs.t: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

x: Before GSTAT benches became available, GST-related
appeals accumulated in the High Courts
An inverted duty structure exists when the tax paid on inputs exceeds the tax charged on output, leading to blocked credit; refunds are allowed in such cases.
E-invoicing, UPI/Aadhaar tracking and AI-based scrutiny are all measures used to counter ITC fraud.

secs.t: GST collections trend - national and AP

x: ₹17.4 lakh crore is approximately 79% of ₹22.08 lakh crore, which is
about three-fourths
and clearly more than one-half but less than the full annual amount.
GST buoyancy remained weak because the revenue loss from the rate cut had not yet been fully offset by volume gains.
The model uses a risk matrix, a Legal-AI assistant trained on about 22,000 judgments, and has covered more than 13,700 cases; other States are studying it.

secs.t: Impact on States - autonomy, compensation dependency, consuming vs producing

x: GST buoyancy was above the national average in only 16 States/UTs; manufacturing States gained, while unorganised-sector States relied more on Finance Commission devolution.

December 2025 net GST was ₹2,652 crore, up 5.78%; it was Andhra Pradesh’s highest December collection and the ninth consecutive month above the corresponding previous-year level, despite GST 2.0 rate cuts.

secs.t: Impact on commerce - logistics, checkposts, formalisation, MSMEs

x: E-way bills replaced physical border checks, reduced waiting time, and recorded 21 per cent year-on-year growth during April–December 2025.
The replacement of physical checks and the dismantling of border check-posts reduced truck waiting time, transit time and logistics costs.
Multiple returns and input tax credit matching
remain important compliance burdens under GST.

secs.t: Centre-State disputes - Mohit Minerals case

x: Safari Retreats and VKC Footsteps
are cited along with Mohit Minerals as landmark GST rulings.
Crude oil, petrol, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel are within the GST law but are taxed outside GST until the Council recommends a date under Article 279A(5).
The Court held that Central and State GST authorities must decide inter se who will proceed against a common entity, thereby preventing dual action.

secs.t: Evaluation studies - Economic Survey, RNR

x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 observed that increased volume of transactions following a rate cut may offset the associated revenue loss.
Gross GST collection during April–November 2019 was
Rs 8.05 lakh crore
The Economic Survey 2019–20 noted that rationalisation shocks raise collections only for about
one to three months

secs.t: Multiple vs single rate structure - drawbacks, classification disputes, inverted duty structure

x: Exam angle: "most important disadvantage of multiple rates" and IDS definition; the current slab set (5/18/40) vs the old four-slab set.
The 40% rate applies to specified demerit goods and services, including
ultra-luxury cars, tobacco, pan masala, online gaming and aerated drinks
Compensation cess over the 28% slab applied to
luxury and sin goods
, including luxury cars, aerated drinks, pan masala and tobacco.

secs.t: GST impact on states - revenue loss, compensation period and cess extension

x: States surrendered instruments such as VAT, entry tax, luxury tax, entertainment tax and octroi to GST.
After the compensation period, the cess was continued to repay loans taken for paying GST compensation during the COVID-19 period.
The compensation cess was scrapped on 22 September 2025 except for
tobacco products
, on which it continues until cess-account loan obligations are discharged.

secs.t: Consuming vs producing states under destination-based tax

x: Under the destination-based principle, GST revenue goes to
the State where goods or services are consumed
, rather than where they are produced.
Article 269A deals with the levy and collection of
GST on inter-State supplies and its apportionment
between the Union and the States.
Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
were identified as manufacturing States that feared losses because GST revenue follows consumption rather than production.

secs.t: GST Appellate Tribunal - set-up and benches

x: GSTAT is the second-appeal forum above appellate authorities, with its Principal Bench at New Delhi and State benches.
Although GSTAT had been notified, functional benches were absent in many States as of mid-2025, causing appeals to accumulate in High Courts.
The operational status of GSTAT benches, including the Andhra Pradesh bench, after July 2025 is not specified.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 57th GST Council meeting was scheduled for
12 September 2026
, and inverted-duty refunds were identified as an issue for consideration.
Cesses outside the divisible pool reduce the share available for devolution and are therefore linked with concerns about States’ fiscal autonomy and vertical fiscal imbalance.
GST came into force on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, with Articles 246A, 269A and 279A forming its key constitutional basis.

The term fiscal is derived from the Latin word fiscus, meaning a basket or public purse.
Public borrowing may be internal, such as bonds, Treasury Bills and small savings, or external, such as multilateral borrowing and sovereign bonds.

secs.t: Fiscal policy objectives - allocation, distribution, stabilisation (Musgrave)

x: The
distribution
function seeks to reduce inequality through progressive taxation and welfare spending, thereby changing the distribution of disposable income.
The stabilisation function seeks to smooth the business cycle and address inflation and unemployment through appropriate fiscal action.
Musgrave identified the three budget functions and popularised the term fiscal federalism in 1959.

secs.t: Crowding-out, counter-cyclical vs pro-cyclical stance, fiscal multiplier

x: Crowding out occurs when heavy government borrowing absorbs loanable funds, raises interest rates and reduces private investment.
A pro-cyclical policy cuts expenditure during slumps and increases it during booms, thereby intensifying economic volatility rather than smoothing it.
Capital expenditure generally has a larger fiscal multiplier than revenue expenditure or transfers because it can create productive capacity and stimulate complementary investment.

secs.t: Deficit trends - latest Union deficits, glide path, historical peaks

x: The fiscal deficit was 9.2% of GDP in 2020-21, the peak shown in the series, and is estimated at 4.3% in 2026-27 (BE).
The fiscal deficit target for 2026-27 is
₹16.96 lakh crore
, equivalent to 4.3% of GDP.
By July-end 2026, the fiscal deficit was ₹4,55,144 crore, representing 26.8% of the 2026-27 target; the comparable earlier-year figure was 29.9%.
The Debt-GDP ratio is estimated at 55.6% in 2026-27 (BE), lower than 56.1% in 2025-26 (RE).

secs.t: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies

x: Under fertiliser DBT, retail sale is recorded on PoS machines and the buyer is authenticated through Aadhaar; the subsidy is then released to the companies.
Major subsidies rose by
in Q1 of FY27, associated with a spike in crude oil prices following developments in West Asia.
Major subsidies were expected to overshoot the budget by about
₹50,000 crore

secs.t: Fiscal stance - expansionary vs contractionary, stimulus, consolidation path

x: Neutral policy seeks a stable demand effect, while counter-cyclical policy offsets the cycle and recession policy may increase public spending.
The fiscal deficit figures are 9.2% in FY21, 4.8% for FY25 (PA), 4.4% for FY26 (RE), and 4.3% for FY27 (BE).
The FY27 (BE) fiscal deficit is estimated at 4.3% of GDP, approximately
₹16.96 lakh crore
Fiscal consolidation seeks a sustainable path for public finances by controlling deficits and debt while preserving productive expenditure where possible.

secs.t: Objectives of fiscal policy - what is not one

x: Managing liquidity and money supply is an objective of monetary policy, not fiscal policy.
Economic growth, equitable distribution, resource mobilisation and balanced regional development are all objectives of fiscal policy.
Both statements are true, and expenditure and taxation affect aggregate demand, thereby explaining how fiscal policy can support employment and growth.

secs.t: Evolution of fiscal policy - Keynes, Long-Term Fiscal Policy

x: J. M. Keynes
developed the theory linking fiscal policy with economic performance.
The correct chronology is Long-Term Fiscal Policy in 1985, FRBM Act in 2003, N. K. Singh Committee in 2016, and the FRBM amendment in 2018.
The N. K. Singh Committee recommended a general government debt anchor of 60% of GDP, divided into 40% for the Centre and 20% for the States.

secs.t: Measures to reduce deficit

x: Rationalising subsidies through direct benefit transfer is an expenditure-side deficit-reduction measure.
All four are recognised measures.

secs.t: Financing of fiscal deficit - market borrowings, small savings, NSSF, external

x: Fiscal deficit is financed through market borrowings, small savings or NSSF, provident funds and external loans.
Borrowings and other liabilities accounted for
24 paise
of every rupee of receipts in Budget 2026-27 and were the largest single item.
Money-printing or direct RBI financing expands the monetary base and is identified as the most inflationary route of deficit financing.

secs.t: Quality of deficit - revenue deficit share in fiscal deficit

x: A high RD/FD ratio means a larger part of borrowing finances revenue or consumption expenditure rather than investment.
Revenue deficit is 1.5% of GDP against a fiscal deficit of 4.3%, giving a ratio of approximately
one-third

secs.t: Twin deficit - fiscal deficit and CAD link

x: Twin deficit denotes the coexistence of a fiscal deficit and a current account deficit.
Government dissaving lowers national savings, and the resulting savings-investment gap can increase reliance on foreign capital and widen the current account deficit.
FDI, FPI, NRI deposits and loans from the IMF or World Bank are all listed sources of CAD financing.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The analyst estimate placed the possible fiscal-deficit impact of oil-subsidy pressure at about 4.6 percent on the new GDP series.
All four statements are correct for Andhra Pradesh Budget Estimates 2026-27: revenue deficit is ₹22,002 crore or 1.11 percent of GSDP, and fiscal deficit is ₹75,868 crore or 3.84 percent of GSDP.
The debt-anchor rule permits a higher debt ratio than the FRBM's 40 percent level, and critics describe consolidation as slow.
S&P cited general government debt above 80 percent of GDP while discussing India's fiscal position and the slow pace of consolidation.

rows.title: FRBM Act - targets, escape clause, N.K. Singh Committee; fiscal consolidation path
sub: Group-II M2-A-33: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act - targets, escape clause and review

secs.t: FRBM Act 2003 - objectives, what it prescribes and what it does not, original targets, statements

x: Exam angle: "FRBM does NOT provide penal provisions" - the favourite trap.
The FRBM framework aims at fiscal discipline, transparency, macroeconomic stability and inter-generational equity, but it does not provide automatic penal provisions for missing targets.
The original framework specified elimination of the revenue deficit by 31 March 2009 and annual reductions of 0.3 per cent of GDP in the fiscal deficit and 0.5 per cent in the revenue deficit.

The Macro-Economic Framework covers macroeconomic prospects and risks; the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement gives rolling targets; the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement sets fiscal strategy; and the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework gives expenditure projections.

The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement covers four rolling indicators: revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, tax-related revenue or tax-GDP indicator, and total outstanding liabilities as percentages of GDP.

secs.t: N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee - debt anchor, targets, fiscal council, escape clause

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2017 - head of the FRBM review panel =
N.K. Singh
The stated grounds include national security, war, national calamity, agricultural collapse, structural reforms with unforeseen fiscal effects and a sharp fall in real output growth.
One escape-clause trigger is a fall in real output growth by
3 percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters

secs.t: Fiscal consolidation path - glide path, target revisions, shift to debt target

x: Exam angle: BPSC 2023 - FD reached
in FY21 (true).
The Economic Survey argued that strict FRBM targets should be delayed to retain flexibility amid a volatile geopolitical environment and also warned of worsening State finances.
The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended that the Centre reach a fiscal deficit of 3.5% of GDP and States reach 3% of GSDP by 2030-31.

secs.t: State fiscal responsibility laws - AP FRBM Act 2005

x: The Twelfth Finance Commission linked debt relief for States to the enactment of fiscal responsibility legislation through
the Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility
The FRBM limits restrain Andhra Pradesh’s
open-market borrowing
by imposing fiscal and borrowing discipline.
The Sixteenth Finance Commission sought State fiscal-rule reform and a wider deficit definition that would include off-budget borrowing.

secs.t: Amendments to FRBM - year and change

x: The 2018 amendment set a 3% fiscal-deficit target by 31 March 2021 and debt anchors of 60% for general government and 40% for the Centre by 31 March 2025.
The sequence is 2004 Rules, 2008-09 suspension, 2012 additions, and 2018 amendment introducing the debt anchor and clauses.
The 2015 change deferred or reset target dates; the dropping of revenue-deficit and effective revenue-deficit targets is associated with the 2018 amendment.

secs.t: Escape clause - conditions and deviation limit

x: The recognised grounds include national security, war, national calamity, collapse of agriculture, structural reforms with fiscal effect and severe economic slowdown or a sharp fall in real output growth.
The buoyancy clause requires a reduction in the fiscal deficit when real output growth rises sharply; it does not permit an automatic increase.

secs.t: Kelkar Task Force on FRBM implementation

x: The Task Force on Implementation of the FRBM Act, 2004 was chaired by
Vijay Kelkar
The Kelkar Task Force emphasised tax reform, widening the tax base and introducing a comprehensive Goods and Services Tax to help meet FRBM targets.
Vijay Kelkar chaired the
Thirteenth Finance Commission
, whose period was 2010–15.

secs.t: Suspension/deviation episodes - GFC, COVID

x: Fiscal targets were suspended during the global financial crisis, the COVID-19 fiscal deficit reached 9.2 per cent of GDP in 2020–21, and a gradual return path was adopted thereafter.
The Economic Survey 2025–26 supported delaying strict FRBM-type targets in view of
a volatile geopolitical environment
, while also warning that States’ finances were worsening.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Budget 2026–27 moved towards a debt-to-GDP anchor of 50 ± 1 per cent by 2031, while rolling fiscal-deficit targets remained suspended.
Experts have called for a published debt and fiscal-deficit glide path based on an explicit
nominal GDP
assumption.
The new debt anchor is 50 ± 1 per cent by 2031, higher than the 40 per cent level associated with FRBM, while repeated misses and the absence of a penalty clause remain criticisms.

rows.title: Union Budget - structure, process, key documents; highlights of the latest Union Budget
sub: Group-II M2-A-38: Recent Union Budget - receipts, expenditure, deficits and major announcements

secs.t: Latest Union Budget (2026-27) - priorities, allocations, schemes, fiscal deficit

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - FD RE 2024-25
was higher than BE 2025-26
(both statements correct).
Expenditure was ₹53,47,315 crore, receipts excluding borrowing were ₹36,51,547 crore and fiscal deficit was 4.3 per cent of GDP.
Defence received ₹7,84,678 crore, Road Transport and Highways ₹3,09,875 crore, Railways ₹2,81,377 crore and Home Affairs ₹2,55,234 crore.
Budget 2026–27 provides customs-duty exemption on capital goods for critical-mineral processing and proposes Rare Earth Corridors in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

secs.t: Receipts classification - order and items

x: A PSU stake sale is a non-debt capital receipt because it
reduces government assets
Market borrowings are debt capital receipts, recovery of loans is a non-debt capital receipt, GST is tax revenue and fees and fines are non-tax revenue.
The revenue budget covers revenue receipts and expenditure, whereas the capital budget covers capital receipts and expenditure, including borrowings and disinvestment.
Capital expenditure creates assets or provides loans, such as
construction of roads
, defence equipment and loans to States.
Wealth tax, gift tax and estate duty were described as paper taxes because they never generated large revenue and are now abolished.

secs.t: Budget history and reforms - first budget, Railway merger, 1 February, plan/non-plan

x: The separate Railway Budget began in 1924, its merger occurred in 2017, the presentation date shifted to 1 February in 2017, and the plan/non-plan distinction was removed in 2017-18.
Morarji Desai presented 10 budgets; 1973-74 was the Black Budget, 1997-98 was the Dream Budget, and Nirmala Sitharaman has presented every Budget since 2019.

secs.t: Budget types - meaning

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - justifying the entire budget from the beginning =
zero-base budgeting
Zero-based budget
ing requires every expenditure item to be justified afresh from zero for each period.
Peter Pyhrr devised zero-based budgeting, and
Jimmy Carter
was the first to use it in government.
The 16th Finance Commission has pushed output-based spending by linking Centrally Sponsored Schemes to measurable outcomes.
Performance budgeting links spending with programmes, activities and results; the First Hoover Commission is associated with it in the USA, and the ARC recommended it for India.

secs.t: Charged vs voted expenditure - Art. 112, Public Account

x: The President’s emoluments, interest on public debt, and the salary and administrative office expenses of the CAG are charged expenditure.
Capital expenditure
creates assets or reduces liabilities
; examples include capital works, loans given and debt repayment.
The old Plan and non-Plan classification, linked to Five-Year Plans, was scrapped from
Budget 2017-18
Developmental expenditure covers
economic and social services
, whereas interest, defence, administration and pensions are classified as non-developmental.
Article 112(3) includes debt charges, specified judicial salaries and pensions, and the salary and pension of the CAG, among other items.
Debt charges, the salary of the CAG, and sums required to satisfy court decrees or awards are charged items under Article 112(3).

secs.t: Budget process - preparation, stages, vote on account, guillotine, cut motions, Bills

x: Article 112 concerns the Annual Financial Statement, Article 113 the procedure on estimates, Article 114 the Appropriation Bill, and Article 115 supplementary, additional or excess grants.
Demands for Grants are voted by the Lok Sabha, while the Rajya Sabha can discuss them; charged expenditure is discussed but not voted upon.
A policy cut motion proposes reducing the demand to Re 1 and expresses
disapproval of the policy underlying the demand
Departmentally Related Standing Committees
examine the demands of the ministries concerned during the parliamentary recess.
The Appropriation Bill provides legal authority for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund, while the Finance Bill gives effect to tax proposals.
Article 114 governs the Appropriation Bill, and amendments cannot vary a voted grant, change its destination or vary charged expenditure.
The Finance Bill must be enacted within
75 days
under the stated provision of the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931.
Article 266 refers to the Consolidated Fund; withdrawal requires an Appropriation Act, while a vote on account authorises advance expenditure for part of the year.
A Finance Bill comes within the scope of a Money Bill under
Article 110(1)(a)
, insofar as it contains provisions dealing with taxation.

secs.t: Rupee comes from and rupee goes to (Budget 2026-27)

x: Borrowings and other liabilities
account for the largest share, at 24 paise of each rupee.
Income tax contributes
21 paise
of every rupee in the stated receipt composition.
Corporation tax, GST and other taxes, non-tax revenue, and Union excise duties account for 18, 15, 10 and 6 paise respectively.
The
States' share of taxes and duties
is the largest outflow, accounting for 22 paise.

secs.t: Key budget documents - content

x: The Annual Financial Statement is provided under Article 112 and covers the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account.
The FRBM statements include the Macro-Economic Framework Statement and the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement-cum-Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement, among others.
The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance prepares the Union Budget, in coordination with NITI Aayog and spending ministries.

The Annual Financial Statement gives estimated receipts and expenditure; Demands for Grants are generally ministry-wise; the Appropriation Bill permits withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund; and the Outcome Budget follows an output-outcome framework.

secs.t: Latest budget deficit estimates - fiscal deficit BE vs RE, capex, borrowing

x: The fiscal deficit was estimated at 4.8% of GDP in 2024-25 RE and 4.4% in 2025-26 BE.
Gross tax revenue to GDP is shown as
11.5% in FY25, 11.4% in FY26 RE and 11.2% in FY27 BE
During April-November 2025, capex increased by 28%, revenue expenditure increased by only 1.8%, and the fiscal deficit reached 62.3% of the budget estimate.

secs.t: Budget expenditure - plan/non-plan, development/non-development, largest items

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - non-plan expenditure =
interest payments
Interest payments, defence, subsidies, salaries, pensions and maintenance of assets created in earlier Plans were non-Plan items.
Non-plan expenditure included
interest payments, defence, subsidies, salaries and pensions
; interest payments were the classic example.
Defence spending is called committed because the scope for reducing it is limited, even when expenditure rationalisation is attempted.

secs.t: Major announcements of recent Union Budgets

x: Budget 2025-26 included
personal income-tax restructuring effective from April 2025 and GST 2.0 in September 2025
Budget 2026-27 maintained fiscal consolidation, with a 4.3% fiscal-deficit estimate and a debt-GDP path, without large tax cuts.

secs.t: Ministry-wise allocations

x: Mission VATSALYA received
Rs 900 crore
in Budget 2021-22 and concerns child protection and welfare.
Every ministry, barring a few exempted ministries, earmarks
of Gross Budgetary Support for the North-Eastern region since 1998-99.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Budget is the principal instrument of fiscal policy and performs the functions of resource allocation, income redistribution and economic stabilisation.
The States’ combined fiscal deficit was 3.2 percent of GDP in FY25, and 18 States exceeded the 3 percent limit in FY24.
The CAG flagged Andhra Pradesh’s revenue deficit for three years, and revenue receipts were only 48 percent of the Budget Estimates by November 2025.

x: Presentation of the Economic Survey before the Union Budget is a convention, whereas Article 112 relates to the Annual Financial Statement.

17 chapters

Artificial intelligence and urbanisation

letting go of non-essential sectors and reducing licensing and inspection burdens on MSMEs
Ease of Doing Business and Ease of Living
was identified as a pillar in Budget 2026-27.
The Bare Necessities Index in the Economic Survey 2020-21 measured Ease of Living at the
State level

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The confidence score in the CII Business Outlook Survey was 66 in Q2 of FY 2026-27.

The Andhra Pradesh Socio-Economic Survey is associated with the
Planning Department
and is tabled in both Houses along with the State Budget.

The constant-price growth estimate was revised downward from 9.24% in the earlier FAE to 8.27% in the FRE.

services
accounted for 40.45% of Andhra Pradesh GVA, exceeding agriculture and allied at 36.19% and industry at 23.36%.
Horticulture was second at ₹65,879 crore, livestock third at ₹65,486 crore, crops fourth at ₹27,999 crore, and forestry and logging stood at ₹2,737 crore.

recorded the slowest growth at 0.04% in 2024-25 FAE at constant prices.

had the largest GVA at ₹77,085 crore in the 2024–25 FAE data.

is not one of them.

GSDP of ₹308 lakh crore and per capita income of ₹55 lakh
Monthly Economic Reports monitor 651 KPIs across 30 Secretariat departments.

rows.title: River water sharing disputes - Krishna and Godavari; KWDT-I and II, GWDT, Apex Council, Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards

secs.t: Apex Council - composition, chairperson, functions (APRA Sec. 84)

x: Exam angle: "power to sanction new projects" = Apex Council, not the Boards or the Ministry.
The Apex Council can supervise the Boards, approve new projects after appraisal, settle disputes by negotiation and refer certain disputes to a tribunal.
The Apex Council is empowered to settle disputes through negotiation and to refer disputes not covered by KWDT to a tribunal under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956.

secs.t: KRMB and GRMB - headquarters, sections, jurisdiction, status, functions

x: The Boards regulate supply from notified headworks in accordance with tribunal awards, release water according to State shares and advise on floods and droughts.
The KRMB’s three-member committee allowed only drinking-water use from Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar because of El Niño and poor inflows.
The KRMB advised Telangana after storage in the
Srisailam
reservoir fell due to its power generation.

secs.t: Krishna water ad hoc sharing ratio between AP and Telangana

x: The ad hoc division was
in the ratio of Andhra Pradesh to Telangana, corresponding approximately to 512 TMC and 299 TMC respectively.
The 66:34 ad hoc division of 811 TMC gave approximately 512 TMC to Andhra Pradesh and 299 TMC to Telangana.
Telangana demanded equal sharing while citing
its larger basin area
as the basis for the claim.

secs.t: Tribunals - chairperson, award year, shares

x: Justice R.S. Bachawat chaired KWDT-I and the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal, whereas KWDT-II was chaired by Justice Brijesh Kumar.
KWDT-I awarded 560 TMC to Maharashtra, 700 TMC to Karnataka and 800 TMC to the united Andhra Pradesh at 75 per cent dependability.
The 800 TMC allocation, together with
11 TMC of return flows
, produced the 811 TMC figure used in the ad hoc division.

secs.t: Tungabhadra Board - parent Act, canals regulated

x: The Tungabhadra Board was established under Section 66 of the Andhra State Act, 1953.
After 2014,
Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
replaced the undivided Andhra Pradesh on the Tungabhadra Board under Section 91(1) of the AP Reorganisation Act.
The Tungabhadra Board continues to regulate releases to the
High Level Canal, Low Level Canal and Rajolibanda Diversion Scheme

secs.t: KWDT-II - AP-Telangana allocation dispute, Section 89 reference

x: Section 89 covered project-wise allocation where necessary and an operational protocol for deficit flows.
Section 89 provided for fixing an operational protocol for releases during
deficit flows
In October 2023, the Centre gave KWDT-II further terms of reference under
Section 5(1) of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956
, for dividing the Andhra Pradesh share between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

secs.t: Contested projects - river and State

x: In relation to Kaleshwaram, Andhra Pradesh sought clearances and Telangana wanted national-project status; the stated objection about exceeding the Krishna share concerns the Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link.
Andhra Pradesh plans to divert
200 TMC
of Polavaram flood water through the proposed link.
The proposed link is expected to benefit about
80 lakh people and 7.5 lakh acres
through reservoirs at Bollapalli and Banakacherla.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting was held at
Mahabalipuram in August 2026
and was chaired by the Union Home Minister.
Telangana sought
protection of its Krishna rights and national-project status for Kaleshwaram and Palamuru-Rangareddy
at the Southern Zonal Council meeting.
The Boards continue to face criticism because they lack full operational control, and disputes concerning unapproved projects and hydel drawal persist.

rows.title: Polavaram Project - status, funding, national project status, submergence and R&R issues

secs.t: National project status - APRA Section 90, executing authority, consent and clearances

x: Exam angle: "which section" (answer
; one old key says Section 30, and some CA notes say Section 89 - both wrong); statement-pairs on 90(1)-(4).
Although the Central Government is responsible under Section 90(4), the
Government of Andhra Pradesh
executes the irrigation component on behalf of the Government of India and claims reimbursement or advance from the Centre.

secs.t: Polavaram funding - Centre's share, cut-off date, cost revisions

x: The Union Budget 2026–27 provided
₹3,320 crore
for the revised cost, associated with storage up to 41.15 metres.
About ₹12,000 crore was reported as pending from the Centre, while Andhra Pradesh sought ₹32,000 crore for Polavaram Phase-II and permanent lifting of the MoEF stop-work order.
The Centre funds the remaining irrigation cost from 1 April 2014, while Andhra Pradesh executes the component and seeks reimbursement or advances.

secs.t: Polavaram Project Authority (PPA) - constitution, CEO, role

x: The Polavaram Project Authority was constituted by the Union after the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 to
oversee the national project, route national-project funding and mediate inter-State coordination
M. Raghuram is the Member-Secretary, and M. Ramesh Kumar is the Chief Engineer at Rajamahendravaram.
The Authority was constituted after the Reorganisation Act, performs inter-State coordination functions, and the CEO sits in New Delhi.

secs.t: Submergence - Khammam mandals (Polavaram Ordinance), other States affected

x: The seven mandals included Kukunoor, Velerupadu, VR Puram, Chintoor, Kunavaram, Bhadrachalam except the temple town, and Burgampadu.
No. 111 was issued on 27 June 2005, the Act came into force on 1 March 2014, the Lok Sabha passed the Bill on 11 July 2014, and the Authority was constituted after the Act.
Odisha and Chhattisgarh
objected in connection with protective embankments, while Telangana raised the issue of backwater at Bhadrachalam.

secs.t: Project features - river, district, reservoir, canals, hydel

x: The project has a 2,467.50-metre earth-cum-rock fill dam and a 1,121.20-metre spillway.
The project provides 23.44 TMC for Visakhapatnam, intended to serve approximately
28.5 lakh people in 540 villages
Sir Sonti Venkataramamurthy
named the proposal “Ramapada Sagaram.”.
The dam is 2,467.50 metres long, the spillway is 1,121.20 metres long, and the irrigation potential is 2.91 lakh hectares.

secs.t: R&R issues - tribal displacement, compensation, court cases

x: The 27.40% figure represented the combined progress of land acquisition and R&R in December 2025, while separate August 2026 figures were 94% for land acquisition and 52% for family relocation.
Compensation of ₹1,943 crore was paid in three phases, house-site value was doubled to ₹2 lakh, and compensation follows the RFCTLARR Act, 2013.

secs.t: Status - diaphragm wall, completion timelines, expert reviews

x: The December 2025 figures were 60.8% overall, 81.61% for head works, 92.79% for the right main canal and 73.40% for the left main canal.
Spillway, radial gates, coffer dams, Gap-III concrete dam and buttress dam were all stated to be completed.
The foreign expert panel, with the CWC, reviewed
Gap-1, Gap-2 and the diaphragm wall
during its sixth visit.

secs.t: GWDT clauses - Polavaram and Godavari-to-Krishna diversion

x: The award provided for Polavaram at FRL +150 feet and diversion of 80 TMC, distributed as 45 TMC to Andhra Pradesh and 35 TMC to Karnataka and Maharashtra together.
The linked projects are Pattiseema and the proposed Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link, earlier called Banakacherla.
Pattiseema is a temporary lift arrangement into the Polavaram Right Main Canal.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A major criticism is that Phase-I storage is proposed at 41.15 metres, below the full reservoir level of 45.72 metres.
The revised cost estimate had not yet been cleared.

rows.title: Irrigation in AP - major and medium projects, Handri-Neeva, Pattiseema, Galeru-Nagari, Vamsadhara
sub: Group-II M2-A-86: Irrigation in Andhra Pradesh - sources, major projects and micro-irrigation

secs.t: Irrigation data - GIA/GCA, net irrigated area, source-wise share, top district

x: In 2023-24, gross irrigated area was 32.71 lakh hectares, net irrigated area was 26.03 lakh hectares and cropping intensity was 1.21.
Wells and tube wells
accounted for the largest share, covering 15.68 lakh hectares or approximately 48% of the GIA.
Eluru
recorded the largest GIA at 2.39 lakh hectares, followed by Ananthapuramu at 2.04 lakh hectares and Nandyal at 1.98 lakh hectares.
Tank irrigation is important because the peninsular plateau has undulating relief and impervious rocks, which favour the accumulation and storage of water.

secs.t: Pattiseema - type, rivers linked, beneficiaries, temporary nature

x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram Right Main Canal, which carries it to the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage.
Pattiseema was a temporary scheme intended to function until gravity flow from the Polavaram project became available.
Pattiseema had 24 pumps, was built during 2014-19, commissioned in 2015 and helped supply the Krishna delta during the 2026 El Niño deficit.

secs.t: Major projects - river, districts, plan period, foundation

x: Exam angle: "Pattiseema is a lift irrigation project" and "not true" statement sets on its canal and purpose.
The Telugu Ganga project carries Krishna surplus through the Srisailam-Somasila-Kandaleru-Poondi system, supplying drinking water to Chennai and irrigation water to Rayalaseema and Nellore.
The Eleventh Schedule lists
Handri-Neeva, Telugu Ganga, Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda, Kalwakurthy and Nettempadu
for completion with the existing water-sharing arrangements.
Construction of Prakasam Barrage began in February 1954, Veligonda’s foundation stone was laid in 1996, Jalayagnam began in 2004, and Veligonda Phase-I was inaugurated in 2026.
Polavaram is a multipurpose project intended for irrigation, drinking water, hydropower and flood control;
salt production
is not listed as its purpose.
The Veligonda Project draws from the Srisailam reservoir through tunnels and serves
Prakasam, Nellore and YSR Kadapa
districts.
Veligonda Phase-I releases
10.70 TMC for 1.19 lakh acres
; 43.5 TMC and 4.47 lakh acres refer to the broader project.

secs.t: Jalayagnam - plan period and incomplete projects

x: Jalayagnam was launched in 2004 by the Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy government during the
Tenth Five Year Plan
period, 2002–07.
Jalayagnam aimed to irrigate one crore acres and stabilise 21 lakh acres; 41 major and 25 minor projects were proposed.
Polavaram, begun in 2005, is treated as a Jalayagnam project.

secs.t: Participatory groundwater management - APFAMGS

x: APWALTA, 2002 requires rainwater-harvesting structures on residential, commercial and other premises of 200 square metres or more and seeks to prevent indiscriminate borewell digging.

All four statements reflect the stated groundwater-management position: APWALTA norms guide investigations and siting, 258 villages were proposed for notification, 3,005 telemetry wells were recorded, and development was about 30% at the safe stage.

secs.t: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

x: Neeru-Meeru was a watershed and rainwater-harvesting drive intended to raise groundwater levels.
Neeru-Chettu operates across line departments under the Water Resources Department and includes the listed water-conservation works.
Neeru-Chettu includes repairs, supply-channel desilting and tank-cascade development, but not construction of nuclear power plants.
₹445.89 crore
was budgeted in 2025–26 to clear pending Neeru-Chettu bills.

secs.t: Water use efficiency - APMIP, drip and sprinkler

x: Per Drop More Crop began in 2015–16, has been under RKVY since 2022–23, and covered 102 lakh hectares nationally since 2015–16.
The Micro Irrigation Fund is maintained through NABARD with a ₹10,000 crore corpus, and Andhra Pradesh is among the eight States funded.
Saturating micro-irrigation could raise groundwater-based net irrigation to about
40 lakh acres

secs.t: Major multipurpose projects → river + state

x: The Damodar Valley project is on the Damodar and is associated with Jharkhand and West Bengal.
Hirakud in Odisha is noted as
one of the longest earthen dams

secs.t: Inter-state boards - Tungabhadra Board, KRMB, GRMB

x: KRMB and GRMB operate under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, following the principles in Schedule 11.
All four statements correctly state the operating and enforcement principles applicable to the Boards.

secs.t: Water disputes tribunals - KWDT, GWDT

x: The 1980 GWDT award permitted the Polavaram diversion of
80 TMC
of Godavari water to the Krishna.
The concern was that the Krishna water settlement with Telangana was being linked to Andhra Pradesh’s consent to the Palamuru–Rangareddy project.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Rayalaseema depends on the Krishna-lift projects HNSS, GNSS and Telugu Ganga, which often run dry.
The proposal was to complete Polavaram before the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu and to divert about 200 TMC of Godavari water to the Nagarjunasagar ayacut.
PMKSY includes AIBP, Har Khet Ko Pani, Watershed and Per Drop More Crop.

rows.title: New challenges to industry and commerce after bifurcation - loss of industrial base, relocation

secs.t: Loss of industrial base - IT and pharma clusters left in Hyderabad

x: The residual State lost Hyderabad's HITEC City and Financial District, important centres of IT and IT-enabled services exports.
Genome Valley and the Hyderabad pharmaceutical belt, including their research and development facilities, remained outside residual Andhra Pradesh.
Many Hyderabad-linked ancillary MSMEs ended up across the border, breaking the supply chains on which they depended.

secs.t: Industrial GVA share of residual AP - before and after

x: Residual Andhra Pradesh was about 60 percent agriculture-dependent, and manufacturing was put at around 10.5 percent of GSDP.
The approximately 10.5 percent figure related to manufacturing just after bifurcation, while 24 percent was the industry share of GVA in 2025-26.
Manufacturing accounted for
of GVA at current prices in 2025-26.
Fishing and Aquaculture was 9.42%, Other Services 8.81%, Horticulture 8.78% and Real Estate 8.51%.

secs.t: Relocation of institutions and headquarters - PSUs, offices, Amaravati move

x: Schedule IX covered 91 companies and corporations; Schedule X covered 142 institutions, mostly in Hyderabad; the Sheela Bhide Committee was associated with the division; and Section 53 provided the location and population basis.
The Schedules have been criticised as non-exhaustive because key training institutes, including APPA and APFA, were left out.

secs.t: Industrial incentives under Section 94 - tax incentives, backward districts

x: Special Category Status was refused with reference to the 14th Finance Commission, and the Centre offered
a Special Assistance Measure of ₹24,350 crore
instead.
Section 46 covers all three matters: consideration of successor-state resources, grants and a special development package, with particular attention to Rayalaseema and the north coastal districts.

secs.t: Commerce challenges - no metro base, investor perception, capital uncertainty

x: Capital uncertainty, the absence of a ready administrative set-up and agitations reduced FDI and private investment.
The high cost of doing business was linked to the lack of mature power grids, logistics parks and ready factories.
With Hyderabad no longer serving as the commercial base, trade had to be re-routed away from Hyderabad-centred supply chains.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: In June 2026, SIPB cleared
87 proposals
worth ₹34,000 crore.
The industrial-hub development in Rayalaseema is associated with
Kia, JSW, Royal Enfield near Tirupati and the Space City
The criticism was that Section 94 incentives and backward-area grants fell short of what was asked, and that Special Category Status was denied.

sub: Group-II M2-A-103: Ports, power and infrastructure as industrial enablers in Andhra Pradesh

secs.t: AP installed power capacity - total and source-wise mix

x: APGENCO and APPDCL together owned
, including thermal, hydel and solar capacity.
The combined 8,789.03 MW owned by APGENCO and APPDCL represented
46.37 percent
of the AP grid.
There are 22.36 lakh farm pump sets receiving nine hours of free daytime power, and aqua power is priced at ₹1.50 per unit.
All three statements are correct: the APGENCO–NHPC joint venture was formed in September 2024, Upper Sileru is 1,350 MW, and the Kamalapadu DPR was cleared at ₹7,377 crore.
Bagasse cogeneration is 206.95 MW, biomass 171.25 MW, small hydro 106.80 MW and municipal solid waste 36.15 MW.

secs.t: AP power DISCOMs - full forms, jurisdiction, reforms, finances

x: All three jurisdictional descriptions are correct: APEPDCL covers the north coastal and Godavari districts, APSPDCL covers Nellore and Rayalaseema, and APCPDCL covers the central coastal districts.
Smart meters and feeder segregation are being used to reduce AT&C losses, and 312 of 3,015 feeders had been completed.
APEPDCL and APSPDCL
are counted among India's top performers on loss reduction.

secs.t: AP energy policies - objectives and targets

x: The policy targets 160 GW of clean energy, Net Zero by 2047, ₹10 lakh crore investment and 7.5 lakh jobs.
The identified National Green Hydrogen Mission hubs are
Paradip, Kandla and Tuticorin
The initiative aims to reduce the cost of green hydrogen to
Rs 160–170 per kg
The Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024 targets 160 GW of renewable-energy capacity and aims for Net Zero by 2047.

secs.t: Railways in AP - new zone, new lines, freight corridors

x: South Coast Railway was promised in the Thirteenth Schedule of the A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014, and was carved from SCR and ECoR.
The policy gives priority to links with the East Coast Dedicated Freight Corridor and the North–South Dedicated Freight Corridor.
The Raipur–Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway is described as a
Bharatmala
economic corridor.
The Narketpally–Addanki–Medarametla road is the completed 125-km PPP link between NH-65 and NH-16.

secs.t: Maritime Policy and AP Maritime Board - port-led targets

x: NSHIP-AP Ltd was formed in 2026 as the special purpose vehicle associated with the maritime policy initiatives.
The policy targets at least one Andhra Pradesh port being placed
among the world's top 20 ports
The policy targets 25% of the national shipbuilding target by 2047, described in connection with the Global Shipyard objective.

secs.t: APIIC and APIDC - incorporation, parks, land bank

x: APIIC was stated to have
331 parks and 304 estates
The figures were presented as 331 UDLs and 635 clusters, with the 331 parks and 304 estates forming the stated industrial infrastructure network.
APIIC
can allot up to 50 acres without Cabinet approval under the stated arrangement.
APIIC was identified as the nodal agency for the Centre's
BHAVYA parks

secs.t: Oil and gas - KG basin, refinery complex

x: The Kakinada–Konaseema region constitutes Andhra Pradesh's oil and gas hub and is associated with the KG basin.
The proposed BPCL refinery-cum-petrochemical complex near Ramayapatnam has a planned capacity of
9 MTPA
HBJ pipeline locations support gas-based urea plants, while Talcher, Ramagundam and Korba are coal-based centres; Kakinada uses KG-basin gas.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: APGIC was established in 2009, the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act was enacted in 2014, the SCoR zone became operational on 1 June 2026, and Bhogapuram airport became operational on 1 August 2026.

All four statements are correct: South Coastal Railway became operational on 1 June 2026, Bhogapuram Airport opened in August 2026, Visakhapatnam Port recorded 91.17 MMT in FY26, and Vijayawada station received IGBC Platinum certification in August 2026.

to attract tourists
by expanding affordable accommodation facilities.
Andhra Pradesh received the GTM 2026 award, a draft MICE policy was proposed for Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada, and the tourism vision was unveiled at the FAITH conclave.

five regional medical hubs for medical tourism and five university townships in industrial corridors

rows.title: Approaches and initiatives in AP agriculture - APCNF/ZBNF, horticulture, aquaculture, allied sectors
