secs.t: Farmer service institutions - year, count, features

x: Rythu Bazars facilitate direct sale from farmers to consumers; 129 are functioning and 10 are under construction.
Rythu Bharosa Kendras were established in 2020, and
10,778 centres
were set up beside village secretariats.
RSKs provide agricultural services such as soil testing, e-Panta, CCRC issuance, input subsidies, crop insurance, drone awareness and procurement.
A total of 10,606 Rythu Seva Kendras provide doorstep veterinary care through Animal Husbandry Assistants.
RySS ran the Debt Redemption Scheme 2014, under which assistance was provided up to ₹1.5 lakh per family, and currently runs APCNF.

secs.t: AP farmer support schemes - amount, instalments, eligibility

x: Exam angle: amount traps (₹13,500 vs ₹20,000 vs Telangana's ₹12,000 per acre) and "tenant farmers included - true".
During 2019–2024, YSR Rythu Bharosa-PM Kisan provided ₹13,500 per family per year and covered owners, tenant farmers and RoFR cultivators.
Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan operates from 2024–25 onwards, covers farmer families including CCRC-holding tenants, and includes the ₹6,000 PM-KISAN component for landholders.

secs.t: Soil and crop health programmes - outlay and objective

x: Soil Health Cards promote judicious fertiliser use by providing information about soil conditions and nutrient requirements.
e-Crop booking creates a digital crop record that serves as the basis for insurance, MSP procurement, input subsidy and loss assessment.
e-Fish booking
provides the corresponding digital record function for aqua farmers.
In 2025–26, 6.0 lakh soil samples were collected and 5.52 lakh samples were tested.

secs.t: Horticulture - AP production and productivity ranks, crops by district

x: Andhra Pradesh recorded horticulture GVA of ₹1,52,950 crore, ranked third after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra, and registered 21% growth in 2024-25.
Andhra Pradesh has set a target of
₹3 lakh crore
horticulture GVA by 2029-30, covering 22 growth-engine crops.
Rayalaseema has about 7.8 lakh hectares under horticulture, contributes roughly half of horticulture GVA and contains 71% of the micro-irrigation area.
Paddy covered 20.97 lakh hectares out of the 37.51 lakh hectares under food grains, which is approximately
Fruits produced 200.66 lakh MT, plantation crops 58.84 lakh MT, vegetables 77.04 lakh MT and spices 20.15 lakh MT in 2023-24.
Total horticulture covered 45.59 lakh acres and produced 365.92 lakh metric tonnes in 2023-24.
Fruits occupied 19.89 lakh acres and recorded production of 200.66 lakh metric tonnes in 2023-24.
Andhra Pradesh ranks first in productivity of oil palm, papaya, lime, cocoa, tomato and chillies
The 2024–25 figures are 18.57 lakh hectares, 406.38 lakh MT, ₹1,52,950 crore and 21% growth.
The listed horticultural crops include dragon fruit, oil palm and Araku coffee.
Cultured shrimp is associated with about 75 per cent of India’s cultured shrimp exports; eggs rank first; oil palm is first in area, production and productivity; and raw silk ranks second.

The October 2025 coverage included

ZBNF promotes no chemicals, local-input seed treatment, mulching, microbial cultures, crop diversity, minimum tillage and livestock integration.

; 3,49,364 seedlings were produced in 2025-26.

CCRCs facilitate loans, insurance, MSP and scheme access, but they do not confer permanent ownership on tenants.

under the CAA Act and Rules, 2005, amended in 2023.

of the geographical area.

fruits, vegetables, flowers and spices
because of their profitability and export potential.

Godavari delta

secs.t: Panta Sanjeevani - meaning, component, initial outlay

100% renewable energy
for agricultural pump-sets.

x: Polambadi means Farmer Field Schools.

Rythu Sadhikara Samstha was incorporated in
October 2014

Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming

secs.t: APCNF practices

x: Jeevamrutham is prepared from cow dung, cow urine, jaggery, pulse flour and soil.
APCNF promotes native seeds, minimal or no tillage, livestock integration and trap crops;
exclusive dependence on purchased chemical fertilisers
is contrary to the model.
Kurnool is promoting PMDS on
92,000 acres
in response to the El Nino-related rain deficit.

Outcomes and evaluations - yield, cost, income, international awards

Direct Benefit Transfer
when prices crash.

wheat

8–9% of GSDP

rows.title: Agro-climatic zones of Andhra Pradesh and their cropping suitability
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I C-114

secs.t: Zone → districts covered (latest Socio-Economic Survey)

x: Godavari and Krishna are river-based; North Coastal and Southern are direction-based; Scarce Rainfall and High Altitude and Tribal Areas refer to physical conditions.

All three statements are correct: the Southern Zone includes Chittoor, YSR Kadapa and SPS Nellore; the Scarce Rainfall Zone includes Kurnool and Anantapur; and Agency areas form the High Altitude and Tribal Zone.

secs.t: Zone → dominant crops and soils

x: The
Godavari
zone, characterised by fertile deltaic alluvium, is described as a rice bowl and an aquaculture hub.
The
Krishna
zone, consisting of deltaic and coastal plains, is associated with paddy, chillies and cotton.
The Southern zone has varied terrain ranging from plains to hills and supports both dryland and irrigated crops.

secs.t: Rainfall by zone - drought-prone zones

x: South-West Monsoon rainfall during 2024-25 was
, compared with the normal of 574.7 mm.
The North-East Monsoon recorded
in 2024-25 against a normal of 285.3 mm.
For the South-West Monsoon, the normal rainfall was 574.7 mm and the actual rainfall was 681.6 mm, representing a positive deviation of 18.6%.

secs.t: Regional Agricultural Research Stations (ANGRAU) per zone

x: Anakapalle is the RARS associated with the North Coastal zone.
Godavari has Maruteru, Krishna has Lam (Guntur), Southern has Tirupati, and High Altitude and Tribal has Chintapalle.
Nandyal
is the Regional Agricultural Research Station associated with the Scarce Rainfall zone.
ANGRAU works on drought-resistant paddy, flood-tolerant pulses, pest-resistant cotton, drone-based precision farming and soil restoration in rain-shadow areas.

secs.t: Agro-ecological subregions (NBSS&LUP)

x: An agro-ecological zone is a land unit carved out of an agro-climatic zone by superimposing
landform
, which modifies climate and the length of the growing period.
The Planning Commission classification had 15 regions and 72 sub-zones, NARP identified 127 agro-climatic zones, and ICAR/NBSS&LUP identified 20 agro-ecological regions.

secs.t: Zone-based contingency crop planning

x: Pre-monsoon dry sowing is referred to as
PMDS
and uses residual soil moisture, particularly in drought-prone areas.
District agricultural contingency plans are prepared by
ICAR-CRIDA
Zone-based planning provides region-specific interventions, including advice on alternative crops when Kharif sowing is inadequate.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Both statements are true, and uneven water distribution across the six agro-climatic zones contributes directly to disparities in irrigation and farm income.
Karnataka
has 10 agro-climatic zones, whereas the current Andhra Pradesh classification has six.

rows.title: Rural credit cooperatives in Andhra Pradesh - structure, performance and problems
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I C-114

secs.t: AP cooperative laws - APCS Act 1964 and MACS Act 1995

x: The MACS Act, 1995 provides for self-reliant societies without government share capital, run by members with minimal state control.
The correct sequence is the Cooperative Credit Societies Act of 1904, the All India Rural Credit Survey of 1951–54, the MACS Act of 1995 and the National Cooperative Policy of 2002.

secs.t: Number of cooperative societies - trend

x: A total of 1,756 primary Labour Contract Cooperative Societies, along with their district and state federations, were under liquidation.
India has about 8.5 lakh cooperatives with over 30 crore members.
Andhra Pradesh had 210 primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies, with defunct societies being wound up.

secs.t: Cooperative credit structure - APCOB, DCCBs, PACS; long-term credit

x: The CDI summary of SES 2025–26 gives 2,024 PACS and 436 DCCB branches, whereas APSES 2024–25 gives 2,042 PACS and 442 branches.
PACS undertake procurement, seed processing, PDS, insurance, RO drinking water, petrol bunks, rice mills and warehousing.
All three figures are reported for 2024–25: production credit of Rs 5,933.92 crore, long-term agricultural credit of Rs 1,345.51 crore, and Rs 125.90 crore to 14,425 tenant farmers.

secs.t: PACS computerisation and multi-purpose PACS

x: A total of
PACS assigned to fertilizer companies had become PM Kisan Samruddhi Kendras.
Nationally, ERP software covers about 80,000 PACS, while model bye-laws allow PACS to undertake more than 25 non-credit activities.
PACS in 207 blocks are being treated as FPOs, and APCOB is the Cluster-Based Business Organisation in this arrangement.

secs.t: Problems - overdues, political interference, low deposits, DCCB losses

x: Political capture distorts credit allocation and shields politically connected defaulters from recovery, thereby feeding overdues.
The identified problems include political interference, inactive societies, weak professional management, inadequate digital capacity, lack of spontaneity and state domination.
State audits in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh indicated that about
one-third
of PACS were inactive despite registration.

secs.t: Committees on cooperative credit → chairman

x: The Cooperative Credit Societies Act of 1904 started the cooperative movement.
The 1912 Act allowed the formation of non-credit cooperative societies.
The 2004 Task Force on revival of cooperative credit was chaired by A.
Vaidyanathan
The 2013 Expert Committee on short-term cooperative credit structure was chaired by
Prakash Bakshi

secs.t: Ministry of Cooperation initiatives - grain storage plan, model bye-laws

x: By July 2026, godowns had been completed in 313 PACS with storage capacity exceeding 1.80 lakh metric tonnes.
All three statements are correct: the plan covers two lakh societies, 24,417 have been set up, and PACS computerisation has an outlay of Rs 2,925.39 crore.
All four are listed among the additional cooperative initiatives: National Cooperative Exports Ltd, National Cooperative Organics Ltd, NUCFDC and NABARD’s Sahakar Sarathi.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The announcements included a cooperative life insurance company, expansion of Bharat Taxi to 500 cities and foundation stones for 47 grain godowns.
Andhra Pradesh’s strategy covers AIF-funded storage and procurement centres at RSKs, along with ICDP-II godowns in the three named districts involving Rs 609.39 crore.
Nehru identified cooperatives,
panchayats and schools
as three pillars of democracy.

rows.title: Institutional credit to agriculture in Andhra Pradesh - banks, NABARD and SHGs
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I C-114

secs.t: NABARD credit plan for AP - State Focus Paper size and growth

x: District Potential Linked Credit Plans are aggregated into NABARD's State Focus Paper, which subsequently feeds the SLBC Annual Credit Plan.
The plan allocated ₹2.55 lakh crore to agriculture and allied activities and ₹1.64 lakh crore to MSMEs.
Crop loans were allocated Rs 1.66 lakh crore; animal husbandry Rs 34,972 crore; fisheries Rs 21,098 crore; and horticulture Rs 11,961 crore.

secs.t: Sources of institutional finance for AP farmers

x: The PACS-DCCB-SCB cooperative system mainly provides short-term credit, whereas ARDBs provide long-term credit.
The review in January 2026 reported Rs 1,490 crore for tenant farmers and Rs 95,714 crore for MSMEs, along with the agriculture and allied-sector disbursement.
The revised directions apply from 1 January 2027 and increase the maximum KCC tenure to six years from the earlier five years.

secs.t: State-NABARD programmes → purpose; RIDF projects in AP

x: RIDF provides rural infrastructure loans to states, with the stated shares of 30% for irrigation, 26% for rural roads and 10% for bridges.

LTIF supports the state share of ongoing PMKSY irrigation projects; the Micro Irrigation Fund supports micro irrigation; the Warehouse Infrastructure Fund supports scientific storage and APMC facilities; and RIDF provides rural infrastructure loans.
The Warehouse Infrastructure Fund, introduced in 2013-14, supports
scientific storage and APMC facilities

secs.t: Interest-free crop loans - YSR Zero Interest Crop Loan scheme

x: Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme,
short-term crop loans up to Rs 3 lakh are available at 4% for prompt repayers
MISS is a Central Sector scheme involving RBI and NABARD; the lending rate is 7 per cent, with a 3 per cent prompt repayment incentive making the effective rate 4 per cent.

secs.t: Stree Nidhi and MEPMA

x: Stree Nidhi is
a credit cooperative federation promoted with SHG federations
MEPMA means
Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas
and serves urban SHGs.
MEPMA has 24 Zilla Samakhyas.
MEPMA provides a revolving fund of
Rs 52.60 crore
to SHGs.
MEPMA permits SHG bank linkage up to Rs 20 lakh.

secs.t: Bank schemes for rural women → launching bank

x: The Pattabhi Sitaramayya-Self Business Group scheme for rural women entrepreneurs was launched by
Andhra Bank
The policy targets five lakh women entrepreneurs.

secs.t: State Level Bankers' Committee - annual credit plan, priority sector

x: The Chief Minister noted inadequate MSME lending and the lagging performance of some banks, and asked banks to lend at scale for PM Surya Ghar.
Priority Sector Lending applies to commercial banks, RRBs, SFBs, LABs and primary UCBs.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Farm credit disbursement was Rs 28.69 lakh crore against a target of Rs 27.50 lakh crore, amounting to
104 per cent
of the target.
Both concerns have been raised: linkage loans may be too small, and members may lack individual CIBIL credit histories necessary for scaling up.
Andhra Pradesh leads India in SHG-bank linkage, has a 36 per cent national share and records a 99.66 per cent recovery rate.

sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I C-114

secs.t: Rythu Bazaars - year, coordinating officer, estate officer, management

x: Farmers sell directly to consumers in Rythu Bazars, while farmers sell to licensed traders in regulated market yards.
Rythu Bazar prices are fixed with the aim of being around
in relation to open-market prices.
Rythu Bazars are outside the Agricultural Market Committee framework, managed by Estate Officers and placed under the Revenue Department.

secs.t: Agricultural Market Committees and market yards - number, commodities, fee

x: APSES 2024-25 reports market fee collection of
Rs 433.39 crore
up to December 2024.
For 2024-25, the total godown stock was 1,052 godowns with a capacity of 9,65,492 metric tonnes.
APSES 2024-25 reports 626 operational godowns with a capacity of 5,65,508 MT.
SES 2025-26 reports 643 operational godowns with a capacity of 5,92,163 MT.

secs.t: AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966 - provisions

x: The Rules govern licensing-related matters such as issue of licences, fees, turnover and the period of validity.
The three central farm laws of 2020 were repealed in November 2021, but the 1966 AMC framework remained operative.
The Model APMC Act introduced a single market fee, registration in place of licensing, and farmers' and consumers' markets.

secs.t: Market intervention / price stabilisation

x: For perishables, the Government intervenes through procurement in Rythu Bazars to stabilise prices.
The Price Support Scheme under PM-AASHA was introduced in
September 2018
The Centre sold onions at
Rs 35 per kilogram
through NAFED and NCCF when retail prices reached Rs 62 per kilogram.

secs.t: Cold storage, warehousing (APSWC) and post-harvest infrastructure

x: AIF funds farm-gate infrastructure at Rythu Bharosa Kendras and supports the conversion of PACS into multipurpose facility centres.
AMI sanctioned 49,796 warehouses with a total capacity of 982.94 lakh metric tonnes.
The main gap is limited operational storage, along with the need for additional cold-storage facilities.

secs.t: FPOs in AP and collective marketing

x: The central scheme for formation of 10,000 FPOs has a budget allocation of
Rs 6,860 crore
The SES 2025-26 figure records 39 FPOs integrated with e-NAM in Andhra Pradesh.
In May 2026, the AP Food Processing Society signed an MoU with
Ace Agri Business
to strengthen FPOs.
The MoU covered
cocoa, coffee, coconut, dry chilli, turmeric and pepper

secs.t: Universal angles

x: e-NAM contributes to price discovery.
The Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Minister sought central help for procurement, storage and cold-chain facilities.

sub: Group-II M2-A-97: Growth and structure of industries in Andhra Pradesh - profile and major sectors
Group-II M2-A-98: Recent Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy - objectives, targets and incentives
Group-II M2-A-99: Single Window Mechanism in Andhra Pradesh - Single Desk Policy and Act
Group-II M2-A-100: Industrial incentives in Andhra Pradesh - capital, power, interest and employment subsidies
Group-II M2-A-101: MSMEs in Andhra Pradesh - profile, clusters, problems and support schemes

secs.t: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

x: Exam angle: "which is NOT a standard incentive"; the policy period (
Exam angle: period of the 4.0 policies (
, APPSC 2025). In the G1 2024 question on IDP 2023-27, the statements "minimum
industry contribution to GSDP" and "end-to-end facilitation in
2 weeks
" were keyed as incorrect.
Exam angle: "maximum capital subsidy of 15% of
Foreign
capital investment" is NOT a standard incentive. FCI stands for
Fixed
Capital Investment.
Industrial Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29
is the current flagship policy for Sub-Large, Large, Mega and Ultra Mega units.
The Single Desk Policy and MSME Policy belong to 2015-20; the IDP editions cover 2020-23, 2023-27 and 2024-29 respectively.
The standard investment subsidy for Sub-Large projects is 12% of Fixed Capital Investment, with an additional 5% for women, SC, ST, BC and specially-abled investors.
Standard incentives include revival support for sick units, 100% stamp and transfer duty reimbursement, 100% land-conversion fee reimbursement and decarbonisation subsidy up to 6% of FCI.
PLI-sector projects obtaining Consent for Establishment within 24 months are eligible for a
40% investment subsidy
The four policy and Government Order pairings are IDP (4.0)—G.O.Ms.68, MSME—G.O.69, Electronics Manufacturing—G.O.70 and Food Processing—G.O.71.
The suite included Private Industrial Parks, described as Plug and Play, and Sustainable Electric Mobility, associated with CDI/APP.

secs.t: MSME policy - definitions, Udyam, MSME & Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0, AP MSMEDC

x: The policy baseline recorded about
9 lakh
registered MSMEs in Andhra Pradesh in February 2024.
All four statements are correct: services predominate, Andhra Pradesh has 28 exclusive MSME parks, MSMEs contribute 23.5% of GSDP, and the national Udyam portal has over seven crore enterprises.
The AP MSMEDC CEO placed the count at over
20 lakh
MSMEs, a broader estimate than the 9 lakh registered-MSME baseline.
The ₹500 crore corpus supports credit guarantee through CGTMSE, technology transfer, revival of sick units and research and development.
The policy provides 100% stamp duty reimbursement, formalisation support for micro units and Industry 4.0 promotion; it does not abolish all compliance requirements.
The 2026 revamp focuses on women-led MSMEs through credit support, capital subsidy and lighter compliance.
AP MSMEDC at Mangalagiri runs the World Bank-supported
RAMP
programme.

secs.t: Major investment announcements - company, product, location

x: ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel
is associated with the proposed 8.2 MTPA steel plant at Rajayyapeta/Nakkapalli in Anakapalli, involving investment of over ₹1.35 lakh crore.
The proposed Adani Group project in Srikakulam involves
beach-sand titanium extraction and value-added products
, with an indicated investment of ₹16,000 crore.
The 8.2 MTPA ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel plant is proposed at
Rajayyapeta near Anakapalli
, with the foundation stone laid on 23 March 2026.

secs.t: Industrial promotion bodies - role

x: APEDB undertakes investor outreach with the Industries Department and opened APEX Korea at Busan, the State’s first overseas investment facilitation centre.

The State Investment Promotion Board, chaired by the Chief Minister, takes final decisions on mega projects, while the State Investment Promotion Committee, chaired by the Chief Secretary, screens proposals.

secs.t: Single Desk Portal and the Single Window Clearance Act - timelines, deemed approval

x: The portal provides online application, payment, tracking and certificates, and is designed to avoid physical visits to regulators.

Applications since inception were 1,20,634; approved applications as of 1 January 2025 were 1,17,954; applications received during the specified period were 16,783; and 16,458 were approved within SLA.
The reported proportion of approvals within the SLA was
, representing 16,458 of 16,783 applications.
The portal includes self-certification, in-principle approval followed by post-inspection and deemed approval on SLA breach.
The Single Desk Portal recorded 99.20% of approvals within the SLA during 2024–25.
SDP 2.0 adds business-specific services, improved service categories, stepwise application timelines with approval hierarchy, and a centralised dashboard.
Tourism investors can access
13 pre-establishment and 11 pre-operation clearances
through the same portal.
All three statements are correct: the portal began in April 2015, cleared 99.20% of 2024-25 applications within the SLA, and is associated with the 'Speed of Doing Business' approach.

secs.t: Sectoral policies - focus

x: These electronics policies focus on electronic system design and manufacturing and EMCs at Kopparthy, Tirupati and Sri City.
The
Textile, Apparel and Garments Policy (4.0) 2024-29
targets more than two lakh jobs.
Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City at Parawada is a bulk-drug and API hub, with units of Hetero and Laurus.

secs.t: Investment summits - Partnership Summits, GIS Visakhapatnam - MoUs

x: The theme of the summit was “
Transforming AP into a Trillion-Dollar Economy
The summit led to 610 MoUs worth ₹13.25 lakh crore, with employment potential exceeding 16 lakh jobs.
The SES tally recorded 193 Industries Department proposals valued at ₹2,80,384 crore.
The Global Investors Summit was held at Visakhapatnam in
March 2023

secs.t: AP's rank in FDI inflows - DPIIT reporting periods

x: Exam angle: rank for a named DPIIT reporting window (calendar year vs Oct-to-date).
The strategic FDI push covers
AI infrastructure, critical minerals, semiconductors, energy transition and advanced technologies
IDP 4.0 sets a target of attracting at least
USD 10 billion
of FDI during 2024-29.
The US$178.09 billion figure is not a reliable State-level amount and should not be treated as the dependable fact.

secs.t: AP's rank in industrial output (Handbook of Statistics on Indian States)

x: AP ranked
7th
in industrial output (RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States
; APPSC 2023).

secs.t: Major industrial units - Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, central PSUs in AP

x: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant is operated by
Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited
(RINL).
The Visakhapatnam Steel Plant is a shore-based integrated steel plant built with Soviet or USSR technical collaboration and dedicated to the nation on 1 August 1992.
HPCL Visakh Refinery, Hindustan Shipyard Limited and NTPC Simhadri are central PSUs in Visakhapatnam.

secs.t: Mineral-based industries - cement, beach sand minerals, barytes

x: The principal concentration of cement industries is in
YSR Kadapa, Kurnool and Guntur
districts.
Limestone, barytes, beach sands and granite are identified as important components of Andhra Pradesh's mineral base.
NGRI found traces of lithium and gallium at
Tummalapalle in Kadapa
district.
The Mines Department signed MoUs with
NGRI and IIT Dhanbad

secs.t: Large and mega projects - number, investment, employment

x: The operational large and mega units numbered 1,074, involved ₹3.01 lakh crore investment and generated 5.33 lakh jobs.
SIPB approved eight projects involving ₹2,45,275 crore and 65,541 jobs during FY 2024-25.
APSES 2024–25 reported 1,074 operational large and mega industries, involving ₹3.01 lakh crore and 5.33 lakh jobs.
The SIPB cleared 87 proposals with an investment value of approximately
₹34,000 crore
in June 2026.

secs.t: Industrial GVA of AP - sector shares and growth

x: The revised IIP framework uses 2022-23 as the base, has nine core industries after adding iron ore, and assigns them a 32.88% weight.
The earlier core index covered eight industries with a 40.27% weight; the revised index has nine industries and a 32.88% weight.
The statement that Andhra Pradesh MSMEs contribute 33.5% of GSDP was keyed as incorrect; no alternative AP percentage is established here.

secs.t: Major industrial sectors - district map

x: Visakhapatnam is associated with engineering, life sciences, electronics, automobiles and metallurgy.
Kadapa and Anantapur are associated with textiles; Anantapur additionally has electronics.
The five endowments are the 974-km coastline, six operational ports, minerals, an agricultural base and power surplus.
Andhra Pradesh has a coastline of about
974 km
, described as the third-longest in the country.

secs.t: AP Economic Development Board - Act, functions, leadership

x: The Board undertakes investor outreach along with the Industries Department, including delegations to countries such as the USA.

secs.t: Policy objectives and targets (IDP 4.0)

x: The policy identifies ₹30 lakh crore as the investment attracted target and ₹5 lakh crore as the realised target, which is approximately 15 per cent of the former.
Exports are targeted to rise from USD 20 billion to USD 40 billion at 15 per cent annual growth.
The stated vision combines global competitiveness with
sustainability, digital innovation and resilience

secs.t: Thrust areas - number and list

x: Green energy
is included in the Propelling group, not the Sustenance group.
Sustenance represents the existing ecosystem, whereas Propelling represents emerging sectors intended to drive the next phase of industrial development.

secs.t: Enterprise classification - micro to ultra-mega

x: The stated limits of ₹50 crore investment and ₹250 crore turnover correspond to a
medium
enterprise.
Projects in PLI sectors with CFE within 24 months are eligible for a
40 per cent
early-bird benefit.
The stated tourism incentive is a 5–10 per cent FCI subsidy capped at ₹40 crore, together with 100 per cent stamp duty benefit.
The 2020 notification prescribed an investment limit of ₹50 crore and a turnover limit of ₹250 crore for a medium enterprise.

secs.t: Local employment law - reservation share

x: The Employment Creation Subsidy is up to 10 per cent of FCI for units having more than five employees and 8–9 per cent for units having five or fewer employees, payable over five years.

secs.t: Purpose of the Single Desk system - clearances handled

x: The Single Desk system provides one application point for every clearance required by an investment proposal.
The system provides online application, document upload, payment, status tracking and certificate download.
The listed activities are integrated online Government-to-Business services under the Single Desk system.

secs.t: One-stop resource and support centre - name and services

x: The Investment Facilitation Cell provides investor handholding, tracks approvals and helps resolve delays.
Country-specific desks
are provided to support foreign investors.
The Tourism Policy 2024–29 established its own Investor Facilitation Cell at
Vijayawada

secs.t: BRAP reforms - online inspections, self-certification

x: Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil Nadu are cited for digitised, single-window clearances.
BRAP 2024 covered digital registration, labour compliance and construction permits.
Preparation for
BRAP 2026
had begun.

secs.t: Investor facilitation - APEDB, DICs, grievance tracking

x: APEDB
and the Industries Department conduct investor outreach under the stated CDI arrangement.
APIIC
coordinates Single Desk clearances in Andhra Pradesh.
Large projects are tracked on the
Investment Tracker

secs.t: Tax incentives - SGST reimbursement, stamp and transfer duty

x: IDP 4.0 provides 100% reimbursement of net SGST for five years from commercial production on final products made, sold and registered in Andhra Pradesh.
The reimbursement covers the listed transactions and is paid only once for a given plot.
For medium, large and mega units, SGST reimbursement was tied to
employment creation
for five years.

secs.t: Land incentives - APIIC plots for SC/ST, concessional allotment, conversion charges

x: IDP 2020-23 reserved
of plots in APIIC parks for SC entrepreneurs.
IDP 4.0 provides
reimbursement of the land-conversion fee.
APIIC parks provide a 25% rebate on land cost, subject to a ceiling of ₹20 lakh per enterprise.

secs.t: Power incentives - power cost reimbursement, electricity duty

x: Fixed power cost is reimbursed at ₹1 per unit for two years from the date of commencement of production (DCP).

secs.t: Interest subsidy - pavala vaddi, MSME interest subvention

x: Under pavala vaddi, the State reimburses interest above 3% a year, so the unit effectively pays a quarter rupee, or 25 paise, per ₹100 per month.
APSEZ units receive a 3% subsidy on term loans, while MSME Policy 4.0 offers collateral-free loans and interest subventions.

secs.t: Incentive arrears - pending dues and clearing

x: IDP 4.0 introduced an
Escrow Guarantee mechanism
for timely payment of promised subsidies.

secs.t: MSME credit tie-ups - MoUs with financial institutions

x: APIIC signed the July 2022 MoU with
Union Bank of India
for loans to MSMEs in 39 industrial parks.
The stated cooperative credit chain consists of
2,042 PACS, 13 DCCBs and APCOB
, and it also reaches rural MSMEs.

secs.t: MSME clusters and CDP projects

x: Etikoppaka lacquer toys are associated with Anakapalli, Kondapalli toys with NTR, and Mangalagiri handloom with Guntur.
APIIC is the State Implementing Agency for MSE-CDP in Andhra Pradesh, while District Industries Centres run the single-window system.
APIIC manages 571 industrial parks, while 45 MSME clusters are covered under the AP Cluster Development Programme with ₹200 crore.

secs.t: Institutions - APMSMEDC, NSIC, MSME-DFO, RAMP

x: APMSMEDC, whose office is at Mangalagiri, implements the

secs.t: SEZs in AP

x: The listed incentives are 100% stamp duty exemption, VAT/CST reimbursement on export inputs, a 15% capital subsidy for micro and small units and a 3% interest subsidy.
Sri City is a multi-product SEZ.

secs.t: PM Gati Shakti and multimodal logistics parks

x: The stated focus includes the Visakhapatnam–Kakinada port corridor and port-led growth, while PM Gati Shakti-related planning includes multimodal logistics parks and freight corridors.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The
SCoR zone, greenfield ports and Bhogapuram airport
are identified as feeding the VCIC logistics chain.
DMIC is associated with the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor and Japanese aid, whereas VCIC is ADB-funded and port-led.
The shrimp boom has contributed to salinisation of coastal soils, while effluents from Pharma City have polluted local water.

rows.title: Special Category Status - criteria, the 14th Finance Commission position and the controversy

secs.t: SCS origin - year, recommending body, first states granted

x: Exam angle: "SCS was first introduced in 1969 on the recommendation of which FC?" - 5th.
The National Development Council endorsed the Gadgil Formula during
The first three States granted Special Category Status were
Jammu & Kashmir, Assam and Nagaland
Special Category Status is not a constitutional category; it emerged as an executive and Planning Commission-era classification linked to preferential Plan assistance.

secs.t: Rajya Sabha assurance on SCS for AP - date, who gave it, duration

x: The assurance was given in the Rajya Sabha on
20 February 2014
Prime Minister
Manmohan Singh
gave the assurance in the Rajya Sabha during the 2014 debates.
The assurance concerned Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh for
five years
The assurance was not incorporated into the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, enabling the Centre later to treat it as non-binding.

secs.t: SCS states - granted, never granted, pending demands

x: Uttarakhand
was among the 11 States granted Special Category Status.
Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory in 2019.
The Centre feared that granting SCS to Andhra Pradesh would trigger identical demands from
Bihar and Odisha

secs.t: SCS criteria - Gadgil-Mukherjee formula parameters, eligibility features

x: Special Category Status was first granted in 1969 on the recommendation of the
5th Finance Commission
The
Gadgil formula
favoured States with Special Category Status in the allocation of assistance.
High population density and advanced infrastructure
were not criteria for Special Category Status.
The Gadgil Formula was later modified and became the
Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula

secs.t: Benefits of SCS - central funding ratio, tax concessions, unspent funds

x: Special Category States received Central loans at
concessional interest
rates, unlike the normal terms applicable to general States.
Industrial units in Special Category States could receive tax breaks and incentives, including income-tax or excise-related concessions.
PMGSY covered habitations of 250 or more in Special Category States, while the corresponding threshold in plains was 500 or more.

secs.t: 14th Finance Commission position on SCS - what changed in devolution

x: The increase from 32 per cent to 42 per cent was described as
the largest increase ever
in the States’ share of the divisible pool.

The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended 42 per cent, while the Fifteenth and Sixteenth Finance Commissions retained 41 per cent; the Sixteenth also added a 10 per cent Contribution to GDP criterion.

secs.t: AP SCS controversy - political events, protests, Parliament motions

x: The correct sequence is 2014 assurance, 2015 Fourteenth Finance Commission award, September 2016 Special Assistance Package, and 2018 withdrawal of TDP from the NDA.
In 2018, the
TDP broke from the NDA and moved a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha
in July; the motion was defeated.
The demand was revived in 2026 through interventions by Congress MP Manickam Tagore in the Lok Sabha, YSRCP leader Botcha Satyanarayana and APCC chief Y.S. Sharmila.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements are correct: the 16th Finance Commission retains a 41 per cent share for the States, ends revenue deficit grants, and covers 2026–2031.
Special Category Status is associated with an automatic 90:10 funding pattern, while a special package consists of project-linked financial assistance.
Special Category Status is regarded as an executive rather than a constitutional category, while its demand has also been linked to a political promise made in Parliament.

rows.title: Special Assistance Package vs Special Category Status - Government's stand and measures taken

secs.t: Special assistance to AP - amounts released year-wise

x: The revenue deficit grant for 2014-15 was
₹3,979 crore
and formed part of the Special Assistance Measure.
The Special Assistance Measure was announced for ₹24,350 crore, including ₹3,979 crore as revenue deficit grant, with the balance meant for infrastructure.
Initial allocations were made to the seven backward districts, but the releases stalled; they were not completed without delay.

secs.t: Special Assistance Package announcement - date and components

x: The promised ten-year tax holiday was delayed, diluted or subsumed in the GST framework; it was not implemented fully and without dilution.
The promised 10-year corporate tax holiday was delayed, diluted or subsumed under GST, while Special Category Status, including its 90% central share of CSS and tax exemptions, was denied.

secs.t: Externally Aided Projects route - how repayment support works

x: The State borrows from agencies such as the World Bank and ADB, and the Centre supports repayment of loan and interest up to the SCS-equivalent amount.
Andhra Pradesh has argued that long approval processes and extensive compliance requirements create red tape and delay project implementation.
The fuller package design described support equivalent to the 90% central grant share under SCS, routed through repayment of externally aided project loans.

secs.t: SCS vs Special Assistance Package - benefit by benefit

x: SCS included
tax concessions for industry
, whereas the package offered only the weaker Section 94(1) incentives.
SCS had recognised and automatic features, while the package was executive in nature and tied to approved externally aided projects.
Andhra Pradesh argued that the apparent monetary equivalence did not compensate for the absence of automatic flows and tax benefits and the reliance on project-linked loans.

secs.t: Centre's stand - reasons for a package over SCS

x: The Centre relied on the 14th Finance Commission's removal of the distinction and increase of devolution to 42% as having absorbed SCS-related benefits.
The Centre referred to constitutional and technical constraints and feared that granting SCS to Andhra Pradesh would lead to similar demands from Bihar and Odisha.

secs.t: AP Government's stand - response and demands over time

x: The relevant sequence is the 2014-18 alliance period, the September 2016 package announcement, the 2018 NDA exit and the 2019 campaign emphasis on SCS.
In 2018, TDP left the NDA over SCS; YSRCP called the package a betrayal and subsequently used SCS as a major 2019 campaign issue.
During 2024-26, Andhra Pradesh sought project money for
Amaravati, Polavaram and SASCI
while again being an NDA ally.

secs.t: Measures taken - SPV route, releases, NITI Aayog and Finance Ministry roles

x: SASCI assistance is outside the Sixteenth Finance Commission's 3 per cent of GSDP deficit ceiling.
Line ministries run sub-schemes under SASCI.
The proposed contribution for the Rayalaseema Global Horticulture Hub is ₹10,000 crore from the Centre and ₹30,000 crore from the State.
For 2026–27, 86 CSS schemes were allocated ₹25,304 crore.
Only
47 per cent
of the funds allocated under the CSS framework had been used by 7 September 2026.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The package has been criticised as a loans-and-projects arrangement instead of a status-based framework.
SASCI and project grants have become the main forms of special help, including the specified grants for Amaravati and Polavaram.
The debate between Special Category Status and the package became an important part of
the 2019 election narrative
in Andhra Pradesh.
